# Varahi Samhita (Bṛhat Saṃhitā)

<page-num>(26)</page-num>
<header>Varahi Samhita—</header>

Just as gold becomes pure after being heated in fire, so does the soul through trials. || 36 || **A mock sun <note>original: "pratisūryo" - a parhelion or optical phenomenon</note> appearing to the north of the Sun brings rain; if situated to the south, it brings wind. If appearing on both sides, there is a fear of floods. If it appears above the Sun, it destroys the king; if below, it brings destruction to the common people.** || 37 || If the Sun appears blood-red in the sky, there will soon be a terrible war between kings. If its body is made crimson by harsh dust, the same result follows. || 38 || If the Sun appears black, variegated, blue, or harsh, it causes the slaughter of people, especially if accompanied by the terrifying and harsh cries of birds and beasts at the beginning of the night. || 39 || When the Sun possesses a spotless body, a perfectly circular orb, and clear, vast, pure, and long rays—bearing its natural form, color, and marks—it brings auspiciousness and well-being to the world. || 40 ||

->Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Course of the Sun," in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā composed by Sri Varahamihira. || 3 ||<-

***

Certainly, at one time the summer solstice <note>original: "dakṣiṇāyana"</note> began from the middle of the constellation Ashlesha and the winter solstice <note>original: "uttarāyaṇa"</note> from the beginning of Dhanishtha; otherwise, why would it be described so in the ancient scriptures? However, the solar solstice currently in practice begins from the start of Cancer <note>Karkata</note> and the start of Capricorn <note>Makara</note>. The absence of this alignment is called a "deviation" <note>vikṛti</note>. Whatever is proven correct by direct observation shall be published here. || 1-2 || At the time of sunrise or sunset, the solstice is tested by piercing the marks of the distance of the great circle, or by the marks of the shadow entering and exiting the great circle. || 3 ||

If the Sun returns without reaching the sign of Capricorn, it destroys the South-West direction. If it returns without reaching the sign of Cancer, it destroys the North-East direction. If it returns after crossing the winter solstice point, it is auspicious and there is an increase in grain; this is called the Sun in its natural state. Fear arises when the Sun's motion is deviated. || 4-5 || If the Sun's orb is eclipsed by Rahu <note>the lunar node responsible for eclipses</note> outside of the predicted time, seven kings will die, and people will be destroyed by weapons, fire, or famine. || 6 ||

There are thirty-three types of Ketus <note>comets or celestial portents</note>, sons of Rahu, named Tamasa, Kilaka, and others. One should judge the results by observing their color, position, and shape within the solar orb. || 7 || If they appear in the solar orb, it is inauspicious; however, if they appear in the lunar orb, they give auspicious results. But if they appear in the lunar orb in the form of a crow, a headless torso <note>kabandha</note>, or a weapon, they are inauspicious. || 8 ||

Upon the rising of these Ketus, there is upheaval everywhere: water becomes turbid, dust covers the sky, and fierce winds blow, crushing the peaks of mountains and trees. Trees bloom out of season. Deer, birds, and other animals run or cry toward the "blazing" <note>Footnote 1 refers to this term</note> directions. Great calamities like forest fires, thunderbolts, and earthquakes occur. || 9-10 || Among these sons of Rahu, if Rahu is seen in the form of an arrow or a spike, the results should be stated as before. In this way, one should determine the cause of their rising and the effects of Ketu and others. || 11 || In whichever countries the Ketus are seen within the Sun's disc, the kings of those countries will face misfortune. || 12 || Upon their rising, even sages—their bodies exhausted by hunger and having abandoned their own dharma and noble character—will take their thin, fleshless children in their arms and go to other countries with great difficulty. || 13 || Thieves will steal the wealth of the virtuous; for this reason, they will sigh deeply, shedding tears from their eyes, their bodies agitated and their voices choked with grief...

***

<note>1. The description of "blazing" <note>dipta</note> and other directions will be explained in the chapter on Omens <note>Shakunadhyaya</note>.</note>

<term>Bṛhat Saṃhitā</term>: A 6th-century Sanskrit encyclopedic work by Varahamihira covering astrology, planetary movements, eclipses, and architecture.
<term>Uttarāyaṇa/Dakṣiṇāyana</term>: The northern and southern progress of the sun, marking the winter and summer solstices.
<term>Rāhu/Ketu</term>: In Indian astronomy, the ascending and descending nodes of the moon; also personified as celestial bodies causing eclipses and portents.

# Chapter 3 with Hindi Commentary

...will remain distressed. ||14|| In that time, men will become extremely weakened by their own king or by other <term>political circles<note>original: "rajachakra" - refers to the sphere of influence or alliances of a king</note> and will become slanderous; some will even criticize the character or the past deeds of their own local king. ||15|| Clouds will remain pregnant with moisture but will not give much water; rivers will have little water, and grain will only grow in a few places. ||16||

If a staff-shaped <term>comet<note>original: "ketu" - here referring to a specific malefic celestial appearance</note> is seen in the solar disc, the king dies. If a headless trunk appears, there is fear of disease. If a crow-like shape appears, there is fear of thieves, and if the shape of a pillar is seen, a famine occurs. ||17|| If the king's regalia—such as the ceremonial umbrella, flag, or fly-whisk—appear to pierce the solar disc, there is a change in the government. If the sun is covered by sparks or smoke, it signifies the death of all men. ||18||

If the sun is pierced by one of the aforementioned signs like the umbrella, there is a famine; if pierced by two or more, the king is destroyed. If pierced by these signs in the colors white, red, yellow, or black, then the <term>Brahmins<note>priestly class</note>, Kshatriyas<note>warrior/ruling class</note>, Vaishyas<note>merchants/farmers</note>, and Shudras<note>laboring class</note></term> are destroyed respectively. ||19|| Wherever these great <term>portents<note>original: "utpata" - unnatural or calamitous phenomena</note> arise and are seen in the solar disc, all people living in that country will experience fear. ||20||

If the rays on the upper part of the sun are copper-colored, the army commander is destroyed; if yellow, the prince; and if white, the royal priest is destroyed. ||21|| If the sun's circle of rays is colored with many hues or is smoke-colored, and if rain does not fall quickly, the entire earth will be distressed by thieves or the falling of weapons <insert>war</insert>. ||22||

The solar disc is auspicious if it is:
* Copper or tawny in the <term>winter season<note>Shishir - late winter</note></term>
* Green like saffron in the <term>spring season<note>Vasant</note></term>
* Somewhat pale <note>a mix of white and yellow</note> and like gold in the <term>summer season<note>Grishma</note></term>
* White in the <term>rainy season<note>Varsha</note></term>
* Like the beauty of the heart of a lotus in the <term>autumn season<note>Sharad</note></term>
* Red in the <term>early winter season<note>Hemant</note></term>
However, it is inauspicious if it appears oily/glossy during the rainy season. ||23-24||

If the sun is dry or white, the Brahmins are destroyed; if it has a bloody glow, the Kshatriyas; if yellow, the Vaishyas; and if black, the Shudras. If there is a brightness in all these colors of the sun, it is auspicious. ||25|| In summer, if the solar disc is red, there is fear for living beings; in the rainy season, if it is black, there is a drought; and in early winter, if it is yellow, there is an immediate fear of disease. ||26||

If the solar disc appears broken in body because a rainbow has appeared in front of it during the rainy season, there is conflict among kings. If it appears with clear rays, there will be rain soon. ||27|| If during the rainy season the solar disc appears with a glow like the <term>Shirisha flower<note>a pale greenish-yellow flower</note></term>, rain will come quickly; but if it appears glowing like a peacock's tail, there will be a drought for twelve years. ||28||

If the solar disc is dark-colored, there is fear of insects (in the country); if it is ash-colored, there is fear from foreign kingdoms. If a hole is seen in the sun while it is positioned in a king's birth star, that king is destroyed. ||29|| If the color of the sun is red like a rabbit's blood, war occurs; and if it appears with a color like the moon, the king of that country is soon destroyed and another king takes his place. ||30||

If the solar disc appears in the shape of a pot, living beings will lose their lives to the flames of hunger; if it is broken in shape, the king is destroyed; if it is devoid of rays, there is fear; if it takes the form of a gateway, the city is destroyed; and if it is shaped like an umbrella, the country is destroyed. ||31||

# Chapter 4
<note>This chapter transitions from the Sun to the Moon, explaining lunar phases and the effects of the Moon's path through the constellations.</note>

The Moon, which always stays below the Sun, has one half (the side facing the Sun) white, while the other half is dark due to its own shadow, just like a water-pot placed in the sunlight. ||1|| The rays of the Sun, falling upon the watery body of the Moon, dispel the darkness of the night, just as rays reflected from a mirror illuminate the interior of a house. ||2|| As the Moon moves away from the Sun, its whiteness begins to appear on the western side; thus, due to the Sun's position, the Moon's illumination increases from the bottom upward. ||3|| In this way, day by day, due to its specific position relative to the Sun, the Moon's whiteness increases in the afternoon on its western part, much like the light on a water-pot. ||4|| If the Moon passes to the south of the constellations Jyeshtha, Mula, or the two Ashadhas, it destroys seeds, aquatic animals, and forests, and brings fear of fire. ||5|| The Moon passing to the south of Vishakha and Anuradha is considered inauspicious; however, passing through the middle of Magha or Vishakha is considered excellent. ||6|| There are six constellations starting from Revati, twelve starting from Ardra, and nine starting from Jyeshtha which... <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence at the end of the page.</note>

Just as when a water-pot is placed in the sunlight, that half which faces the sun becomes white from the sun's rays, while the other half remains dark due to its own shadow; in the same way, the half of the Moon—which is situated below the Sun—is daily illuminated by the Sun's rays, while the other half remains dark-colored by its own shadow. || 1 || Just as the essence of the Sun's rays falls upon a mirror and, entering a dark house, destroys the darkness within by its reflection; so do the Sun's rays fall upon the watery Moon to destroy the mass of the night's darkness. || 2 || As the Moon leaves the lower part of the Sun, its western portion assumes whiteness due to the power of the Sun's rays; it becomes increasingly illuminated from the bottom upwards. || 3 || In this manner, every day, due to its specific position during the third watch of the day <note>afternoon</note>, the whiteness of the Moon is increased by the Sun, similar to the light on a water-pot. || 4 ||

When the Moon passes to the right side of the <term>Nakshatras</term> <note>Lunar mansions or star clusters</note> of Jyeshtha, Mula, Purvashadha, and Uttarashadha, there is a loss of seeds, water, and forests, and the danger of fire arises. || 5 || When the Moon moves to the right of Vishakha and Anuradha, it is called a "Sinful Moon"; however, if the Moon stays in the middle of Vishakha, Anuradha, and Magha, the results are auspicious. || 6 || Six Nakshatras from Revati to Mrigashira meet the Moon before they have fully arrived <note>anagata</note>; twelve from Ardra to Anuradha meet the Moon in the middle; and nine stars from Jyeshtha to Uttarabhadrapada meet the Moon after they have passed <note>atikranta</note>. || 7 ||

If the <term>Shringa</term> <note>the "horn" or cusp of the crescent moon</note> is slightly raised and attains a width like a boat, it brings distress to sailors but is auspicious for all other people. || 8 || When the cusp of the half-risen Moon is shaped like a <term>Langala</term> <note>a plow</note>, it brings distress to those who live by the plow <note>farmers</note>, but kings remain joyful without cause and there is an abundance of food. || 9 || If the southern cusp of the Moon is raised halfway, it is called the "Evil Plow" cusp; the result of this Moon is that the army of the King of the Pandya country <note>an ancient kingdom in Southern India</note> will attempt to kill their own king. || 10 || If the Moon rises with both cusps equal, there is an abundance of food, welfare, and rain as in former days. If the Moon rises looking like a staff, cattle and oxen suffer, and kings become harsh punishers. || 11 || If the Moon rises in the shape of a bow, war occurs; however, victory belongs to the country toward which the bowstring of this lunar bow is facing. # Chapter 4: With Hindi Commentary
### (Page 31)

If the **horn** <note>original: *shringa*; the tips of the lunar crescent</note> is spread towards the south and north, it is called a *Sthana* or *Yuga* formation; this causes earthquakes. ||12|| If this same *Yuga* horn is slightly higher on the southern side, it is called the **Side-Reclining** <note>original: *parshvashayi*</note> horn; it brings destruction to merchants—those who engage in forest trade—and results in a lack of rain. ||13|| Due to a tilt, if any horn of the Moon is downward-facing, it is called the **Bent** <note>original: *avajjita*</note> horn; this leads to famine for cattle and livestock, meaning grass and fodder will not grow. ||14|| If an unbroken circular line is seen all around the Moon, it is the **Bowl** <note>original: *kunda*</note> horn formation; because of this, the kings of the twelve regions lose their positions. ||15||

In the absence of the previously mentioned positions, if the northern horn of the Moon is slightly higher, there is an increase in grain and the rains are good. If the southern horn is slightly higher, famine occurs. ||16|| Seeing a Moon with only one horn, a downward-facing mouth, no horns at all, or a completely new and strange appearance signifies the death of one among those who behold it. ||17|| The constitution of the Moon's body has been described; from this, the Moon takes many forms. If the Moon appears small, there is famine; if it appears large, there is **abundance** <note>original: *subhiksha*; a time of plenty</note>. ||18||

When the Moon rises in a medium size (neither too large nor too small), it is called the **Thunderbolt** <note>original: *vajra*</note>; this causes great hunger among living beings and creates turmoil among kings. When the Moon rises in the shape of a **Mridanga** <note>original: *mridanga*; a barrel-shaped drum</note>, it brings auspiciousness and abundance. ||19|| If the form of the Moon is extremely vast, prosperity increases in the palaces of kings; if it is thick, there is abundance; if it is beautiful, there is excellent grain. ||20||

If the **Mars** planet strikes the horn of the Moon (the Lord of Stars), the wicked kings of the **Foreign Lands** <note>original: *mlechchha-desha*; often referring to non-Vedic or border regions</note> are destroyed. If the Moon's horn is struck by **Saturn**, there is fear of weapons and fear of hunger. If the Moon's horn is pierced by **Mercury**, there is drought and famine. If it is by **Jupiter**, great kings are destroyed, and if by **Venus**, ordinary kings are destroyed. However, if the Moon's horn is pierced by a planet during the waxing phase (bright fortnight), the result is only slight; the results for the waning phase (dark fortnight) are stated below. ||21||

If the Moon's horn is afflicted by **Venus** during the waning phase, then in the lands of Magadha, Yavana <note>Greeks or Westerners</note>, Pulinda, Nepal, Bhringi, Maru, Kutch, Surat, Madras, Punjab, Kashmir, Kuluta, Purushada, and Ushinara, a plague persists for seven months. ||22||

If the Moon's horn is pierced by **Jupiter**, then the people of Gandhara (Kandahar), Sauvarika, Indus, Keera, Dravida <note>Southern India</note>, the Brahmins of the mountain regions, and all the grains of those lands are distressed for ten months. ||23||

If the body of the Moon is pierced by **Mars**, it destroys the industrious kings along with their vehicles in Trigarta, Malwa, Kaulinda, Ganapati, Shibi, and the land of Ayodhya, and afflicts the noble warriors of Kuru, Matsya, and Shuktidesha for six months. ||24||

If the lunar orb is pierced by **Saturn**, it destroys the kings of the lineage of Arjuna and the Kuru lineage living in the eastern lands, along with their ministers and warriors, after afflicting them for ten months. ||25||

If the planet **Mercury** emerges after piercing the Moon, it afflicts Magadha, Mathura, and the lands settled on the banks of the Vena River, while in the western lands, an age of truth <note>original: *sat-yuga*; a golden age</note> begins. ||26||

If the Moon is afflicted by **Ketu** <note>the descending lunar node/comets</note>, there is inauspiciousness, disease, famine, and the destruction of those who live by the sword, and thieves suffer extreme pain. ||27||

If a meteor falls upon the Moon when it is eclipsed by Rahu or Ketu <note>The ascending and descending nodes of the Moon, personified as the shadow-planets that cause eclipses</note>, the king in whose birth star the Moon is situated will meet his death. || 28 || If the body of the Moon appears dry like ashes, reddish-brown, devoid of rays, blackish, fractured, or trembling, then there is fear of hunger, war, disease, or thieves. || 29 || That Moon alone brings auspiciousness to the world which—as if carefully polished by Parvati, the daughter of the Himalayas, with the thought that it will be exceedingly pleasing to us at night—shines as white as a frost particle, a Kunda flower, a white water-lily, or a crystal. || 30 || That cool-rayed Moon which, being as white as a water-lily, a lotus stalk, or a pearl necklace, waxes and wanes according to the rules of the lunar date, whose orb is free from defects, and which possesses proper motion and radiance, brings victory to all men. || 31 || In the bright fortnight <note>Shukla Paksha</note>, if a lunar date increases so that the fortnight is extended and the Moon attains excessive growth, then the Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and the subjects prosper greatly; if the Moon is diminished in such a state, there is loss for all; if it is medium, all attain equality. However, if this occurs in the dark fortnight <note>Krishna Paksha</note>, the results are the opposite. || 32 ||

### Chapter Five

Some say that because of the special taste of the nectar <note>Amrita, the elixir of immortality</note>, this head of the Demon <note>Rahu</note>, though severed, did not lose its life and attained the status of a planet. || 1 || Because of its blackness, it is said to have the shape of the orb of the Moon or Sun but is not seen in the sky except at the time of the nodes <note>eclipses</note>, due to a boon granted by the Lotus-born <note>Brahma, the Creator</note>. || 2 || Others teach that it has the form of a serpent with a distinct head and tail. Others say the one named 'Son of Sinhika' <note>Rahu</note> is formless and composed of darkness. || 3 || If Rahu were a celestial traveler with a physical body, or a head, or a circular orb, and moved with a fixed motion, how could he eclipse planets separated by half a zodiac? || 4 || If his motion were indeed unfixed, how could his position be determined by calculation? And if he is defined as having a head and a tail, why does he not eclipse the space between them? || 5 || Furthermore, if he has the form of a King of Serpents and seizes with either his tail or his mouth, why does he not obstruct the half-zodiac situated between the mouth and the tail? || 6 || If there were two Rahus, then when the Moon is eclipsed at sunset or sunrise, the Sun should also be seen eclipsed by the other, but this is not the case. || 7 || In a lunar eclipse, the Moon enters the shadow of the Earth, and in a solar eclipse, the Moon enters the Sun <note>meaning it covers the Sun</note>. Therefore, the commencement of an eclipse begins from the eastern side for the Moon and from the western side for the Sun. || 8 || Just as the shadow of a tree falls long on one side, so at night the Earth's shadow is cast by the obstruction of the Sun. || 9 || When the Moon is in the seventh sign from the Sun and is not too far to the North or South, it then enters the Earth's shadow which faces East. || 10 || The Moon, being situated below, obstructs the Sun like a cloud coming from the West. Therefore, the solar eclipse appears different in every country due to the variation in the line of sight. || 11 || Because the obstructing body of the Moon is large, its horns <note>the cusps of the crescent</note> appear blunt when half-covered; because the Sun's obstruction is small, the Sun appears with sharp horns. || 12 || Thus, the cause of eclipses has been explained by the ancient teachers who possessed divine vision. # Chapter 5: With Hindi Commentary
## Page (33)

The statement that "there is a cause in this" refers to the existence of the sacred scriptures. ॥ 13 ॥ That demon known as Rahu was granted a boon by Brahma: "During an eclipse, a portion of the offerings made to the gods and ancestors shall belong to you." ॥ 14 ॥ At that specific time, his presence is invoked; therefore, Rahu is used as a figurative term. In calculations, the north and south motion of the Moon is also treated figuratively through him. ॥ 15 ॥ Signs and omens are not understood in any other way; however, portents of various forms do occur at other times as well. ॥ 16 ॥ An eclipse does not actually occur simply from the conjunction of five planets. <note>The author is debunking a common myth that five planets meeting causes an eclipse.</note> Wise men should not consider the idea that an eclipse is like oil spreading on water on the eighth lunar day. ॥ 17 ॥

The extent of the eclipse <term>grāsa</term><note>literally "the bite" or portion obscured</note> of the Sun is known through parallax <term>avanati</term>, and the direction is known through the deflection <term>valana</term> and parallax. The time of the end of the lunar day <term>tithi</term> has been explained by me in the manual of calculation <term>karaṇa</term>. ॥ 18 ॥

With an increase of six months each, there are seven presiding deities of the eclipse periods <term>parva</term> to be known in order: Brahma, the Moon, Indra, Kubera, Varuna, Agni, and Yama. ॥ 19 ॥
*   **Brahma:** Increase in Brahmins and cattle, prosperity, health, and abundance of crops.
*   **The Moon (Sowmya):** Similarly beneficial, but if afflicted, causes suffering to scholars and a lack of rain. ॥ 20 ॥
*   **Indra (Aindra):** Conflict between kings, destruction of autumn crops, and lack of safety.
*   **Kubera (Kaubera):** Loss of wealth for the wealthy, yet general abundance of food. ॥ 21 ॥
*   **Varuna (Varuna):** Inauspicious for kings but brings safety and crop growth for others.
*   **Agni (Agneya/Mitra):** Good for crops, health, safety, and water. ॥ 22 ॥
*   **Yama (Yamya):** Causes drought, famine, and the destruction of crops.
Any period beyond these is inauspicious, bringing hunger, death, and drought. ॥ 23 ॥

In an eclipse period lacking strength, there is danger to pregnancies and outbreaks of violence with weapons. If it occurs past the proper time, there is a loss of flowers and fruits, fear, and destruction of crops. ॥ 24 ॥ The results of eclipses occurring at diminished or excessive times are stated based on ancient scriptures; however, for one who knows accurate mathematics <term>sphuṭa-gaṇita</term>, the time never deviates. ॥ 25 ॥

If an eclipse of both the Sun and the Moon occurs in the same month, then kings perish due to the upheaval of their own armies, and there is intense conflict with weapons. ॥ 26 ॥ Eclipses occurring at sunrise or sunset destroy autumn crops and kings. A total eclipse <term>sarva-grāsa</term> accompanied by malefic influences brings famine and plague. ॥ 27 ॥

*   **Eclipse at partial rise:** Destroys those who live on the fringes of society and all sacrificial rites.
*   **First part of the day:** Destroys those who work with fire, virtuous Brahmins, and ascetics. ॥ 28 ॥
*   **Second part:** Destroys artisans, heretics, merchants, and the strength of the warrior class.
*   **Third part:** Destroys laborers, the lower classes, foreigners <term>mleccha</term>, and ministers. ॥ 29 ॥
*   **Midday:** Destroys the King and the central country, but the price of grain remains good.
*   **Fifth part:** Destroys herbivores, ministers, the royal harem, and the merchant class. ॥ 30 ॥
*   **Sixth part:** Destroys women and the lower classes.
*   **At sunset:** Destroys bandits and those living on the borders.
Prosperity comes to those mentioned in the specific division of the sky where the liberation <term>mokṣa</term><note>the end of the eclipse</note> occurs. ॥ 31 ॥

An eclipse during the Sun's northern course <term>uttarāyaṇa</term> harms Brahmins and kings; in the southern course <term>dakṣiṇāyana</term>, it harms the merchant and laboring classes. If Rahu is seen moving clockwise from the north, it harms Brahmins and others in order. ॥ 32 ॥ If situated in an intermediate direction, it harms foreigners, travelers, and those who work with fire. An eclipse in the south harms aquatic creatures and elephants; in the north, it is inauspicious for cows. ॥ 33 ॥ If the Demon <note>Rahu</note> appears in the East, he fills the earth with water; in the West, he is said to bring destruction to farmers, servants, and seeds. ॥ 34 ॥

When the eclipse occurs in **Aries (Mesha)**: The people of Panchala, Kalinga, Shurasena, Kamboja, Odra, Kirata, and those who live by weapons or fire suffer distress. ॥ 35 ॥
When the Sun or Moon is eclipsed in **Taurus (Vrishabha)**: Cowherds, livestock, cattle-owners, and men who have attained great importance suffer distress. ॥ 36 ॥
In **Gemini (Mithuna)**: Noble women, kings, royal officers, powerful people, artists, those living on the banks of the Yamuna, the Bahlika people, and the Matsyas...

# The Samhita of Varahamihira

...accompanied by friends. || 37 || When an eclipse occurs in **Cancer**, it destroys the Abhiras, Shabaras, Pallavas, Mallas, Matsyas, Kurus, Shakas, and Panchalas; it also afflicts the disabled and destroys food supplies. || 38 ||

In **Leo**, it strikes the Pulinda tribes, those endowed with singular courage, king-like figures, monarchs, and forest-dwellers. In the **sixth sign (Virgo)**, it destroys those devoted to crops, poetry, writing, and singing, as well as the regions of Ashmaka, Tripura, and those rich in rice. || 39 ||

In **Libra**, it afflicts the people of Avanti and the western borders, holy men, merchants, the Dasharnas, and the people of Marukaccha. In **Scorpio**, it strikes the Udumbaras, Madras, Cholas, ancient trees, the Yaudheyas, and those who live by poisoned weapons <note>mercenaries or those using poisoned arrows</note>. || 40 ||

In **Sagittarius**, it destroys chief ministers, horses, the Videhas, Mallas, the Panchalas, physicians, merchants, and those using irregular weapons. In **Capricorn**, it strikes the families of fish-eaters and ministers, the low-born, those skilled in mantras and herbs, and elderly warriors. || 41 ||

In **Aquarius**, it destroys the inhabitants of the inner mountains, westerners, carriers of heavy loads, thieves, Abhiras, Dardas, and the people of Singhapura and Barbary. In **Pisces**, it affects products of the ocean shore and sea water, honorable men, the wise, and those who live by water. One should declare the results of the signs based on the "Instruction of the Tortoise" <note>The *Kurma-vibhaga*, a traditional geographical mapping of India onto the body of a tortoise</note>. || 42 ||

### The Ten Types of Eclipses

The ten types of "seizures" (grasas) are: Left-sided, Right-sided, Licking, Swallowing, Obstruction, Crushing, Mounting, Striking, Central Darkness, and Edge Darkness. || 43 ||

When the darkness (Rahu) moves to the **left**, the world is flooded with water, but people are happy and free from fear. In a **right-sided** movement, there is destruction of the subjects through the oppression of kings and thieves. || 44 ||

If the darkness "licks" the solar or lunar orb all around like a tongue, it is called **Licking** (*Leha*). Then all beings are delighted and the earth is abundant with water. || 45 ||

**Swallowing** (*Grasana*) is when a third, a quarter, or a half of the orb is taken. It causes the loss of wealth for prosperous kings and distress to flourishing countries. || 46 ||

If the darkness seizes the edges and then stays as a mass in the center, it is known as **Obstruction** (*Nirodha*). It brings joy to all living beings. || 47 ||

**Crushing** (*Avamardana*) is when the darkness completely covers the orb and remains for a long time. This "dark-natured" eclipse destroys the principal regions and the most important kings. || 48 ||

If, after the orb is released, the darkness immediately covers it again, it is **Mounting** (*Arohana*). It brings fear of mutual conflict among kings. || 49 ||

If a portion appears like a mirror clouded by the breath of a sigh, it is **Striking** (*Aghata*). It brings the world an increase in good rainfall. || 50 ||

If the darkness enters the **center** and the surrounding orb remains bright, it causes the destruction of the central regions and fear of stomach diseases. || 51 ||

When the darkness is very thick at the **edges** and thin in the middle, it is called **Edge Darkness** (*Tamontya*). In this, there is danger to crops from pests and fear of thieves. || 52 ||

### Colors of the Eclipse

If Rahu is **white**, one should predict peace and plenty, but distress for the Brahmins. If it is the **color of fire**, there is fear of fire and distress for those who work with fire. || 53 ||

If **green**, there is a prevalence of disease and destruction of crops by pests. If **brown** (tawny), it brings swift-moving creatures, the destruction of barbarians (*Mlechhas*), and famine. || 54 ||

If it resembles the **rays of the dawn**, there is famine, lack of rain, and distress to birds. If **smoky**, one should predict peace, plenty, and moderate rain. || 55 ||

If it looks like a **pigeon, or is reddish-brown or like a corpse**, fear of hunger should be predicted. The **pigeon-colored** eclipse brings disease to the Shudras, as does the **black** color. || 56 ||

A color like a **pure yellow gem** brings destruction to the Vaishyas but leads to plenty. If it is **flaming**, there is fear of fire; if it looks like **red chalk** (*Gairika*), there will be wars. || 57 ||

If it is **dark like a blade of Durva grass** or **yellow like turmeric**, death should be predicted. Rahu, appearing like a **Patala flower**, brings both safety and fear...

# Chapter 5: The Course of Rahu (Continued)

-> **The Effects of Color and Planetary Aspects** <-

**58-59.** An eclipse that appears **dusty red** <note>original: *pāṃśuvilohita*</note> in color foretells the destruction of the *Kshatriyas* <note>the warrior and ruling class</note> and brings drought. If it resembles the **rising sun, a lotus, or a rainbow**, it leads to conflict involving harsh weapons.

**60.** If **Mercury** <note>original: *Saumya*</note> views the eclipsed body, there will be a scarcity of ghee, honey, and oil, and kings will suffer. If **Mars** <note>original: *Bhauma*</note> views it, there will be the clash of war, outbreaks of fire <note>original: *shikhi-kopam*</note>, and fear of thieves.

**61.** **Venus** <note>original: *Shukra*</note> causes the destruction of crops and various afflictions upon the earth. **Saturn** <note>original: *Ravija*, literally "Son of the Sun"</note> brings a lack of rain, famine, and danger from bandits.

**62.** Whatever evil is predicted by these planetary aspects during the beginning or end of an eclipse, it is all pacified if **Jupiter** <note>original: *Surapati-guru*, the teacher of the gods</note> looks upon it, just as water extinguishes a blazing fire.

**63.** After an eclipse, the effects may be felt for up to six months, intensified by portents such as strong winds, meteors, dust storms, earthquakes, darkness, or thunderbolts.

-> **Regional Effects Based on Planets** <-

**64.** If **Mars** is involved in the eclipse, the people of Avanti, those living on the banks of the Kaveri and Narmada rivers, and arrogant monarchs will suffer.

**65.** If **Mercury** is involved, it destroys those in the Antarvedi <note>the land between the Ganges and Yamuna</note>, the Sarayu region, Nepal, the eastern ocean, and the Sone river; it also harms women, kings, soldiers, boys, and scholars.

**66.** When **Jupiter** <note>original: *Jiva*</note> is eclipsed <note>or occulted</note>, scholars, ministers, elephants, and horses are destroyed, as well as the inhabitants of the Indus valley and those residing in the northern direction.

**67.** When **Venus** <note>original: *Bhrigu-tanaya*</note> is reached by Rahu, the people of Daseraka, Kaikaya, Yaudheya, Aryavarta, and the Shibis suffer, along with women and groups of ministers.

**68.** When **Saturn** <note>original: *Saura*</note> is involved, the inhabitants of Maru <note>the desert</note>, Pushkara, Saurashtra, the Arbuda mountains, and those of the lowest castes, as well as those living in the Gomanta and Pariyatra hills, quickly meet their end.

-> **Effects by Lunar Month** <-

**69.** In the month of **Karttika** <note>Oct-Nov</note>: Those who live by fire, the people of Magadha, eastern kings, Kosala, Kalmasha, Shurasena, and Kashi are distressed. The King of Kalinga, his ministers, and servants are destroyed. However, if the eclipse is seen <note>under favorable conditions</note>, it may bring safety and abundance after the initial distress to the *Kshatriyas*.

**70.** In **Margashirsha** <note>Nov-Dec</note>: It harms the people of Kashmir, Kosala, Pundra, and the Mrigas, as well as those in the western borderlands <note>Aparanta</note>. It destroys those who perform Soma sacrifices, yet it also brings good rain and prosperity.

**71.** In **Pausha** <note>Dec-Jan</note>: There is trouble for Brahmins and Kshatriyas. The people of Sindh, Kukura, and Videha are destroyed. One should expect light rain and fear coupled with famine.

**72.** In **Magha** <note>Jan-Feb</note>: Rahu distresses those devoted to their parents, the Vashistha clan, those dedicated to Vedic study and duty, elephants, horses, and the people of the Ganges and Kashi. However, it brings rain that pleases the farmers.

**73.** In **Phalguna** <note>Feb-March</note>: The eclipse brings trouble to Vanga <note>Bengal</note>, Ashmaka, Avanti, and Mekala. It affects dancers, fine crops, beautiful women, archers, and ascetics.

**74.** In **Chaitra** <note>March-April</note>: Painters, writers, singers, those who live by their beauty, Vedic scholars, and gold merchants suffer. The people of Pundra, Odra, Kaikaya, and Ashmaka are distressed.

**75.** In **Vaishakha** <note>April-May</note>: Cotton, sesame, and the ocean suffer. The Ikshvaku, Yaudheya, Shaka, and Kalinga tribes face calamities, though the land remains fertile.

**76.** In **Jyeshtha** <note>May-June</note>: Great kings, the wives of kings, crops, rain, and large assemblies are destroyed, as well as noble men, the Salvas, and the Nishada tribes.

**77.** In **Ashadha** <note>June-July</note>: Wells, embankments, and river flows are affected, as are those who live on fruits and roots. The people of Gandhara, Kashmir, Pulinda, and China are said to be destroyed, though there is rain in certain regions.

**78.** In **Shravana** <note>July-August</note>: If the eclipse is seen, it harms Kashmir, Pulinda, China, the Yavanas <note>Greeks/foreigners</note>, Kurukshetra, Gandhara, and the Middle Country <note>Madhyadesha</note>, as well as the Kamboja tribes...

(36)
# Varāhī Saṃhitā

...as previously stated, he <note>Rahu, the eclipse-demon</note> covers the earth with abundant food and joyful men. (78) When the Demon <note>Rahu</note> enters the sign of Gemini, he destroys the peoples of Kalinga, Vanga, Magadha, Surashtra, the Mlecchas <note>foreigners or non-Aryans</note>, Suviras, Daradas, and Shakas, and destroys the fetuses of women, yet brings about a time of good alms <note>prosperity/abundance</note>. (79) When the Demon is seen in the sign of Ashvini, he destroys the Kambojas, Chinese, and Yavanas <note>Greeks/Ionians</note> along with those who live by the sword, the inhabitants of Bahlika and the banks of the Indus, the people of Anarta and Paundra, physicians, and the Kiratas, yet he creates great abundance. (80)

Based on the divisions of the jaw, belly, and anus, the learned describe ten types of "releases" <note>the way the eclipse ends</note> for the Moon and Sun: *Vomiting* (Sac-chardana), *Digestion* (Jarana), and *Splitting* of the middle and ends. (81) The exit of the Moon toward the South-East is called the "Splitting of the Right Jaw"; it results in the destruction of crops, diseases of the mouth, suffering for kings, but good rain. (82) An exit toward the North-East is the "Splitting of the Left Jaw," which brings fear to princes, mouth diseases, and fear of weapons, but one should know it also brings abundance. (83)

If the release occurs toward the south side, it is the "Splitting of the Right Belly." It brings suffering to the sons of kings, and enemies from the south will attack. (84) If Rahu is situated on the northern path, it is the "Splitting of the Left Belly"; it causes the loss of pregnancies in women, and the crops there will be of middling quality. (85) Exits toward the South-West and North-West are the two "Splittings of the Anus," right and left respectively. Both cause diseases of the private parts and little rain; the left one specifically causes the downfall of queens. (86)

When the eclipse begins in the East and the shadow retreats toward the East, it is called *Vomiting*; it brings peace, good crops, and joy to the world. (87) When the eclipse begins in the East but the shadow retreats toward the West, it is *Digestion*; people, agitated by hunger and fear of weapons, will wonder where to seek refuge. (88) If light first appears in the center, it is named "Splitting of the Middle." It causes internal strife but brings abundance and moderate rain. (89) When there is clarity at the edges but thick darkness remains in the center, it is called "Splitting of the Ends"; it brings destruction to the central regions and the loss of the autumn harvest. (90)

All these "releases" described for the Moon should also be applied to the Sun, but with this difference: the directions (East, etc.) mentioned for the Moon must be reversed for the Sun <note>literally: "as East is for the Moon, so West is to be imagined for the Sun"</note>. (91)

If within seven days of an eclipse there is a fall of dust, it causes a scarcity of food. Mist brings fear of disease; an earthquake brings the death of a prominent king. (92) A meteor destroys ministers; multi-colored clouds bring incomparable fear. Thunder causes the loss of pregnancies; lightning brings suffering from kings and predators <note>literally: "those with tusks/fangs"</note>. (93) A halo around the sun or moon brings suffering from disease; a "burning of the quarters" <note>an atmospheric glow</note> brings fear of kings and fire. A harsh, strong wind brings fear arising from thieves. (94) A thunderclap, a rainbow, or a "staff" <note>a vertical atmospheric phenomenon</note> brings fear of hunger and foreign armies. A "war of the planets" or the appearance of a comet brings war between kings. (95)

If there is a fall of pure water <note>rain</note> within seven days, abundance should be predicted, and all the evil effects generated by the eclipse will be destroyed. (96) If a solar eclipse occurs at the end of the same fortnight as a lunar eclipse, there will be distress among the people and mutual discord between husbands and wives. (97) But if a lunar eclipse is seen after a solar eclipse, then the Brahmins will enjoy the fruits of many sacrifices and the people will be joyful. (98)

->### Thus ends the Fifth Chapter, "The Course of Rahu," in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā composed by the illustrious Varāhamihira. ###<-

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the astronomical and mythological causes of eclipses, specifically addressing the nature of Rahu and the physical mechanics of lunar and solar shadows.</meta>

->Page 37<-
->Chapter 5, with Hindi Commentary<-

Due to a divine boon, Rahu is never seen in the sky at any time other than during an eclipse. <note>1-2</note> Some scholars say that this Rahu is serpent-shaped with a mouth and a tail, while other scholars say that Rahu has no form at all but is instead composed of darkness. <note>3</note> If this Rahu, which moves through the sky, possessed a physical body, a head, or a circular form, then how could it cause an eclipse while being at a distance of half a zodiac cycle <note>original: "bhaganardha," meaning six signs or 180 degrees</note> away? <note>4</note> If there were no stability in Rahu's motion, how could it be known through mathematics? And if it were of a shape possessing a mouth and tail, why would an eclipse not occur at times other than the New Moon or Full Moon? <note>5</note> If its shape were like a serpent, then sometimes the eclipse would be caused by the mouth, sometimes by the tail, and there would even be the possibility of an eclipse caused by its middle section. <note>6</note> If someone were to say there are two Rahus, then while one Rahu was swallowing, rising with, or hiding the Moon, it would be seen that the Sun was also being swallowed by the second Rahu moving at the same pace. <note>7</note>

Whatever the case may be, during a lunar eclipse, the Moon enters the shadow of the Earth, and during a solar eclipse, the Moon enters the solar disc <insert>from the perspective of the observer</insert>; this is the reason why a lunar eclipse does not begin from the west and a solar eclipse does not begin from the east. <note>8</note> Just as the shadow of a tree spreads in one direction by obstructing the Sun, similarly, due to the obstruction of the Sun, the shadow of the Earth also extends daily. <note>9</note> When the Moon is in the seventh sign from the Sun and does not travel too far north or south, then the Moon, moving eastward, enters the shadow of the Earth. <note>10</note> During a solar eclipse, the Moon, situated below the Sun, arrives from the western direction and covers the solar disc like a cloud; this is why the solar eclipse, being dependent on the line of sight, appears differently in every country. <note>11</note> Because the Moon's covering <insert>of the Earth's shadow</insert> is greater, the "horns" or cusps of a half-eclipsed Moon appear very blunt, whereas the covering of the Sun is much less, which is why the cusps of the Sun appear extremely sharp. <note>12</note>

The sages endowed with divine vision have explained the cause of eclipses in this manner; however, naming Rahu as the cause regarding the occurrence of an eclipse is merely to maintain the sacred tradition of the scriptures. <note>13</note> Brahma gave a boon to the demon named Rahu, saying:
> "You shall be satisfied by the portion of the offerings <note>original: "homam"</note> that people perform during the time of an eclipse."
<note>14</note> For this reason, Rahu is present during an eclipse, and because of this, in mathematics, the motion of the Moon also shifts north and south; thus, an eclipse cannot occur at any other time. If the signs of an eclipse are described at any other time, it is considered a portent of calamity <note>original: "utpata"</note>. <note>15-16</note> An eclipse cannot occur even by the conjunction of five planets, and scholars should not believe the scriptural claim about pouring oil into water on the eighth day of the lunar fortnight <note>1</note>. <note>17</note> How the eclipse of the Sun should be determined through parallax <term>avanati: the vertical depression or parallax in latitude</term>, and how the time should be determined according to the direction and the end of the lunar day through deflection <term>valana: the angular deflection of the eclipse's orientation</term>, we have already explained in our authored <term>Karana Granth: a concise astronomical treatise used for calculations</term>. <note>18</note> Brahma, the Moon, Indra, Kubera, Varuna...

---

<margin>1. It is written in the scriptures that by pouring oil into water on the eighth day, the direction in which the oil does not spread is the direction where the eclipse will end, and the opposite direction is where the swallowing (start) will occur. As Garga says: **"On the eighth day, one should indicate the location by throwing oil into water,"** etc. <note>original Latin/Sanskrit: "tatraashtamyaam, jale tailam kshiptvaa sthaanam vinirdishet"</note></margin>

<summary>This page provides a rationalist critique of the mythological serpent Rahu, arguing that eclipses are actually caused by the Earth's shadow and the Moon's position. It reconciles scientific observation with religious tradition by explaining that Rahu's "presence" is a scriptural honor granted by Brahma rather than a physical obstruction.</summary>

# The Varahi Samhita

Agni and Yama, these seven deities, are the lords of eclipses according to an increase of six months each. || 19 || During an eclipse where Brahma is the lord, there is an increase in the population of twice-born <note>Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas</note> and cattle; there is auspiciousness, health, and an abundance of grain. The same occurs during the time of the Moon, though scholars suffer and there is a lack of rain. || 20 || When Indra is the lord of the eclipse, there is conflict among kings, the destruction of autumn crops, and inauspiciousness. During Kubera’s time, the wealth of the rich is destroyed, yet there is a good harvest. || 21 || During Varuna’s time, it is inauspicious for kings, but auspicious for the people, and grain increases. When Agni is the lord, it is called "Mitra" <note>meaning friend/friendly</note>; during this time, there is grain, health, fearlessness, and excellent rainfall. || 22 || When Yama is the lord of the eclipse, his influence causes a lack of rain, famine, and loss of grain. If an eclipse occurs at any other time <note>outside the calculated period</note>, it results in hunger, plague, and drought. || 23 || If an eclipse occurs <term>Velahina</term> <note>prematurely</note>, meaning before the time calculated by mathematics, there is danger to embryos and an outbreak of violence with weapons. If it occurs <term>Ativela</term> <note>belatedly</note>, meaning after the mathematically fixed time, there is destruction of fruits and flowers, fear, and loss of grain. || 24 || The results of eclipses occurring in diminished or extra time were previously described by looking at the ancient scriptures; however, the time stated by one who knows precise mathematics can never be false. || 25 ||

If both the Sun and the Moon are eclipsed within a single month, kings meet their end due to turmoil within their own armies, and the fury of weapons is extreme. || 26 || If the Sun or Moon are eclipsed while being "aspected" <note>influenced by the gaze of</note> by malefic planets at the time of rising or setting, the autumn crops and the king are destroyed. Similarly, if a total eclipse occurs while under the influence of malefic planets, famine and pestilence break out. || 27 ||

If the Sun or Moon is seized by Rahu <note>the shadow planet responsible for eclipses</note> while half-risen, it destroys all <term>Naikritika</term> <note>sacrifices performed with great difficulty or those belonging to the Nishada tribes</note> sacrifices. If the eclipse begins in the <term>Ayugma</term> <note>odd-numbered</note> 1st, 3rd, 5th, or 7th parts of the sky, it destroys those who live by fire (such as goldsmiths and grain-parchers), highly virtuous Brahmins, and those living in hermitages. || 28 || If the eclipse begins in the second part of the sky, farmers, heretics, merchants, Kshatriyas, and army commanders are destroyed. If the eclipse begins in the third part, <term>Karuka</term> <note>artisans/craftsmen</note>, Shudras, barbarians, and ministers are destroyed. || 29 || If the eclipse begins in the middle part of the sky, i.e., at <term>Madhyahna</term> <note>midday</note>, the central kingdom of the king is destroyed, and the price of grain becomes favorable. If the eclipse begins in the fifth part of the sky, those who eat grass <note>livestock</note>, ministers, the <term>Antahpura</term> <note>the inner royal harem</note>, and Vaishyas are destroyed. || 30 || If the eclipse occurs in the sixth part of the sky, women and Shudras are destroyed; and if it begins in the seventh part, i.e., at the time of setting, thieves and inhabitants of barbarian lands like Gahvar are destroyed. However, in whichever part of the sky the "Moksha" <note>release/end of the eclipse</note> occurs, it brings auspiciousness to the regions and creatures associated with that part. || 31 ||

<gloss>1</gloss> If an eclipse occurs during the <term>Uttarayana</term> <note>the northern transit of the sun</note>, there is loss for Brahmins and Kshatriyas. If it occurs during the <term>Dakshinayana</term> <note>the southern transit</note>, there is loss for Vaishyas and Shudras. In the North, East, South, and West, these—

If Rahu <note>The shadow planet or "node" responsible for eclipses in Vedic astrology</note> is seen in any of the four cardinal directions, then in the order of the southern sequence, there is harm to the Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra castes respectively. ||32|| If seen in the Northeast (Ishana), the Mleccha <note>Foreign or non-Vedic</note> tribes suffer; if in the Southeast (Agni), travelers suffer; in the South, aquatic creatures and elephants; and in the North, cattle and livestock face misfortune. ||33|| If Rahu approaches from the East, the earth will be filled with water; if it comes from the West, farmers, servants, and seeds will be destroyed. ||34||

If an eclipse of Rahu is observed in the sign of **Aries** <term>Mesha-rashi: The first sign of the zodiac</term>, then Punjab, Kalinga, Shurasena, Kamboj, Audu, Kirat, and Shastravartta (those who bear arms) and all such countries, as well as those who earn their living through fire <note>e.g., blacksmiths or goldsmiths</note>, will all be greatly distressed. ||35|| If the Sun or Moon are eclipsed by Rahu in **Taurus** <term>Vrishabha-rashi</term>, then cowherds, animals—especially those who keep cattle—and highly virtuous or talented people will be greatly distressed. ||36||

If an eclipse occurs in **Gemini** <term>Mithuna-rashi</term>, then noble women, kings, ordinary kings (landlords), powerful men, dancers, singers, musicians, those living on the banks of the Yamuna river, and the inhabitants of Bahlika, Matsya, and Suhya countries will suffer. ||37|| If the eclipse of the Moon or Sun occurs in **Cancer** <term>Karkata-rashi</term>, then the Abhiras, the Shabar tribe, and the people of Pallava, Malla, Matsya, Kuru, Shaka, Panchala, and Vikala countries will be distressed, and grains will be destroyed. ||38||

By an eclipse in **Leo** <term>Simha-rashi</term>, the Pulindas, Mekala, powerful kings, men equal to kings, and forest-dwellers are destroyed. If the eclipse is in **Virgo** <term>Kanya-rashi</term>, then poets, writers, and those who earn their living by singing songs are destroyed; crops are ruined, and the prominent regions of Ashmaka, Tripura, and Shali are devastated. ||39|| If the eclipse of the Sun or Moon is in **Libra** <term>Tula-rashi</term>, then the Avanti country, the lands near the western sea, the Dasharna country, holy men, merchants, and the king of the Maccha-Kaccha country will be destroyed. If the eclipse is in **Scorpio** <term>Vrishchika-rashi</term>, then the people of Udumbara, Madra, and Chola countries, trees, great warriors, and those who deal in poison will be destroyed. ||40||

If the eclipse occurs in **Sagittarius** <term>Dhanu-rashi</term>, then ministers, noble horses, the countries of Videha, Malla, and Panchala, physicians, merchants, and men skilled in irregular weapons will be destroyed. By a solar eclipse in **Capricorn** <term>Makara-rashi</term>, the Matsyas, ministerial families, those skilled in low counsel or in knowing and preparing medicines, and elderly weapon-bearers are destroyed. ||41|| If the eclipse occurs in **Aquarius** <term>Kumbha-rashi</term>, then mountain-dwellers, westerners, porters, thieves, Ahirs, the Darad Aryans, and the people of Singhanagar and the Barbar country will be destroyed. If the eclipse occurs in **Pisces** <term>Meena-rashi</term>, then those on the seacoast, products born of sea water, respected men, scholars, and those who earn a living from water, such as fishermen and boatmen, will be destroyed. In this manner, the results of eclipses are told according to the *Kurmopadesha* <note>The "Instruction of the Tortoise," a traditional geographical arrangement of India</note>, that is, according to the tortoise-shaped division of the earth. ||42||

There are ten types of "grasps" (obscurations) in the eclipses of the Moon and Sun, namely: 1. Savya (Right), 2. Apasavya (Left), 3. Leha (Licking), 4. Grasana (Swallowing), 5. Nirodha (Obstruction), 6. Avamarda (Crushing), 7. Aroha (Ascending), 8. Aghata (Striking), 9. Madhyatama (Central Darkness), and 10. Tamantya (Edge Darkness). ||43|| If Rahu moves to the right, that is, if the eclipse is called *Savya*, the world will be filled with water; people will be joyful and fearless. In the *Apasavya* grasp, the subjects are destroyed due to distress caused by kings or thieves. ||44|| If Rahu licks the lunar orb like a tongue, that eclipse is called *Leha*. By the occurrence of this eclipse, the creatures of the earth are joyful and much water rains upon the earth. ||45|| When one-quarter, one-half, or three-quarters of the planetary orb is seized, it is called *Grasana*. This causes the destruction of the wealth of proud kings and to proud countries...

## The Varahi Samhita

...suffering occurs. <note>Verse 46</note> When <term>Rahu</term><note>The celestial shadow-demon responsible for eclipses</note> swallows the solar or lunar orb up to its outer boundary and remains seated in the center like a solid mass, it is called **Nirodha** (Obstruction). This brings joy to all living beings. <note>Verse 47</note>

If the shadow of Rahu completely covers the orb for a long duration, it is called **Avamardana** (Crushing). This leads to the destruction of the primary regions, the chief leaders, and the prominent kings, and there is a fear of darkness. <note>Verse 48</note>

When Rahu covers the circular orb—that is, an eclipse occurs—and then Rahu becomes visible again immediately, it is called **Arohana** (Ascending). This causes kings to have extreme fear of mutual warfare. <note>Verse 49</note>

Just as a mirror becomes clouded by the vapor of breath, if one side of the Moon or Sun appears soiled by Rahu, that grasp is called **Aghata** (Blow). This results in good rains in the world and the prosperity of the entire universe. <note>Verse 50</note>

If Rahu enters the central part of the Moon while the edges of the lunar orb remain clear, this grasp is called **Madhyatama** (Central Darkness). This destroys the <term>Madhyadesha</term><note>The "Middle Country" of ancient India, roughly the Ganges-Yamuna doab</note> and causes diseases of the womb. <note>Verse 51</note>

When Rahu is seen predominantly on the outer boundary of the lunar orb and only slightly in the center, it is called the grasp named **Tamontya** (Final Darkness). This brings fear of <term>Iti</term><note>The six traditional calamities of agriculture: drought, floods, locusts, rats, birds, and foreign invasion</note> which destroys grains, and fear of thieves. <note>Verse 52</note>

If Rahu is white in color, there is auspiciousness, plenty of food, but suffering for the <term>Brahmins</term><note>The priestly class</note>. If it is the color of fire, there is fear of fire, and those who earn their living through fire, such as blacksmiths, suffer. <note>Verse 53</note>

If Rahu is green, there is an increase in disease and the destruction of grain by agricultural pests. If Rahu is tawny-colored, swift-moving creatures and <term>Mlechhas</term><note>Foreigners or non-Vedic peoples</note> will be destroyed, and there will be famine. <note>Verse 54</note>

If the color of Rahu appears reddish-brown, there is famine, lack of rain, and suffering for birds. If it is somewhat the color of smoke, there is auspiciousness and plenty, but rainfall is sparse. <note>Verse 55</note>

If Rahu appears the color of a pigeon, reddish-brown, tawny, or brownish-yellow, there is fear of hunger. If it is the color of a dove or black, the <term>Shudras</term><note>The laboring class</note> suffer. <note>Verse 56</note>

If Rahu is yellow like a pure gem, the <term>Vaishyas</term><note>The merchant and farmer class</note> are destroyed, but there is plenty of food. If it is like a flame of fire, there is fear of fire, and if it appears like red ochre, there is war. <note>Verse 57</note>

If Rahu appears dark like a blade of <term>Durva</term> grass or yellow like turmeric, a plague occurs. If the color of Rahu is like a pale red trumpet-flower, there is fear of lightning strikes. <note>Verse 58</note>

If it appears like dust or red-colored, there is rain and the destruction of <term>Kshatriyas</term><note>The warrior and ruling class</note>. If the color of Rahu is like the morning sun, a lotus, or a rainbow, there is the fury of weapons (war). <note>Verse 59</note>

Now the **Results of Aspects** (planetary glances) are described:
If the eclipsed orb is aspected by **Mercury**, then ghee, honey, and oil become expensive, and there is fear of kings. If aspected by **Mars**, there is crushing in war, the fury of fire, and fear of thieves. <note>Verse 60</note>

If aspected by **Venus**, there is destruction of grains on earth and various types of calamities. If aspected by **Saturn**, there is famine, drought, and fear of thieves. <note>Verse 61</note>

All the inauspicious results mentioned due to the appearance at the beginning or end of an eclipse are pacified by the aspect of **Jupiter**, just as a great fire is extinguished by a mass of water. <note>Verse 62</note>

Eclipses often occur six months after omens such as strong winds, meteors, dust storms, earthquakes, darkness, and lightning strikes. <note>Verse 63</note>

If an eclipse occurs in the sign of **Mars**, the Avanti region, the lands near the Kaveri and Narmada rivers, and all proud kings are destroyed...

If the lunar eclipse ends in the southeast corner, it is called the Right Jaw-cleaving release; this causes the destruction of grain, diseases of the mouth, suffering for the King, but results in good rainfall ||82|| When the release occurs from the northeast corner, it is the Left Jaw-cleaving release; this brings fear to the King and princes, mouth diseases, fear of weapons, and abundance of food ||83|| When the release is from the south, it is the Right Belly-cleaving release, which causes pain to princes and conflict among enemies in the south ||84||

If Rahu <note>The celestial shadow-demon responsible for eclipses in Vedic mythology</note> is positioned in the northern side, it is the Left Belly-cleaving release; this brings danger to the pregnancies of women and the grain harvest is mediocre ||85|| If the release is from the southwest corner, it is called the Right Wind-cleaving; both types of this release cause general hidden ailments <note>literally 'secret pains'</note> and good rain, while the Left Wind-cleaving causes the decline of the Queen ||86|| If Rahu begins to swallow the orb from the eastern part and returns toward the east, it is called the Vomiting release; this brings welfare to the world and happiness through grain ||87||

That in which the eclipse begins in the east and the release occurs in the western regions is called the Digestion release; when the Digestion release occurs, men, troubled by hunger and the fear of weapons, wander without knowing where to find refuge ||88|| When the center is illuminated first, it is called the Middle-splitting release; this causes mental anger among creatures, and though it provides some abundance, the rains are not excellent, and there is turmoil in the kingdom ||89|| If, during a lunar eclipse, the edges of the orb are clear while a thick dark shadow remains in the center, it is the End-splitting release; this destroys the central regions and the autumn crops ||90|| These are the releases described for the lunar eclipse; all these matters should also be applied to the solar eclipse, but where 'east' is mentioned for the Moon, 'west' should be applied for the Sun ||91||

If within seven days after the release, dust falls from the sky, the grain is destroyed; if there is fog, there is fear of disease; an earthquake brings the death of a great King; a falling star (meteor) destroys the Minister; and if multicolored clouds appear at times other than twilight, there is great terror. Thunder causes miscarriages; lightning strikes cause pain to the King and to tusked animals like snakes and boars; a halo around the sun or moon brings the pain of disease. A glow in the sky (*Digdaha*) brings fear of the state and fire; fierce and dry winds bring fear of thieves. A sudden thunderclap (*Nirghata*), the appearance of a rainbow, or a collision of winds brings famine and fear from the armies of other kings. A conflict between planets leads to war between kings; the sighting of Ketu <note>A comet or the descending node of the moon</note> also leads to war. If, within seven days after the eclipse release, there is good rain without any unnatural disturbances, then there is abundance, and all the evil effects of the eclipse are destroyed ||92||||93||||94||||95||||96||

# Now begins the Sixth Chapter
## The Transit of Mars <note>original: "Bhaumachara"</note>

**If Mars begins its retrograde motion in the ninth, eighth, or seventh constellation <note>term: Nakshatra (lunar mansion)</note> from the one in which it rose, that retrograde motion is called "Ushna" (Hot). During its rise, it causes suffering to those who earn their living through fire <note>such as blacksmiths or goldsmiths</note>. || 1 || If Mars turns retrograde in the twelfth, tenth, or eleventh constellation from its rising sign, it is called "Ashrumukha" (Tear-faced). At its rise, it spoils liquids <note>juices, oils, or dairy</note> and causes diseases and drought. || 2 || If the retrograde motion occurs in the thirteenth or fourteenth constellation from the one in which it sets, it is called "Vyala" (Serpent-like). It causes suffering from tusked animals, snakes, and wild beasts, yet brings about plenty of food. || 3 || If it turns back from the fifteenth or sixteenth constellation, it is called "Rudhiranan" (Blood-faced). At that time, it brings diseases of the mouth and fear, but also a good harvest. || 4 || If it turns retrograde in the seventeenth or eighteenth constellation, it is called "Asimushala" (Sword and Club). It causes suffering from gangs of robbers, drought, and the fear of weapons. || 5 || If Mars rises in Purva Phalguni or Uttara Phalguni and turns back in Rohini, or if it sets in Rohini, it oppresses the inhabitants of all three worlds. || 6 || If it rises in Shravana and turns retrograde in Pushya, it causes suffering to anointed kings. In whichever constellation it rises, it destroys the people of the regions associated with that constellation. || 7 || If Mars <note>original: "Lohita" (The Red One)</note> moves back and forth through the middle of Magha, then the Pandya king perishes, and there is fear from military expeditions and a lack of rain. || 8 || By breaking through Magha and Vishakha, Mars causes famine. If it pierces through Rohini, it causes a terrible plague. || 9 || Moving to the south of Rohini, the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> causes partial rain and high prices. If it appears smoky or crested with flames, it destroys the people of the Pariyatra mountains. || 10 || While traversing Rohini, Shravana, Mula, the three Uttaras, or Jyeshtha, the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> destroys hoards of wealth. || 11 || The rising of Mars is considered auspicious in Shravana, Magha, Punarvasu, Mula, and Hasta; also in Purva Bhadrapada, Ashwini, Vishakha, and Rohini. || 12 || If the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> moves along the northern path, possessing a large and clear body, colored like the Kimshuka or Ashoka flower <note>bright red</note>, with distinct and beautiful rays like molten copper, it brings prosperity to kings and joy to the subjects. || 13 ||**

->Thus ends the sixth chapter, "The Transit of Mars," in the *Brihat Samhita* by Sri Varahamihira. || 6 ||<-

During its rise, all liquids become spoiled, and diseases and drought occur. ||2|| Similarly, in whichever constellation Mars sets, if its "Vipaka"—that is, its retrograde motion—occurs in the thirteenth or fourteenth constellation from that setting constellation, then this...

# Varahi Samhita

(44)

The retrograde motion is named 'Vyala' <note>Sanskrit: *Vyala* meaning serpent or predator</note>; during this period, there is suffering caused by tusked animals, predators, and deer, yet there is an abundance of food (a good harvest) ॥3॥ If the retrograde of Mars occurs in the fifteenth or sixteenth lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra (lunar mansion)</term> from the mansion of its setting, it is called 'Rudhiranan' <note>Sanskrit: *Rudhiranan* meaning 'Blood-faced'</note>. At that time, people suffer from mouth diseases and fear, though food remains plentiful ॥4॥ If the sub-retrograde <note>secondary retrograde motion</note> of Mars occurs in the seventeenth or eighteenth mansion from its setting, it is called 'Asimushala' <note>Sanskrit: *Asimushala* meaning 'Sword and Mace'</note>; this leads to fear of thieves, fear of weapons, and drought ॥5॥ If the planet Mars rises in the *Purva Phalguni* or *Uttara Phalguni* mansions, turns retrograde in *Uttara Ashadha*, and sets in the *Rohini* mansion, then all three worlds—Heaven, Earth, and the Underworld—suffer distress ॥6॥ If Mars rises in the *Shravana* mansion and turns retrograde in the *Pushya* mansion, the 'Anointed Ones' <note>original: *Murdhabhishikta*, referring to consecrated Kings or the Kshatriya caste</note> suffer; furthermore, whichever direction the rising mansion belongs to, the people living in that direction face destruction ॥7॥ If Mars passes through the *Magha* mansion, it causes the destruction of the Pandya King, fear of weapons, and lack of rain ॥8॥ If Mars pierces through the *Magha* mansion and then pierces the *Vishakha* mansion, a famine occurs; if it pierces through *Rohini*, a great plague or high mortality follows. If the 'Son of Earth' <note>a common epithet for Mars</note> wanders beside the *Rohini* mansion, goods become expensive and the rains fail. If it appears with a crest/tail and looks as if covered in smoke, the inhabitants of the Pariyatra mountains <note>Western Vindhya range</note> are destroyed ॥9॥10॥ If Mars wanders through *Rohini, Shravana, Mula, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada,* or *Jyeshtha*, the clouds are destroyed (no rain) ॥11॥ It is considered auspicious for Mars to wander or rise in the *Shravana, Magha, Punarvasu, Mula, Hasta, Purva Bhadrapada, Ashwini, Vishakha,* and *Rohini* mansions ॥12॥ If the planet Mars is large, clear in form, colored like the Flame-of-the-Forest <note>Palash</note> or Ashoka flower, possesses bright and beautiful rays, and has the luster of molten copper while moving in the Northern Path <note>Northern declination</note>, it brings good fortune to Kings and happiness to the subjects ॥13॥

->Thus ends the sixth chapter of the Hindi commentary on the Brihat Samhita, composed by Sri Varahamihira, written by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western province. ॥6॥<-

### Now begins the Seventh Chapter
### The Transit of Mercury

The Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> never rises without being deprived of the sun's heat <note>due to its proximity to the sun</note>. It causes fear from water, fire, and wind, or leads to an increase in the prices of grains ॥1॥ While traversing *Shravana, Dhanishta, Rohini, Mrigashira,* or *Vaishvadeva* <note>Uttara Ashadha</note>, if the Son of the Moon crushes <note>afflicts</note> these, it causes drought along with the fear of disease ॥2॥ When the Son of the Moon stays in the mansions starting from *Ardra* and ending with *Magha*, there is suffering for the subjects through the fall of weapons, hunger, fear, disease, drought, and great distress ॥3॥ While traversing and afflicting the six mansions starting from *Hasta*, it is inauspicious for cattle; however, it causes an increase in the price of oils and liquids and fills the earth with abundant grain ॥4॥ By striking *Aryaman* <note>Uttara Phalguni</note>, *Hautabhuj* <note>Krittika</note>, *Uttara Bhadrapada*, and *Yamya* <note>Bharani</note>, the Son of the Moon causes the depletion of the vital humors <note>health</note> of living beings ॥5॥ By crushing *Ashwini, Varuna* <note>Shatabhisha</note>, *Mula*, and *Revati*, the Son of the Moon brings harm to traders, physicians, those who live by fire <note>blacksmiths/cooks</note>, aquatic products, and cowherds ॥6॥

# Chapter 7: The Course of Mercury
## From the Brihat Samhita by Varahamihira

If Mercury, the son of the Moon, should pierce <note>The term "pierce" (abhimardati) refers to a planetary conjunction or occultation where one body appears to strike or pass through another's space.</note> any of the three "Purva" stars <note>Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada.</note>, he moves through the world bringing hunger, weapons, thieves, and disease. || 7 ||

In the treatise of the sage Parashara <note>An ancient Vedic seer and one of the founding fathers of Indian astronomy/astrology.</note>, seven distinct motions of Mercury are described according to the constellations: Natural, Mixed, Shortened, Sharp, End-of-Yoga, Terrible, and Evil. || 8 ||

The **Natural** (Prakrita) motion involves the constellations of Vayu, Yama, Brahma, and Bahula <note>Svati, Bharani, Rohini, and Krittika.</note>. The **Mixed** (Mishra) motion occurs in the constellations of the Moon, Shiva, the Ancestors, the Serpent, and the Gods <note>Mrigashira, Ardra, Magha, Ashlesha, and Vishakha.</note>. || 9 ||

In the **Shortened** (Sankshipta) motion are Pushya, Punarvasu, and the two Phalgunis. In the **Sharp** (Tikshna) motion are the two Bhadrapadas, Jyeshtha, Ashwini, and Revati. || 10 ||

The **End-of-Yoga** (Yogantika) motion belongs to Mula and the two Ashadhas. The **Terrible** (Ghora) motion includes Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, and Chitra. || 11 ||

The **Evil** (Papa) motion includes Savitra, Maitra, and Vishakha <note>Hasta, Anuradha, and Vishakha.</note>. The sage Parashara also defined these motions by the number of days Mercury remains visible or invisible. || 12 ||

The durations for the motions starting with the "Natural" one are: 40, 30, 22, 18, 9, 15, and 11 days; or otherwise 9 months, half a month, or 10 months plus one. <note>These figures represent the varying periods Mercury stays in certain sectors of the sky.</note> || 13 ||

In the **Natural** motion, there is health, rain, growth of crops, and safety. In the **Shortened** and **Mixed** motions, the results are mixed. In all other motions, the effects are the opposite <note>i.e., harmful.</note>. || 14 ||

According to the opinion of Devala <note>Another ancient authority on Dharma and Astrology.</note>, there are four types of movement: Straight, Very Crooked, Crooked, and Deficient. These last for 30, 24, 12, and 6 days respectively, multiplied by six. || 15 ||

**Straight** motion is beneficial for the people; **Very Crooked** motion destroys wealth; **Crooked** motion brings fear of weapons; and **Deficient** motion generates fear and disease. || 16 ||

If Mercury is seen in the months of Pausha, Ashadha, Shravana, Vaishakha, or Magha, it brings fear to the world. If it remains invisible during these months, it produces auspicious results. || 17 ||

If the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is seen in the months of Kartika or Ashwayuja, he creates fear from weapons, thieves, fire, sickness, and hunger. || 18 ||

When Mercury sets in the east, those regions that were oppressed are liberated; others say that when he rises in the west, the cities gain prosperity. || 19 ||

If Mercury has the color of gold, or is green like a parrot, or resembles the *Sasyaka* gem <note>Likely an emerald or malachite.</note>, and appears glossy and large, he is beneficial. If he appears otherwise, he is not auspicious. || 20 ||

->**Thus ends the Seventh Chapter, "The Course of Mercury," in the Brihat Samhita of Shri Varahamihira.**<-

<margin>Mercury, the son of the Moon, never rises without causing some omen. At the time of Mercury's rising, there is often rain, fire, or storms, which cause the price of grain to fluctuate.</margin>

1. Shravana, Dhanishtha, Rohini, Mrigashira, or Uttara Ashadha: If Mercury treads here, there is fear of disease and drought. || 2 ||
2. From Ardra to Magha: If Mercury is present in any of these, there is suffering from weapons, hunger, fear, disease, and heat. || 3 ||
3. From Hasta to Jyeshtha: If Mercury moves through these six, cattle suffer, the price of oil rises, but the earth is filled with various goods. || 4 ||
4. Uttara Phalguni, Krittika, Uttara Bhadrapada, and Bharani: If struck by Mercury, the "vital humors" <term>Dhatu: in Ayurveda, the seven fundamental tissues of the body</term> of living beings are depleted. || 5 ||
5. Ashwini, Shatabhisha, Mula, and Revati: If Mercury pierces these, there is trouble for market goods, physicians, sailors, aquatic products, and horses. || 6 ||
6. Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada: If Mercury pierces any of these three, there is hunger, weapons, thieves, disease, and fear in the world. || 7 ||

Seven types of motion for Mercury <note>original: "Budha"</note> are described based on the constellations <note>original: "Nakshatras"</note>: 1. Natural <note>Prakrita</note>, 2. Mixed <note>Vimishra</note>, 3. Abridged <note>Sankshipta</note>, 4. Sharp <note>Tikshna</note>, 5. Conjunctional <note>Yoganta</note>, 6. Terrible <note>Ghora</note>, and 7. Evil <note>Papa</note>. ||8|| When Mercury is in the constellations of Svati, Bharani, Rohini, or Krittika, this motion is called **Natural**. When in Mrigashira, Ardra, Magha, or Ashlesha, the motion is called **Mixed**. ||9|| In Pushya, Punarvasu, Purva Phalguni, or Uttara Phalguni, it is **Abridged**; and in Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada, Jyeshtha, Ashvini, or Revati, the motion of Mercury is called **Sharp**. ||10|| The motion occurring in Mula, Purva Ashadha, or Uttara Ashadha is called **Conjunctional**, and the motion in Shravana, Chitra, Dhanishtha, or Shatabhisha is called **Terrible**. ||11|| When Mercury resides in Hasta, Anuradha, or Jyeshtha, the name of its motion is **Evil**. In this manner, the Sage Parashara has determined the motions and characteristics of Mercury based on the days between its rising and setting. ||12||

The **Natural** motion lasts 40 days, **Mixed** 30 days, **Abridged** 22 days, **Sharp** 18 days, **Conjunctional** 9 days, **Terrible** 15 days, and the **Evil** motion lasts for 11 days. ||13|| During Mercury's Natural motion, there is health, rain, increase in grain, and auspiciousness. In the Abridged and Mixed motions, the results are mixed—neither very good nor very bad—and in the other motions, the results are contrary <note>inauspicious</note>. ||14|| According to the opinion of Devala, Mercury's motion is of four types: **Straight** <note>Rijvi</note>, **Excessively Retrograde** <note>Ativakra</note>, **Retrograde** <note>Vakra</note>, and **Deficient** <note>Vikala</note>. The duration of these motions is 30 days, 24 days, 12 days, and 6 days respectively. ||15|| Straight motion is beneficial for the subjects; Excessively Retrograde motion causes loss of wealth; Retrograde motion brings fear of weapons; and Deficient motion brings fear and disease. ||16||

If the planet Mercury is visible in the months of Pausha, Ashadha, Shravana, Vaishakha, or Magha, there is fear in the world; if it sets during this time, it is auspicious. ||17|| If Mercury, the son of the Moon, is visible in the months of Kartika or Ashvin, there is fear of weapons, thieves, fire, disease, water, and hunger. ||18|| Regarding the transit of Mercury, learned men who know all things well say that cities which are besieged during Mercury's setting are released when Mercury rises. Some say that if Mercury rises in the western direction, all the towns in that direction will gain profit. ||19|| When the color of Mercury, the son of the Moon, is like gold, or like a parrot, or like a green emerald <note>original: "Sasyakamani"</note>, and when Mercury's form is clear and large, then there is auspiciousness for all. If it is not so, it is inauspicious. ||20||

->Thus ends the Seventh Chapter in the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western province, on the Brihat Samhita composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira.<-

# Chapter Eight
## The Transit of Jupiter <note>original: "Brihaspati-chara"</note>

The year is to be named after the constellation <note>Nakshatra</note> in which the Minister of the King of Gods <note>Jupiter/Brihaspati</note> rises, following the sequence of the months. ||1|| The years beginning with Kartika follow in pairs from the constellation Krittika <note>Agneya</note> in succession; however, the fifth, the penultimate, and the final years are associated with three constellations each. ||2|| In the year of Kartika, there is suffering for those who live by carts and fire, distress for cattle, and outbreaks of disease and weapons, but there is an increase in red and yellow flowers. ||3|| In the year of Margashirsha <note>Saumya</note>, there is a lack of rain...
