When Jupiter is in the month of **Pausha** <note>December-January</note>, it brings goodness to the world; kings cease their hostilities toward one another. The price of grain increases two or three-fold, and acts of nourishment and strengthening <term>Paushtika-karma: rituals for prosperity</term> meet with success. || 5 ||

In **Magha** <note>January-February</note>, there is an increase in the worship of ancestors <note>Pitru-puja</note> and affection among all living beings. There is health, rain, an abundance of grain, and the gaining of friends. || 6 ||

If it rains in **Phalguna** <note>February-March</note>, know that in some places there will be an increase in welfare and crops. However, women may face misfortune, and thieves will become powerful. || 7 ||

In **Chaitra** <note>March-April</note>, rain is sparse, but food is dear, there is safety, and rulers become mild-mannered. There is an increase in the treasury and grain, but those of beautiful form <note>perhaps the elite or youth</note> suffer. || 8 ||

In **Vaishakha** <note>April-May</note>, people and their kings are devoted to righteousness <term>Dharma</term>, free from fear, and joyful. Sacrificial rites <note>Yajna</note> flourish, and all crops reach fulfillment. || 9 ||

In **Jyeshtha** <note>May-June</note>, the leaders of castes, families, wealthy guilds, and kings become knowers of righteousness. Grains suffer, except for millet <note>Kangu</note> and varieties of legumes <note>Shami</note>. || 10 ||

In **Ashadha** <note>June-July</note>, crops grow in some places while rain falls elsewhere. General welfare <term>Yoga-kshema</term> is mediocre, and rulers become preoccupied or anxious. || 11 ||

When it rains in **Shravana** <note>July-August</note>, there is safety and crops ripen fully. Lowly heretics <term>Pashandas</term> and those devoted to them suffer. || 12 ||

In **Bhadrapada** <note>August-September</note>, creeping plants <term>Vallija</term> and early crops reach fulfillment. Late crops do not grow; in some places there is plenty, in others, fear. || 13 ||

In the year of **Ashwayuja** <note>September-October</note>, water falls incessantly, the people are joyful and safe. There is a restoration of life-force in all living beings and an abundance of food. || 14 ||

When the Lord of Speech <note>Jupiter/Brihaspati</note> moves through the northern stars, he brings health, plenty, and safety. In the south, the opposite occurs; in the middle, the results are middling. || 15 ||

Moving through the center of the asterisms is desirable; in such a year, the results are moderate. If he should ever move excessively <note>in retrograde or fast motion</note>, he destroys the crops. || 16 ||

If Jupiter appears fire-colored, there is fear of fire; if yellow, disease; if dark/blue, the coming of war. If green, suffering from thieves; if red, fear of weapons. || 17 ||

If he appears smoke-colored, there is drought. If the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> is seen during the day, a king is killed. If he is seen at night as large, clear, and bright, the people remain healthy and at peace. || 18 ||

**Rohini** is the body of the year, **Krittika** the heart, the two **Ashadhas** the navel, **Aslesha** the heart <note>alternate system</note>, and **Magha** the flower. If these are clear, the fruit is good. If the body is afflicted by cruel planets, there is fear from wind; if the navel, fear from hunger; if **Pushya**, loss of roots and fruits; if the heart, the destruction of crops is certain. || 19 ||

Take the years elapsed since the era of the Saka King <note>78 CE</note>, multiply by eleven and then by four. Add 8589 and divide by 3750. || 20 ||

Add the result to the Saka era year, then divide by sixty. The quotient gives the cycles <term>Yugas</term> starting from Narayana; the remainders are the years <term>Samvatsaras</term> in sequence. || 21 ||

# The Varahi Samhita

...[the previous years] are mentioned. Four are considered middling, four are average, and the final four should be known as inferior. || 26 ||

When Jupiter <note>original: "Surejya," a title for Jupiter meaning "Teacher of the Gods"</note> rises in the first degree of the lunar mansion Dhanistha in the month of Magha <note>roughly January/February</note>, the first year of the sixty-year cycle, named **Prabhava**, begins. This year is generally beneficial for all living beings. || 27 ||

In some places, there may be localized rain, or disturbances from wind and fire; there may also be calamities <note>term: "Itis" — the six traditional calamities of agriculture: drought, floods, locusts, rats, birds, and foreign invasion</note> and diseases caused by phlegm. Nevertheless, even when this year of **Prabhava** prevails, the people do not suffer excessively. || 28 ||

After that, the second year is declared to be **Vibhava**, the third is **Shukla**, the fourth is **Pramoda**, and the fifth is **Prajapati**. As these years follow one another, they are considered increasingly auspicious in their fruits. || 29 ||

During these years, the Earth <note>original: "Bhutadhatri," the supporter of beings</note> produces abundant crops of rice, sugarcane, and barley; she is free from fear and hostilities are pacified. The people are joyful and liberated from the vices of the Kali age <note>the current dark age in Hindu cosmology</note>, while the ruling class protects the land. || 30 ||

In the second five-year cycle <note>term: "Yuga" — here referring to a 5-year sub-cycle of the 60-year Jovian period</note>, the years are **Angiras**, **Shrimukha**, **Bhava**, **Yuvan**, and **Dhata**. Among these five, the first three are auspicious, while the latter two are considered average. || 31 ||

During the three years starting with **Angiras**, the gods grant rain as desired and the world is free from disease and fear. In the final two years of this cycle, the rainfall is average, but there are diseases and the onset of wars. || 32 ||

In the third cycle, dedicated to Indra <note>original: "Shakra"</note>, the first year is **Ishvara**, the second is **Bahudhanya** <note>meaning "Many Grains"</note>, followed by **Pramathin**, **Vikrama**, and **Vrisha**. These are known through the movements of Jupiter. || 33 ||

The first and second years of this cycle bring a likeness of the Golden Age <note>original: "Krita-yuga"</note> to the people. However, the year **Pramathin** is wicked, while **Vrisha** and **Vikrama** provide good food but also bring the fear of disease. || 34 ||

The first year of the fourth cycle, which they call **Chitrabhanu**, is excellent. The second, named **Subhanu**, is middling; while it brings some disease, it is not deadly. || 35 ||

After that comes **Tarana**, which brings abundant rain clouds; then **Parthiva**, which is said to increase crops and joy. The fifth is **Vyaya**, which is considered pleasant, characterized by the influence of love <note>original: "Manmatha," the god of desire</note> and many festivals. || 36 ||

In the cycle dedicated to Tvashtar, **Sarvajit** is said to be the first, and the next year is **Sarvadhari**. After that come **Virodha**, **Vikrita**, and **Khara**. In this group, the second year is auspicious, but the rest bring fear. || 37 || <note>Verse 37 is incorrectly numbered as 7 in the source.</note>

Then come **Nandana**, **Vijaya**, **Jaya**, **Manmatha**, and after that **Durmukha**. In this cycle, the first three are beautiful/pleasant; **Manmatha** yields average results, and the last one is inferior. || 38 ||

In the seventh cycle, there is **Hemalamba**, followed by **Vilamba**, **Vikari**, **Sharvari**, and then **Plava**, which is the fifth year according to Jupiter's position. || 39 ||

In the first year of this cycle, there are generally strong winds and rain; in the second year, crops are slow to grow and water is not abundant. The third year brings great anxiety but much water; the fourth, **Sharvari**, leads to famine, but the following year, **Plava**, is auspicious with plenty of water. || 40 ||

In the cycle dedicated to Vishnu, the first year is **Kshobhakrit**, followed by the auspicious **Shubhakrit**. The third is **Krodhi**, followed in order by **Vishvavasu** and **Parabhava**. || 41 ||

The first and second of these bring joy to the people, but the third year brings many faults/evils. The last two are average, but in **Parabhava**, there is danger from fire, weapons, and disease, as well as fear for Brahmins and cattle. || 42 ||

In the ninth cycle, the first year is **Plavanga**, the next is **Kilaka**, and after that is **Saumya**. Then come **Sadharana** and **Rodhakrit**. The years named **Kilaka** and **Saumya** bestow blessings. || 43 ||

**Plavanga** is difficult for many people; **Sadharana** brings little water and some calamities. The fifth year, **Rodhakrit**, brings strange/varied rainfall and a wealth of crops. || 44 ||

In the tenth cycle, dedicated to the dual gods Indra and Agni, the first year is named **Paridhavin**. After that comes **Pramadin**, then **Ananda**, followed by **Rakshasa** and **Anala**. || 45 ||

# Chapter 8 with Hindi Commentary

In the year *Paridhavin*, there is destruction in the central regions, the loss of kings, little water, and anger from fire. In the year *Pramadin*, people become lazy, and there is strife along with the destruction of red flowers and seeds. ॥46॥

The year *Ananda* brings joy to all people, while *Rakshasa* is destructive and fiery. In *Rakshasa*, summer grains are produced, but there is anger from fire and hellish suffering in *Anala*. ॥47॥

In the eleventh cycle are *Pingala*, *Kalayukta*, *Siddhartha*, *Raudra*, and *Durmati*. In the first (*Pingala*), there is great rain, but also thieves, breathing difficulties, and coughing with trembling of the jaw. ॥48॥

The year *Kalayukta* possesses many faults, while in the year named *Siddhartha*, there are many virtues. *Raudra* is declared to be extremely fierce and destructive, and *Durmati* brings moderate rain. ॥49॥

In the final cycle, the first year named *Dundubhi* brings a great increase in crops. Following that is *Udgari*, which leads to the destruction of kings and uneven rainfall. ॥50॥

The third year is called *Raktaksha*, in which there is fear from tusked animals <note>likely wild boars or elephants</note> and diseases. The fourth is *Krodha*, which causes much anger and leaves kingdoms desolate due to conflict. ॥51॥

The final year of the cycle is *Kshaya*, which causes much depletion and fear; however, it brings growth for Brahmins and farmers. It is said to bring prosperity to the Vaishyas and Shudras, as well as to those who take the property of others. Thus, the sixty-year cycle has been described in brief. ॥52॥

If the Guru of the Immortals <note>Jupiter</note> is thick-bodied, possesses clear rays, and shines like a white water-lily, jasmine, or crystal, and is not struck by other planets, he remains on the path of truth and is beneficial to mankind. ॥53॥

->Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Course of Jupiter," in the Brihat Samhita composed by Sri Varahamihira.<-

***

The year is named after the month corresponding to the lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra: one of the 27 sectors of the sky along the ecliptic</term> in which Jupiter, the minister of Indra, rises. ॥1॥ Since there are twelve months, there are twelve such years. Starting from the *Kruttika* Nakshatra, each year corresponds to two Nakshatras (e.g., the year *Kartika*). However, among these twelve years, the fifth, eleventh, and twelfth years will encompass three Nakshatras. For example, if Jupiter rises in the *Kruttika* or *Rohini* Nakshatras, the year is called *Kartika*. ॥2॥

(1) If it is the year named **Kartika**, those who earn a living via carts (traders/nomads), those who live by fire <note>blacksmiths or priests</note>, and cattle suffer. People are afflicted by disease and the fury of weapons. Red and yellow flowers flourish. ॥3॥

(2) If it is the year named **Saumya** <note>Margashirsha</note>, there is a lack of rain. Crops are destroyed by deer, mice, locusts, and birds. Humans fear disease, and even kings who were friends become enemies. ॥4॥

(3) In the year named **Pausha**, the world experiences auspiciousness. Kings abandon their mutual animosity, the price of grain doubles or triples, and there is an increase in nourishing activities. ॥5॥

(4) In the year named **Magha**, the worship of ancestors increases. All living beings experience well-being, health, good rain, fair grain prices, great wealth, and the gain of friends. ॥6॥

(5) In the year named **Phalguna**, there is auspiciousness in some places and crops increase. However, women face misfortune, thieves become powerful, and kings—

When **Jupiter** (Brihaspati) moves to the north of all the lunar mansions (*Nakshatras*), there is health, good rain, and auspiciousness for all. If Jupiter is in the southern direction, the results are the opposite of those mentioned; if he wanders in the middle portion, the results are mediocre. ||15|| If Jupiter traverses between two Nakshatras in one year, it is auspicious; if he traverses two and a half Nakshatras, the result is mediocre; and if he ever traverses more Nakshatras than that in a <term>Samvatsara</term> <note>a full Jovian year</note>, the grain is destroyed. ||16||

If the color of Jupiter is like fire, there is fear of fire; if yellow, disease; if dark/black, there will be war; if green, there will be suffering caused by thieves; if red, fear of weapons; and if smoke-colored, there is drought. If Jupiter is visible during the day, it brings destruction to men; if he appears large and clear like a beautiful star at night, the subjects find happiness. ||17||18||

The Nakshatras **Krittika** and **Rohini** are the "body" of the year; **Purvashadha** and **Uttarashadha** are the "navel"; **Ashlesha** is the "heart," and **Magha** is the "flower" of the year. If these are pure, the results are auspicious. During Jupiter's transit, if the "body" Nakshatra is afflicted by malefic planets, there is fear from fire and wind. If the "navel" Nakshatra is afflicted, there is fear of hunger. In the Nakshatra **Pushya**, roots (such as radish) and fruits perish. If the "heart" Nakshatra is afflicted by malefic planets, the destruction of grain is certain. ||19||

It must be explained that if the result is 25, it is the Purva Bhadrapada Nakshatra; if 2, it is the 26th, Uttara Bhadrapada, and so on. ||22|| In the sixty-year cycle starting from *Prabhava*, there are a total of 12 *Yugas* <note>Eras or cycles</note>; each *Yuga* consists of five years. The presiding deities of these twelve *Yugas* are, in order: 1. Vishnu, 2. Surejya <note>Jupiter/Brihaspati</note>, 3. Balabhit <note>Indra</note>, 4. Agni, 5. Twashta, 6. Ahirbudhnya <note>original: Uttaraprosthapada</note>, 7. Pitris, 8. Vishwadevas, 9. Soma, 10. Indragni <note>original: Shakranal</note>, 11. Ashvins, and 12. Bhaga. Samvatsara, 2. Parivatsara, 3. Idavatsara, 4. Anuvatsara, 5. Idvatsara. The presiding deities are: 1. Agni, 2. Surya, 3. Chandra, 4. Prajapati, 5. Mahadeva ||24|| Regarding the rainfall in these five years: in the first year (*Samvatsara*), there is moderate rain; in the second, rain occurs at the beginning of the season; in the third, there is excessive rain; in the fourth, rain occurs at the end of the season; and in the fifth year, there is ordinary rainfall. ||25|| Among the twelve *Yugas* previously described, the first four—presided over by Vishnu, Indra, Brihaspati, and Agni—are considered the best. The middle four are mediocre, and the final four should be known to yield moderate to poor results. ||26|| When Jupiter (*Brihaspati*) enters the first part of the Dhanishta Nakshatra and rises in the month of Magha <note>January/February</note>, the first year of the sixty-year cycle, named *Prabhava*, begins. This year is beneficial for all living beings. ||27|| During the year *Prabhava*, even if there is a lack of rain in some places, or the wrath of wind and fire in others, or fear of pests <term>Iti-bhaya: six calamities including locusts, rats, and foreign invasion</term> or suffering from phlegmatic diseases in some regions, nevertheless, living beings do not experience significant distress in this year. ||28|| The second year is named *Vibhava*, the third is *Shukla*, the fourth is *Pramoda*, and the fifth year is named *Prajapati*. All these years provide progressively auspicious results. In these years, kings protect the earth in such a way that, by the virtue of their rule, the earth abounds in grain, sugarcane, barley, and other crops; it becomes free from fear and enmity, and filled with joyful people, it is liberated from the vices of the *Kali Yuga*. ||29||30|| In the second *Yuga* (the *Yuga* of Brihaspati), the five years are named: Angira, Shrimukha, Bhava, Yuva, and Dhata. Among these, the first three years are quite good, and the latter two are average. ||31|| In the three years starting with Angira, the gods grant plentiful rain and people are free from terror and fear. In the last two years, although agriculture remains average, diseases and conflicts occur. ||32|| By the movement of Jupiter—

The third Yuga, named **Aindra** <note>dedicated to Indra, the king of gods</note>, has as its first year 1. <term>Ishvara</term> (The Lord), 2. <term>Bahudhana</term> (Abundant Wealth), 3. <term>Pramathi</term> (The Tormentor), 4. <term>Vikrama</term> (Valor), and the fifth is named <term>Vrisha</term> (The Bull) ||33|| In this group, the first and second years bring good fortune; indeed, for the subjects, it is as if the Golden Age <note>Satya Yuga</note> has returned. The year <term>Pramathi</term> is extremely sinful and harmful. The two years named <term>Vikrama</term> and <term>Vrisha</term> bring good harvests, but they also cause disease and fear ||34||

The first year of the fourth Yuga (named **Hutasha** <note>dedicated to Agni, the god of fire</note>), which is called <term>Chitrabhanu</term> (Bright Sun), gives excellent results. The second year, <term>Subhanu</term> (Radiant Sun), has moderate results, meaning it brings illness but is not fatal. The fifth year is named <term>Tarana</term> (The Savior) (according to some opinions, <term>Daruna</term> or "Harsh"); in this year, there is excessive rain. The fourth year is named <term>Parthiva</term> (Earthly); in this year, there is joy due to the increase of grain. The fifth year is named <term>Vyaya</term> (Expenditure/Loss); in this year, passion is ignited in living beings, and they appear splendid and full of festivities ||35|| ||36||

In the fifth Yuga named **Tvashtra** <note>dedicated to Vishwakarma, the divine architect</note>, the names of the years are 1. <term>Sarvajit</term> (All-Conquering), 2. <term>Sarvadhari</term> (All-Supporting), 3. <term>Virodhi</term> (Opposing), 4. <term>Vikrita</term> (Deformed), and 5. <term>Khara</term> (Harsh). Among these five years, the second year is auspicious, and the rest are causes of fear ||37||

In the sixth Yuga named **Prosthapada**, the first year is named <term>Nandana</term> (Joyful), 2. <term>Vijaya</term> (Victory), 3. <term>Jaya</term> (Conquest), 4. <term>Manmatha</term> (Love/Cupid), and the fifth is <term>Durmukha</term> (Ugly-faced). Among these five years, the first three are pleasant; the <term>Manmatha</term> year has neutral results, and the fifth year is extremely wretched ||38||

By the influence of Jupiter's movement, the seventh (**Pitri**) Yuga <note>dedicated to the Ancestors</note> consists of 1. <term>Hemalamba</term> (Golden-Pendant), 2. <term>Vilambi</term> (Tardy), 3. <term>Vikari</term> (Changeable/Sickly), 4. <term>Sharvari</term> (The Night), and 5. <term>Plava</term> (The Boat/Flood). In its first year, there is fear of natural calamities <note>iti-bhaya: refers to the six traditional plagues: drought, flood, locusts, rats, birds, and foreign invasion</note> and fear of storms; rain falls along with the storms. Subsequently, in the second year, there is a scarcity of grain and rain. In the third year, there is great anxiety and excessive rain. In the fourth year, there is fear of famine, and in the <term>Plava</term> year, there is excellent rain and prosperity ||39|| ||40||

In the **Vaishva** Yuga <note>dedicated to the Vishvadevas</note>, the first year is named <term>Kshobhakrit</term> (Agitator), 2. <term>Shubhakrit</term> (Doer of Good), 3. <term>Krodhi</term> (Angry), 4. <term>Vishvavasu</term> (Wealth of the Universe), and 5. <term>Parabhava</term> (Defeat). Its first and second years please the subjects. The third year brings many faults, and the remaining two years have neutral results; however, in the <term>Parabhava</term> year, there is suffering from fire, weapons, and disease, as well as distress to cows and Brahmins ||41|| 42||

In the ninth (**Saumya**) Yuga <note>dedicated to the Moon or Mercury</note>, the first year is named <term>Plavanga</term> (Leaping/Monkey), 2. <term>Kilaka</term> (The Bolt), 3. <term>Saumya</term> (Gentle), 4. <term>Sadharana</term> (Ordinary), and the fifth is <term>Rodhakrit</term> (Obstructor). In the <term>Sadharana</term> year, there is ordinary rain and fear of calamities. And in the fifth year, named <term>Rodhakrit</term>, there is beautiful rain and wealth of grain ||44||

In the tenth Yuga, whose deity is **Shakragni** <note>Indra and Agni combined</note>, the first year is named <term>Paridhavi</term> (Running Around), the second <term>Pramadi</term> (Careless), 3. <term>Ananda</term> (Joy), 4. <term>Rakshasa</term> (Demon), and 5. <term>Anala</term> (Fire). Among these, in the year named <term>Paridhavi</term>, there is the destruction of the Middle Country <note>Madhyadesha: the central region of ancient India</note>, loss of the king, ordinary rain, and fear of fire. In the <term>Pramadi</term> year, people become extremely lazy; there is upheaval, and the seeds of red-colored flowers are destroyed. The <term>Ananda</term> year brings joy, and in the <term>Rakshasa</term> or <term>Anala</term> years, there is decay/destruction. However, the distinction is that in the <term>Rakshasa</term> year, summer crops are produced, while the <term>Anala</term> year brings the wrath of fire and hellish suffering ||45|| 46|| 47||

In the eleventh (**Ashvi**) Yuga <note>dedicated to the Ashvins, the divine physicians</note>, there are five years: 1. <term>Pingala</term> (Tawny), 2. <term>Kalayukta</term> (Time-linked), 3. <term>Siddhartha</term> (Accomplished), 4. <term>Raudra</term> (Terrible), and 5. <term>Durmati</term> (Evil-minded). ### Now Begins the Ninth Chapter
->The Course of Venus<-

The paths <term>Vithis</term> are named Naga, Gaja, Airavata, Vrisha, Go, Jaradgava, Mriga, Aja, and Dahana. Some say these paths are formed by groups of three constellations <term>Nakshatras</term> starting from Ashvini. ॥1॥ The **Naga** path consists of the constellations Swati, Bharani, and Krittika. The **Gaja** path consists of Rohini, Mrigashira, and Ardra. The **Airavata** path consists of Punarvasu, Pushya, and Ashlesha. The **Go** path consists of Magha, Purva Phalguni, and Uttara Phalguni. The **Jaradgava** path consists of Hasta, Chitra, and Swati <note>Note: different systems of grouping are being compared here</note>. ॥2-3॥ These paths are situated in the Northern, Middle, and Southern routes respectively. ॥4॥ Others describe the paths of the stars based on their positions relative to the celestial equator. ॥5॥ The Northern route is said to begin with the Southern constellations, the Middle route begins with the auspicious ones, and the Southern route begins with Ashadha; thus have some arranged the routes. ॥6॥ Astrology is a traditional science <term>Agama Shastra</term>; it is not proper for us to create our own alternatives when there is a disagreement, but I shall state the opinions of the many. ॥7॥ When Venus <term>Shukra</term> sets or rises in the **Northern paths**, it brings good food and well-being; in the **Middle paths**, it gives middling results; and in the **Southern paths**, it brings distress. ॥8॥ One should declare the results as: most excellent, excellent, slightly less, even, middling, below middling, and distressing, according to the paths starting from the Northern one. ॥9॥ The first circle <term>Mandala</term> begins with Bharani and contains four constellations; it brings good food but creates fear in the lands of Vanga, Anga, Mahisha, Bahlika, and Kalinga. ॥10॥ If another planet should overtake Venus here, it destroys the kings of Bhadrashva, Shurasena, Yaudheya, and Kotivarsha. ॥11॥ The second circle of four constellations begins with Ardra; it is for the prosperity of water and crops, but it is inauspicious for priests, especially those of cruel deeds. ॥12॥ If Venus is attacked here by another planet, fire touches the Mlechhas <term>foreigners/outsiders</term>, forest-dwellers, those who live with dogs, the Gomantas, the Gonardas, the Shudras, and the people of Videha. ॥13॥ Moving through the five constellations starting with Magha, Venus causes the destruction of crops, hunger, and fear of thieves, and causes the rise of the low and the mixing of classes. ॥14॥ If Venus is obstructed in the constellation of the Manes <term>Magha</term>, it destroys sailors and hunters...

If Venus occupies this area, there is death for the king of the Kiratas <note>mountain tribes</note>, and it crushes the Ikshvakus, the border-dwellers, and the armies of Avanti, Pulinda, Vanga, and Anga. **||17||**

The fifth circle, beginning with **Jyeshtha**, consists of five asterisms. It brings hunger, thieves, and disease. It afflicts Kashmir, Ashmaka, Matsya, and the city of Avanti along with its queen Charudevi. **||18||**

As it rises here, it destroys the Abhiras, Dravidas, Ambasthas, Trigartas, and Saurashtras. It also brings about the destruction of the people of Sindhu-Sauvira and the death of the King of Kashi <note>modern-day Varanasi</note>. **||19||**

The sixth circle, beginning with **Dhanishtha**, consists of six asterisms and is auspicious. The earth becomes crowded with great wealth and herds of cattle, and there is no lack of grain, though fear arises in some places. **||20||**

When Venus rises here, the Shulikas, Gandharas, and Avantis are oppressed. There is the death of the King of Videha, but an increase in the prosperity of the border-dwelling Yavanas <note>Greeks or foreigners</note>, Shakas <note>Scythians</note>, and servants. **||21||**

In the western sky, the circles beginning with **Swati** and **Jyeshtha** are auspicious. In the eastern sky, the circle beginning with **Magha** <note>original: "Pitri-adya", referring to the ancestors who rule Magha</note> is auspicious. The rest yield results as previously stated. **||22||**

If Venus is seen at sunset, it creates fear and minor diseases throughout the day. If seen at midday along with the Moon, it causes the destruction of kings, their armies, and their cities. **||23||**

If Venus passes through and "breaks" the asterism of Fire <note>original: "Anala-ksha", referring to Krittika</note>, the earth becomes covered by rivers overflowing their banks with muddy water. **||24||**

If the "Wagon of Rohini" <note>original: "Prajapatya-shakata"</note> is broken by Venus, the earth—as if having committed a great sin—takes on the "Skull-Bearing Vow" <note>Kapala-vrata; a penance involving carrying a skull</note>, becoming covered in hair and fragments of bone. **||25||**

When Venus reaches **Mrigashira** <note>original: "Saumya"</note>, it is said to destroy liquids and crops. Reaching **Ardra**, it destroys the people of Kosala and Kalinga but brings a great abundance of water <note>rain</note>. **||26||**

When Venus stays in **Punarvasu**, there is great misfortune for the Ashmakas and Vidarbhas. In **Pushya**, there is abundant rain but conflict among the Vidyadharas <note>celestial musicians/beings</note>. **||27||**

In **Ashlesha**, Venus brings terrible suffering from snakes. Breaking through **Magha**, it causes trouble for high ministers <note>Mahamatras</note> but brings heavy rain. **||28||**

In **Purva Phalguni** <note>original: "Bhagya"</note>, it destroys the Shabaras and Pulindas and releases a flood of water. In **Uttara Phalguni** <note>original: "Aryamna"</note>, it destroys the Kurujangala and Panchala regions but provides water. **||29||**

In **Hasta**, there is suffering for the Kurus and painters, and the rain is withheld. In **Chitra**, there is suffering for those who dig wells and for birds, but the rain is beautiful. **||30||**

In **Swati**, there is much rain, but misfortune touches the merchants. In **Vishakha** <note>original: "Aindragni"</note>, there is good rain, but one should know there is fear for traders. **||31||**

In **Anuradha** <note>original: "Mitra"</note>, there is conflict among the Kshatriyas. In **Jyeshtha**, there is distress for the chiefs of the Kshatriyas. In **Mula**, there is distress for root-sellers and physicians. In all three of these, there is a lack of rain. **||32||**

In **Purvashadha** <note>original: "Apya"</note>, there is suffering for aquatic creatures. In **Uttarashadha** <note>original: "Vishvesha"</note>, diseases break out. In **Shravana**, there are ear diseases. In **Dhanishtha**, there is fear of heretics <note>Pashandas</note>. **||33||**

In **Shatabhishak**, there is trouble for distillers. In **Purva Bhadrapada** <note>original: "Ajaikapada"</note>, there is trouble for gamblers and the Kuru-Panchalas, yet Venus still brings water. **||34||**

In **Uttara Bhadrapada** <note>original: "Ahirbudhnya"</note>, it causes heat/distress for fruits and roots. In **Revati**, for travelers. In **Ashwini**, for horses and their keepers. In **Bharani** <note>original: "Yamya"</note>, for the Kiratas and Yavanas. **||35||**

When the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> rises or sets on the 14th, 15th, or 8th lunar day of the dark fortnight, the earth appears as if made of water <note>due to heavy rain</note>. **||36||**

When Jupiter and Venus are in the seventh sign from each other in the East and West, the people are afflicted by disease, fear, and sorrow, and they do not see rain released by Indra. **||37||**

When Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and the Sun all follow the path of Venus, there are battles between men, Nagas <note>serpent beings</note>, and Vidyadharas, and great winds arise...

### The Compendium of Varahamihira

...the threads are destroyed. **(38)** Friends do not remain established in their friendly nature; the twice-born <note>The "twice-born" or *Dvija* refers to the upper three social classes—Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas—who undergo a spiritual initiation.</note> do not properly engage in their rituals; Indra <note>The King of Gods and bringer of rain.</note> does not grant even a little water, and he breaks the heads of kings with his thunderbolt. **(39)** When Saturn is the influencer, the foreigners <note>original: "Mleccha"</note>, cats, elephants, donkeys, buffaloes, dark grains, and pigs perish. The Pulindas <note>A forest-dwelling tribe.</note>, the Shudras, and the inhabitants of the southern regions perish due to diseases of the eyes and wind. **(40)** If Venus is situated in front of Mars, the subjects are destroyed by fire, weapons, hunger, lack of rain, and thieves; the moving and stationary world is clearly distressed, and the directions are afflicted by fire, lightning, and dust. **(41)** When Venus is situated in front of Jupiter, it destroys everything white, as well as the twice-born, cows, and temples. In the eastern direction, clouds pour down hail, and there is an abundance of throat diseases during the autumn. **(42)** When Mercury is in front of Venus at its rising or setting, it causes frequent diseases, bile-related ailments, and jaundice, yet it nourishes the summer crops. It destroys ascetics, those who maintain the sacred fire, physicians, those who live by the Vedas, horses, the merchant class, cows along with their vehicles, kings, and the yellow-colored things in the western direction. **(43)** If Venus appears like fire, there is fear of fire; if red, there is the fury of weapons; if pale yellow like the touchstone of gold, there are diseases. If it appears green or tawny, there is an outbreak of cough and asthma; if it appears rough and like the color of ash, no water falls from the sky. **(44)** But when Venus possesses the luster of curd, the white lily, or the moon, with clearly blooming rays and a large body, moving gracefully and without distortion, it is victorious and brings about the conditions of the Golden Age <note>original: "Krita Yuga," the age of truth and perfection.</note>. **(45)**

->**Thus ends the Ninth Chapter, titled "The Course of Venus," in the Brihat Samhita composed by Sri Varahamihira.**<-

Some scholars say that every three constellations <note>original: "Nakshatras"</note> starting from Ashwini form one "Path" <note>original: "Vithi" - a technical term for the celestial lanes or orbits of planets.</note>. This Path is divided into nine parts, namely: 1. Serpent (Naga), 2. Elephant (Gaja), 3. Airavata (the celestial elephant), 4. Bull (Vrishabha), 5. Cow (Gau), 6. Old Bull (Jaradgava), 7. Deer (Mriga), 8. Goat (Aja), and 9. Fire (Dahana). **(1)** According to some opinions, the Serpent Path consists of the constellations Svati, Bharani, and Krittika. The three paths named Elephant, Airavata, and Bull occur in groups of three constellations each from Rohini to Uttara Phalguni. The Cow Path occurs in the constellations Ashwini, Revati, Purva Bhadrapada, and Uttara Bhadrapada. **(2)** The Old Bull Path is in Shravana, Dhanishta, and Shatabhisha; the Deer Path is in Anuradha, Jyeshtha, and Mula; the Goat Path is in Hasta, Vishakha, and Chitra; and the Fire Path occurs in Purva Ashadha and Uttara Ashadha. **(3)** In this way, with nine paths across twenty-seven constellations, each path occurs three times; therefore, among all these paths, three paths each are situated in the Northern, Middle, and Southern routes of the Sun. Furthermore, each of them is situated respectively in the Northern, Middle, and Southern tracks—for example, there are three Serpent Paths, of which one is in the Northern route, the second in the Middle, and the third in the Southern route. **(4)** Some great souls say that just as the junction stars <note>original: "Yoga Tara" - the principal star of a constellation.</note> of all constellations are situated in the Northern, Middle, and Southern parts, all the Path routes are situated in the same way. **(5)** According to the opinion of some scholars, the Northern route begins from Bharani, the Middle route from Purva Phalguni, and the Southern from Purva Ashadha...

# Chapter 9 with Hindi Commentary

(57)

The beginning of the Southern Path occurs. ||6|| The science of Astrology <note>original: "Jyotish"</note> and the scriptures of tradition—that is, to investigate a matter with skepticism—is beyond my (a man like me) capability; for this reason (without blaming the opinion of any among the sages or supporting only one), I shall present the opinions of many. ||7|| At the time when **Shukracharya** <note>The planet Venus, personified as the preceptor of the demons</note> is situated in the Northern Path <note>vithi</note> and rises or sets, only then will there be good harvests <note>subhiksha</note> or auspiciousness. Being in the Middle Path results in moderate fruits, and being in the Southern Path results in distressing outcomes. ||8|| Starting from the **Ardra** lunar mansion <note>nakshatra</note> up to **Mrigashira**, there are nine paths; the rising or setting of Venus in these produces, in order: excellent, good, slightly less, even, moderate, low, base, distressing, and most distressing results. ||9|| In the circle or path consisting of the four lunar mansions starting from **Bharani**, if Venus rises or sets in the first path, there is a good harvest; however, there is fear in the regions of **Anga, Vanga, Mahisha, Bahlika,** and **Kalinga**. ||10|| If any planet moves over **Shukracharya** while he is risen in this first circle, the kings of **Bhadrashva, Shurasenaka, Yaudheyaka,** and **Kotivarsha** are destroyed. ||11|| The four lunar mansions starting from **Ardra** are called the second circle. (By the rising or setting of Venus in these) much rain falls and it is a cause for wealth in grain. However, it is inauspicious for **Brahmins**; specifically, those of cruel conduct suffer great loss. ||12|| If any planet attacks Venus while in the second circle, then injustice touches the **Mlechhas** <note>foreigners or non-Aryans</note>, forest-dwellers, those who live by horses (nomads/traders), the **Gomanta** (those who live by dogs), low-caste **Shudras** who keep many cows, and the inhabitants of the **Videha** region. ||13|| If the Preceptor of the Demons <note>Venus</note> rises while wandering through the five lunar mansions from **Magha** to **Chitra**, all grain is destroyed. There is fear of hunger and fear of thieves. There is the rise of the lowly and the birth of mixed-caste <note>varna-sankar</note> populations. ||14|| If the Preceptor of the Demons in this third circle (Magha etc.) is obstructed by any other planet, then groups of trees, the **Shabara** people, **Shudras, Pundra**, the weaponry of the western border, the **Shulika**, forest-dwellers, **Dravidians**, and the men of the sea are destroyed. ||15|| The fourth circle consists of the **Swati, Vishakha,** and **Anuradha** lunar mansions. By the transit of **Shukracharya** in these, there is freedom from fear; there is a good harvest for the **Brahmin** and **Kshatriya** castes, but mutual division arises among friends. ||16|| If this fourth circle is attacked, the **Kirata** king dies, and those of the **Ikshvaku** lineage, those living in the borderlands or the **Avanti** region, the **Pulinda, Tangana,** and the inhabitants of **Shurasena** are nourished. ||17|| The five lunar mansions from **Jyeshtha** to **Shravana** constitute the fifth circle; in this, there are obstacles of hunger, thieves, and disease. If the Son of **Bhrigu** <note>Venus</note> ascends in this, the men living in **Kashmir, Ashmaka, Matsya, Charudevi,** and **Avanti**, the **Abhira** tribe, **Dravidians, Ambashtha, Trigarta, Saurashtra, Sindhu,** and **Sauvira**, and the King of **Kashmir** are destroyed. ||18||19|| The six lunar mansions from **Dhanishtha** to **Ashwini** are called the sixth circle; these are auspicious. In this, all people become extremely happy, endowed with much wealth, grain, and cattle; however, some places remain fearful. Upon the ascension of Venus in this, the people living in **Shulika, Gandhara,** and **Avanti** are afflicted; the King of **Videha** is destroyed, and the **Yavanas** <note>Greeks or Westerners</note>, **Shakas** <note>Scythians</note>, and servants of the borderlands increase. ||20||21|| Among the six circles described, the two circles starting with the **Swati** lunar mansion and the **Jyeshtha** lunar mansion—these two circles...

# The Varahi Samhita
<note>The Varahi Samhita, also known as the Brihat Samhita, is a 6th-century Sanskrit encyclopedic work by Varahamihira covering astrology, planetary movements, and omens.</note>

If they occur in the western direction, they are auspicious; the circle beginning with the Magha constellation <note>Magha is the 10th lunar mansion, associated with ancestral spirits</note> is extremely auspicious if it occurs in the eastern direction. The remaining circles provide results as previously stated. ||22||

If Venus is sighted before sunset, there is fear; if it is visible throughout the entire day, hunger and disease occur. If it is visible at midday or seen alongside the Moon, it causes discord among kings, the army, and the city. ||23||

If the Preceptor Venus <note>original: "Shukracharya"</note> travels by piercing the Krittika constellation <note>The Pleiades</note>, the high and low places of the earth become indistinguishable and leveled by rivers carrying vast masses of water that overflow their banks; that is to say, a very great flood occurs. ||24||

If the Rohini constellation or its "Cart"¹ <note>The "Cart of Rohini" is a specific V-shaped star configuration in Taurus</note> is pierced by Venus (just as sinful people observe the *Kapalika* vow to atone for their sins), then the earth, covered in various colors from hair and fragments of bones, appears as if it is observing the skull-carrying vow after committing a sin; that is, there is a massive mortality rate. ||25||

If it enters the Mrigashira constellation, there is destruction of water and grain. If it travels in the Ardra constellation, the regions of Kaushal and Kalinga are destroyed, though there is much rain. ||26||

Upon the Preceptor Venus entering the Punarvasu constellation, extreme lawlessness comes upon the people living in the Ashmaka and Vidarbha regions. Upon entering the Pushya constellation, there is abundant rain, but there is constant conflict among the *Vidyadharas* <note>A class of celestial beings or supernatural scholars</note>. ||27||

By the sun-like Venus entering the Ashlesha constellation, there is fear of serpents and extreme suffering. Upon piercing the Magha constellation, it causes trouble for elephant-keepers <term>Hastipaka: professional elephant trainers or riders</term> and there is extreme rain. ||28||

If the Purva Phalguni constellation is pierced by Venus, the Shabar and Pulinda tribes meet their destruction, and there is much rain. If Uttara Phalguni is pierced, there is rain, and the regions of Kurujangala and Panchala are destroyed. ||29||

If the Hasta constellation is pierced by Venus, the Kauravas and painters suffer, and it does not rain. If the Chitra constellation is pierced by Venus, well-diggers and egg-born creatures <note>birds and reptiles</note> suffer; the rain is sporadic but beautiful. ||30||

If Venus enters the Swati constellation, there is rain, and extreme lawlessness touches messengers, merchants, and sailors. If Venus is in Vishakha, there is good rain and fear for traders. ||31||

In Anuradha, there is the slaughter of warriors <term>Kshatriyas: the ruling and military caste</term>; in Jyeshtha, distress for the chief warriors; in Mula, suffering for the chief physicians. For as many days as Venus remains in these three constellations, there is a drought. ||32||

If Venus travels in the Purva Ashadha constellation, creatures born of water suffer. In Uttara Ashadha, there is disease; in Shravana, ear ailments; and in Dhanishtha, there is fear for heretics <term>Pakhandi: those who follow non-Vedic or unorthodox paths</term>. ||33||

If Venus travels in the Shatabhisha constellation, distillers <note>original: "Kalwar"</note> suffer. In Purva Bhadrapada, gamblers and the people of Kuru-Panchala suffer, and there is rain. ||34||

In Uttara Bhadrapada, fruits and roots are affected; in Revati, infantrymen; in Ashwini, horse-keepers; and in Bharani, the Kirata and Yavana <note>Yavana: historically referring to Greeks or foreigners from the West</note> people suffer distress. ||35||

If the rising or setting of Venus occurs on the fourteenth, fifteenth, or eighth day of the dark fortnight, much water rains upon the earth. ||36||

If Jupiter and Venus move in opposition to each other in the seventh house (East and West), the subjects suffer greatly from disease and fear, and it does not rain. ||37||

# Chapter 10: The Movement of Saturn
## Hindi Commentary, Page 59

If Saturn and other planets move in the path ahead of Venus, there is war among humans, <term>Nagas</term><note>Serpent-beings or semi-divine entities</note>, and <term>Vidyadharas</term><note>Celestial beings possessing magical knowledge</note>. Destruction is caused by storms, kinsmen lose their mutual affection, and the <term>twice-born</term><note>The upper three castes: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas</note> abandon their religious duties. Even the common rains of Indra do not fall; instead, thunderbolts strike and shatter the peaks of mountains. **[38-39]**

When Saturn specifically moves ahead of Venus, the <term>Mlechha</term><note>Foreigners or non-Vedic peoples</note> tribes, the cat-like races, elephants, donkeys, buffaloes, black grains, pigs, the <term>Pulinda</term><note>A specific forest-dwelling tribe</note> tribe, the <term>Shudras</term><note>The laboring class</note>, and the southern regions are destroyed by diseases of the eyes and wind. **[40]**

If Mars travels ahead of Venus, all subjects suffer from fire, weapons, hunger, drought, and thieves; the northern direction is destroyed, and all directions are afflicted by fire, lightning, and dust. **[41]**

Should Jupiter travel in the path ahead of Venus, then all sweet substances, Brahmins, cattle, temples, and the eastern direction are destroyed. Clouds rain hailstones, everyone suffers from throat ailments, but all autumn crops flourish. **[42]**

When Mercury is in the path ahead of Venus during its rising or setting, there are rains and diseases, particularly those arising from bile and jaundice. All goods produced in the summer season are produced in abundance. However, ascetics, those who maintain the sacred fire, physicians, those who live by dancing, horses, the <term>Vaishyas</term><note>The merchant and farming class</note>, cows, kings with their vehicles, yellow-colored objects, and the western direction are destroyed. **[43]**

When the color of Venus is like fire, there is fear of fire; if it is blood-red, there is the fury of weapons; if it is pale-gold like a line of gold rubbed on a touchstone, there is disease. If Venus appears green or tawny, there is suffering from asthma and cough; and if it is dry like ash or black in color, there is no rain from the sky. **[44]**

When the preceptor of the demons, <term>Shukracharya</term><note>Venus personified</note>, is as bright as curd, the white water-lily, or the moon—shining clearly with spreading rays, moving in an excellent path, free from defects, and victorious—it is as if the <term>Satya Yuga</term><note>The Golden Age of truth and righteousness</note> has arrived for all living beings. **[45]**

->Thus ends the ninth chapter in the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western province, on the *Brihat Samhita* composed by the Great Acharya Varahamihira. <-

# The Compendium of Varāha
## Chapter 10: The Course of Saturn

...[those who deal in] pots, Greeks, merchants, gamblers, and flowers. **(6)** When in *Aśleṣā* <note>The Serpent star</note>, aquatic creatures and serpents are afflicted; in *Maghā* <note>The Ancestor star</note>, the people of Bahlika, China, and Gandhara <note>Modern-day regions of Bactria, China, and Afghanistan</note>, as well as the Shulikas, Paratas, the merchant caste, granaries, and traders. **(7)** In *Pūrvaphalgunī*, sellers of liquids, prostitutes, young maidens, and the people of Maharashtra are affected; in *Uttaraphalgunī*, kings, molasses, merchants, sugarcane, water, and the people of Takshashila. **(8)** In *Hasta*, barbers, oil-millers, thieves, physicians, informants, elephant-catchers, harlots, the people of Koshala, and garland-makers suffer. **(9)** When Saturn stays in *Citra*, women, writers, painters, and decorated vessels are impacted; in *Svāti*, the people of Magadha, spies, messengers, charioteers, sailors, and actors. **(10)** In the mansion called *Viśākhā*, the people of Trigarta, China, and Kuluta, as well as saffron, lac, crops, madder, and safflower perish. **(11)** In *Anurādhā*, the people of Kuluta, Tangana, Khasa, and Kashmir, along with ministers and those who travel in circles <note>likely wandering performers or secret agents</note>, suffer distress, as do bell-ringers and there is a breaking of friendships. **(12)** In *Jyeṣṭhā*, kings, royal priests, those honored by kings, heroes, noble families, and guilds are affected; in *Mūla*, the people of Kashi, Koshala, and Panchala, as well as fruits, medicinal herbs, and soldiers. **(13)** In *Pūrvāṣāḍhā*, the people of Anga, Vanga, Koshala, Girivraja, Magadha, Pundra, and Mithila suffer, as do those living in Tamralipti. **(14)** In *Uttarāṣāḍhā*, the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> traveling there destroys the Dasharnas, Greeks, Ujjain, the Shavaras, the Pariyatrikas, and the Kuntibhojas. **(15)** In *Śravaṇa*, royal officials, eminent Brahmins, physicians, priests, and the people of Kalinga suffer; in *Dhaniṣṭhā*, there is victory for the Lord of Magadha and an increase in wealth for the unrefined. **(16)** In *Śatabhiṣaj*, physicians, poets, vintners, and those involved in trade and politics suffer; in *Pūrvabhādrapadā*, actors, vehicle-makers, women, and gold. **(17)** In *Revatī*, royal servants, those living on the Krauncha islands, autumn crops, Shavaras, and Greeks are oppressed while Saturn moves there. **(18)** When the Minister of Indra <note>Jupiter</note> is in *Viśākhā* and the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> enters the mansion of Fire <note>Kṛttikā</note>, then a terrible calamity befalls the subjects and cities are destroyed. **(19)** If the Son of the Sun appears variegated like a bird, he causes fear of hunger; if his rays are yellow, he causes fear of weapons; if he is blood-red, he causes fear of war; and if he is ash-colored, he creates much enmity. **(20)** If he is clear with the luster of a lapis lazuli, he brings prosperity to the subjects; if he has the color of a Baṇa or Atasi flower <note>blue-hued flowers</note>, he is considered auspicious. The sage's tradition says that the Son of the Sun destroys those things whose color he assumes among the five colors. **(21)**

->Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Course of Saturn," in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā composed by Sri Varāhamihira. <-

If Saturn, the son of the Sun, resides in the constellations of *Śravaṇa, Svāti, Hasta, Ārdrā, Bharaṇī*, or *Pūrvaphalgunī* and possesses a beautiful color, then it rains heavily upon the earth. **(1)** If Saturn wanders in *Aśleṣā, Śatabhiṣaj*, or *Jyeṣṭhā*, it is auspicious, but there is no excessive rain. If he wanders in *Mūla*, there is hunger, fear of weapons, and drought. This is the general result. Now, the specific results of Saturn's transit through each constellation are stated. **(2)** If Saturn wanders in *Aśvinī*, horses, horse-riders, poets, physicians, and ministers suffer loss. If he wanders in *Bharaṇī*, dancers, instrumentalists, singers, and those who earn a living by small boats suffer loss. **(3)** If Saturn is in *Kṛttikā*, those who live by fire <note>blacksmiths, etc.</note> and kings are troubled. If Saturn resides in *Rohiṇī*, the regions of Koshala, Madra, Kashi, and Panchala...

# Now begins the Eleventh Chapter
## The Course of Ketus (Comets)

Having observed the works of Garga on the "Course of the Crested Ones" <note>original: "Shikhichara," referring to comets</note>, as well as the works of Parashara, Asita, and Devala, and many others, this "Incomprehensible Course" is being composed. ||1|| Their rising or setting cannot be known through mathematical calculation alone, because Ketus <note>In Indian astronomy, 'Ketu' refers to comets, meteors, and eclipses; here specifically comets</note> are of three types: Celestial, Atmospheric, and Terrestrial. ||2|| A form that appears like fire but is not caused by fuel is called a Ketu-form; this excludes fireflies, the glow of a ghost's abode <note>likely referring to phosphorescence or "will-o'-the-wisp"</note>, and the luster of swords or gems. ||3|| Those appearing on banners, weapons, houses, trees, horses, or elephants are Atmospheric; those appearing in the Celestial constellations are Divine; and others are Terrestrial "Crested Ones." ||4|| Some say there are one hundred and one Ketus, others say a thousand; but the Sage Narada has stated that there is only one Ketu which appears in many forms. ||5|| Whether there be one or many, the results must certainly be told based on their rising, setting, position, contact <note>conjunction with stars</note>, smokiness, and color. ||6|| For as many days as a Ketu is visible, for that many months will its effects ripen. One should predict the results in years if the visibility lasts beyond the first three fortnights. ||7|| A Ketu that is short, thin, clear, glossy, straight, well-situated, white, and seen at its rising brings abundance and happiness. ||8|| A "Smoke-Ketu" <note>Dhumaketu</note> that possesses the opposite characteristics is not auspicious, especially if it mimics the shape of a rainbow or has two or three crests (tails). ||9|| There are twenty-five Ketus called "The Rayed Ones" <note>Kirana</note>, appearing like necklaces, gems, or gold, and possessing crests. Born of the Sun <note>Ravija</note>, they are visible in the East and West and bring conflict between kings. ||10|| Those appearing like parrots, fire, Bandhujiva flowers, or lac, resembling blood, are the "Sons of Fire" <note>Hutashasuta</note>. They are seen in the South-East and bring danger from fire. ||11|| Those with curved crests, rough and black, are the "Sons of Death" <note>Mrityusuta</note>; they are also twenty-five in number. Seen in the Southern direction, they announce pestilence and death among the people. ||12|| Those shaped like a round mirror, without a crest but possessing rays, are the "Sons of the Earth" <note>Dharatanaya</note>. There are twenty-two of them, appearing in the North-East with the luster of water or oil; they bring famine. ||13|| Those resembling moonbeams, silver, snow, white lilies, or Kunda flowers are the "Sons of the Moon" <note>Shashisuta</note>. Three such "Crested Ones" appear in the North and bring about abundance. ||14|| There is one "Son of Brahma" <note>Brahmasuta</note> with three crests and three colors, which brings the end of an era <note>Yuganta</note>. It appears in no fixed direction and is known as the "Staff of Brahma" <note>Brahmadanda</note>. ||15|| Thus one hundred and one have been described. Now, I shall describe the nine hundred Ketus with their distinct characteristics. ||16|| The "Sons of Venus" <note>Shukrasuta</note> rise in the North and North-East...

# Chapter 11: On Comets (Continued)

There are eighty-four comets known as the **Kanaka** <note>literally "Golden"</note> comets. They possess large, dark pupils, appear glossy, and bring about intense results. (17)

Sixty comets, born from Saturn, are glossy, radiant, and possess two crests. These are also called **Kanaka** comets; they are visible everywhere and portend extreme suffering. (18)

The sons of Jupiter are named **Vikaca** <note>meaning "Hairless" or "Radiant"</note>. They have a single white star and lack a tail. There are sixty-five of them; they appear glossy in the southern quarter and are considered malefic. (19)

Fifty-one comets born from Mercury are called **Taskara** <note>"Thieves"</note>. They are not very distinct, appearing thin, long, and white. They can appear in any direction and yield evil results. (20)

The sixty sons of Mars are blood-red or fire-like in color and possess three-pointed stars <note>resembling a trident</note>. They are named **Kaukuma** <note>"Saffron-colored"</note>; they appear in the northern quarter and are malefic. (21)

The thirty-three comets of Rahu <note>the shadow planet responsible for eclipses</note> are famous as the **Tāmasa Kīlakas** <note>"Dark Spikes"</note>. They are seen appearing upon the discs of the Sun and Moon; their effects are the same as those described for the movements of the Sun. (22)

There are one hundred and twenty comets known as **Viśvarūpa** <note>"Universal Form"</note>, born of Fire. They are surrounded by a garland of flames and bring the dread of intense fires. (23)

Seventy-seven comets born of the Wind are named **Aruna** <note>"Tawny"</note>. They are dark red, lack a distinct star, appear like a chowrie <note>a fly-whisk made of yak tail</note>, and scatter their rays. They bring evil to mankind. (24)

Eight comets named **Ganaka** <note>"Calculators"</note> are the children of Prajāpati; they resemble a cluster of stars. There are also two hundred and four comets born of Brahma, which are square in shape. (25)

Thirty-two comets born of Varuna <note>the god of the waters</note> are named **Kanka**. They appear like the stalks of a lotus, possess a radiance like the Moon, and are said to bring intense consequences. (26)

The ninety-six sons of Time (Kāla) are called **Kabandha** <note>"Headless Trunks"</note>. They have the shape of a headless body, are fierce, terrifying, and possess stars but no tails. (27)

Nine comets with white, large, single stars are born in the intermediate directions. Thus, there are a thousand comets in total. I shall now describe their specific characteristics. (28)

The comet **Vasā-ketu** <note>"Fat-comet"</note> is large, glossy, and stretches toward the north. It rises in the west and immediately causes pestilence, yet it also brings an excellent abundance of food. (29)

The **Asthi-ketu** <note>"Bone-comet"</note> has similar traits but is rough <note>lacking luster</note> and is said to bring the fear of hunger. A similar glossy comet appearing in the east is called **Śastra-ketu** <note>"Weapon-comet"</note>; it brings about wars and riots. (30)

**Kapāla-ketu** <note>"Skull-comet"</note> is visible on the New Moon day with a smoky tail and rays. It wanders through half the eastern sky and causes hunger, pestilence, drought, and disease. (31)

The comet **Raudra** <note>"Terrible"</note> appears in the path of Agni <note>the south-east</note> with a sharp point like a trident. It is dark, red, and copper-colored, traveling through a third of the sky. Its effects are similar to the Skull-comet. (32)

In the west, the comet **Cala-ketu** <note>"Moving-comet"</note> appears with a tail pointing south, as high as a finger's breadth. As it moves further north, the price of goods increases. (33)

After touching the Seven Sages <note>the Big Dipper</note>, the Pole Star, and Abhijit <note>Vega</note>, it turns back. Having traveled through half the sky, it sets in the south. (34)

It destroys the region from the banks of the Prayag to Avanti and the place called Pushkara. It also affects the north, the Devika river, and especially the region known as Madhyadeśa <note>the Middle Country/Heartland of India</note>. (35)

It also destroys other countries here and there with disease and famine. Its effects ripen over ten months, though some say eighteen. (36)

**Śveta-ketu** <note>"White-comet"</note> is visible in the first half of the night with its tail pointing south. Another comet, **Ka**, appears at the same time in the opposite direction, shaped like a yoke. Both are visible for seven days. (37)

If they are glossy, they bring abundance and welfare. However, if the one named **Ka** is seen for a longer duration, it creates ten years of suffering caused by the outbreak of weapons <note>war</note>. (38)

The **Śveta** <note>White</note> comet appears like matted hair, is rough and dark, and occupies a third of the sky. It moves in a counter-clockwise direction and destroys two-thirds of the population. (39)

With a smoky tail...

# The Course of Comets

<page-num>64</page-num>
## Varāhī Saṃhitā <note>Also known as the Bṛhat Saṃhitā</note>

When a comet appears in the constellation of the Pleiades <note>original: "Kṛttikā"</note>, it is known as the **Beam-Comet** <term>Raśmiketu: literally 'having rays of light'</term>. Its effects are understood to be the same as those of the White Comet. **40**

The **Fixed Comet** <term>Dhruvacetu</term> is one whose path, size, color, and shape are not fixed; it appears everywhere. It may be celestial, atmospheric, or terrestrial. When it is glossy/oily in appearance, it brings desirable results. **41**

It appears on the limbs of the king's army, on houses, trees, and mountains of various countries, or on the household utensils of those destined for destruction. **42**

The comet named **Lily** <term>Kumuda</term> has the luster of a white water-lily and appears in the western quarter <note>original: "Vāruṇyāṃ," the direction of Varuna</note> with its tail pointing east for one night. When seen, it creates incomparable abundance <term>Subhikṣa: a time of plenty and good food</term> for ten years. **43**

The **Jewel Comet** <term>Maṇiketu</term> is visible only once for a single watch of the night <note>approx. 3 hours</note>. It has a very tiny star and appears in the west. Its tail is straight, white, and rises from the body like a stream of milk. **44**

As soon as it rises, it creates abundance for four and a half months. However, it generally causes the appearance of small, troublesome creatures <note>pests or insects</note>. **45**

The **Water Comet** <term>Jalaketu</term> also appears in the west, glossy, with its tail pointing upward. It brings abundance and peace to the world for nine months. **46**

The **Being Comet** <term>Bhavaketu</term> is visible for a single night in the east. It has a tiny star and is glossy, with a tail resembling a lion's tail that curves to the right. **47**

For as many moments <term>Muhūrtas: units of 48 minutes</term> as it remains visible, it indicates that many months of incomparable abundance. If it appears rough/dim, it brings life-threatening diseases. **48**

In the west, the **Lotus Comet** <term>Padmaketu</term> appears, white as a lotus stalk, for one night. It brings seven years of abundance and great joy. **49**

The comet called **The Whirl** <term>Āvarta</term> appears at midnight in the west, glossy and red like the dawn, with its tail pointing to the left. For as many moments as it is visible, it brings abundance for that many months. **50**

In the west, during the twilight hour, appears the comet named **The Destroyer** <term>Saṃvarta</term>. It has a smoke-colored, copper tail. It is fierce, occupying one-third of the sky, and stands with its tip shaped like a trident. **51**

For as many moments as it is visible, it brings that many years of war. It strikes kings with the fall of weapons and afflicts the constellation in which it rises. **52**

I shall now describe the kings who face destruction when their birth stars <note>Nakṣatras</note> are touched or obscured by the smoke of these comets, excluding those comets previously described as auspicious. **53**

In **Aśvinī**, it kills the King of Aśmaka; in **Bharaṇī**, the Kirāta king. In **Kṛttikā**, the Lord of Kaliṅga; in **Rohiṇī**, the King of Śūrasena. **54**

In **Mṛgaśīrṣa**, the King of Uśīnara; in **Ārdrā**, the ruler of those living by water-products. In **Punarvasu**, the Lord of Aśmaka; in **Puṣya**, it kills the King of Magadha. **55**

In **Aśleṣā**, the King of Asikeśa; in **Maghā**, the King of Aṅga; in **Pūrvaphālgunī**, the Lord of Pāṇḍya. In **Uttara-phālgunī**, the King of Ujjain; in **Hastā**, the ruler of Daṇḍaka. **56**

In **Citrā**, the wise should predict the death of the King of Kurukṣetra. In **Svātī**, the kings of Kashmir and Kāmboja will cease to be. **57**

The kings of Ikṣvāku and Alaka are killed if it appears in **Viśākhā**. In **Anurādhā**, the Lord of Puṇḍra; in **Jyeṣṭhā**, the death of the universal emperor <term>Sārvabhauma</term>. **58**

In **Mūla**, the kings of Andhra and Madraka; in **Pūrvāṣāḍhā**, the King of Kāśī dies. In **Uttarāṣāḍhā**, the kings of Maudherya, Ārjunāyana, Śibi, and Cedi. **59**

It kills the King of Kekaya, the ruler of the Punjab <note>Pañcanada</note>, the King of Ceylon <note>Siṃhala</note>, the King of Vaṅga, the King of Naimiṣa, and the Kirāta king, respectively, in the six stars starting from **Śravaṇa**. **60**

A comet whose tail is struck by a meteor is auspicious; one that is rained upon is even more auspicious. But that same comet is inauspicious for the Colas, the Avantis, the White Huns, and the Chinese. **61**

In whichever direction the crest of the comet's tail points, or whichever constellation it touches, the countries associated with those regions are consumed by the king of that land, just as Garuda <note>the divine eagle</note> consumes snakes, after those lands have been struck by divine power. **62**

->**Thus ends the eleventh chapter, "The Course of Comets," in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā of Śrī Varāhamihira.**<-

# Chapter 11: With Hindi Commentary
->Page 65<-

Having observed everything that the sages Garga, Parashara, Asita, and Devala, as well as other scholars, have said regarding the movement of comets <note>original: "Ketuchar"</note>, this definitive account of their movements is stated. ||1|| The rising or setting of comets cannot be known through mathematics in any way, because comets are of three types: Celestial <note>divya</note>, Atmospheric <note>antariksha</note>, and Terrestrial <note>bhauma</note>. ||2|| Aside from fireflies, phosphorescence <note>literally: "abode of ghosts"</note>, ink, or jewels, when substances that are not naturally fiery take on a form as bright as fire, that is called a "Ketu-form." ||3||

The Ketu-forms seen in banners, weapons, houses, trees, horses, and elephants are Atmospheric comets. Those seen among the constellations are called Celestial comets. All others besides these are Terrestrial comets. ||4|| Some scholars say the number of comets is 101; others say there are one thousand. The sage Narada says there is only one comet, and that this single one possesses many forms. ||5|| Whether there is one comet or many does not matter; however, it is proper to describe in every way the results that arise from their rising, setting, position, contact, and various colors such as smokiness. ||6||

For as many days as a comet remains visible, its effects will ripen for that many months. However, the effects of a comet begin to manifest after 45 days—that is, from the time of its rising to its setting, however many days it is visible, the results will begin after a delay of 45 days. ||7|| A comet that appears small, clear, oily <note>gloss: smooth/lustrous</note>, straight, beautiful, and white in color will be a giver of great abundance <note>term: Subhikshadaayi; a period of easy access to food/plenty</note> and happiness. ||8|| Comets with forms opposite to this are not auspicious; they are specifically named "Dhumaketu" <note>literally: "smoke-bannered"</note>. In particular, comets that have many colors like a rainbow or possess two or three tails <note>literally: "crests" or "braids"</note> are causes of inauspiciousness. ||9||

Those comets that bear a form like a necklace of pearls, gems, or gold, are crested, and appear in the East or West directions, are "Sun-born" <note>Ravija</note>. Their name is "Kirana" <note>Beam/Ray</note>, and they are twenty-five in number. Their rising causes conflict among kings. ||10|| Those comets that appear in the South-East <note>Agni-corner</note> with colors like a parrot, fire, the midday flower, lac, or blood, are "Fire-born," and they are also twenty-five in number. $(25+25=50)$ Their rising causes fear of fire. ||11|| The twenty-five $(50 + 25 = 75)$ that have crooked crests, are rough/dry, black in color, and appear in the South, are "Yama-born" <note>Yama is the god of death</note>. Their rising brings about plague/mortality. ||12||

The twenty-two comets $(75+22=97)$ that appear in the North-East <note>Ishan direction</note>, round in shape like a mirror, without tails, possessing rays, and having a luster like oily water, are "Earth-born." Their rising causes famine and fear. ||13|| The three comets $(97+3=100)$ that are like moonbeams, silver, snow, white water-lilies, or the Kunda flower are "Sons of the Moon" and appear in the North. Their rising brings abundance. ||14|| And there is one comet born from Brahma called "Brahmadanda" <note>The Staff of Brahma</note>, which signals the end of an age. $(100+1=101)$ This one has three tails and three colors; there is no fixed rule for which direction it may appear in. ||15||

In this manner, the description of the one hundred and one comets is written. Now, the description of the remaining 899 comets is given with clear characteristics. ||16|| The eighty-four comets known as "Sons of Venus" <note>Shukratanaya</note> appear in the North and North-East directions...

When they rise, the people of the earth become sinful. || 19 || Those Ketus who are not clearly visible, being subtle, long, white-colored, appearing in any direction, and named *Taskara* <note>meaning "thief"</note> are the sons of Mercury. They number fifty-one (209 + 51 = 260) and bring extremely sinful results. || 20 || Those whose color is like blood or fire, who have three crests and resemble stars, number sixty (260 + 60 = 320). Located in the northern direction and named *Kaukuma*, these sons of Mars are also givers of sinful results. || 21 || There are thirty-three (320 + 33 = 353) sons of Rahu named *Tamasakilaka* <note>meaning "dark spikes"</note>; they are seen crossing the paths of the Sun and Moon, and their effects are described in the section on Sunday. || 22 || Those whose bodies are adorned with a garland of flames, numbering one hundred and twenty (353 + 120 = 473) and named *Agnivashvarupa*, grant a fierce fear of fire. || 23 || Those Ketus who are dark reddish-brown, whose rays spread out like a fly-whisk <note>original: "chamar"</note>, who are rough, born of the wind, and number seventy-seven (473 + 77 = 550)—their rising brings fear of sin. || 24 || The eight (550 + 8 = 558) Ketus who are sons of Prajapati and shaped like a cluster of stars are named *Ganaka*. The Ketus known as the offspring of Brahma, who are square in shape, number two hundred and four (558 + 204 = 762). || 25 || Those whose shape is like a *Gulma* <note>a bush or cluster of vines</note>, numbering thirty-two (762 + 32 = 794) and named *Kanka*, are the sons of Varuna; they have a luster like the moon and give extremely inauspicious results. || 26 || Those who possess a shape like a headless torso <note>original: "kabandh"</note>, numbering ninety-six (794 + 96 = 890) and named *Kabandha*, are the sons of Time <note>Kala</note>; these are terrifying, fear-inducing, and are studded with misshapen stars. || 27 || The nine (890 + 9 = 899) Ketus that consist of single large stars are born from the intermediate directions. In this manner (the previous 101 and the current 899 totaling 1000), one thousand Ketus have been described; now their specific details are told. || 28 || The Ketus that rise in the western direction and spread toward the north, being large and smooth in form, are called *Vasaketu*. Their rising brings pestilence <note>mari</note> but also an excellent, abundant harvest. || 29 || Those Ketus that rise with the same characteristics as before but are rough yet smooth are named *Shastra*; their rising brings fear of hunger, upheaval <note>damar</note>, and pestilence. || 30 || The Ketu that appears on the day of the new moon in the eastern half of the sky with a thousand rays and a thousand crests is named *Kapala Ketu*; it causes hunger, pestilence, drought, and fear of disease. || 31 || In the south-eastern path of the sky, appearing like the tip of a trident, brownish-grey, rough, and possessed of copper-colored rays that travel through three parts of the sky—this is called *Raudra Ketu*. It is called **Chal-Ketu** <note>The "Moving Comet"</note>. If this Chal-Ketu gradually lengthens in this manner and touches the **Great Bear** <note>original: "Saptarshi-mandal"; the seven sages constellation</note> or the star **Vega** <note>original: "Abhijit Nakshatra"</note>, and after traversing a portion of the sky, sets in the southern direction, then the great **Middle Country** <note>original: "Madhyadesh"; the central cultural heartland of ancient India</note>—extending from near **Prayag** <note>Modern-day Prayagraj/Allahabad</note> to **Avanti** <note>The region around Ujjain</note>, including **Pushkar-desh** and up to the northern **Devika River**—is destroyed. At certain times, other countries are also destroyed by disease or famine. Its effects ripen in ten months; however, some scholars say its effects manifest in eighteen months. ||34|| ||35|| ||36||

The comet seen in the eastern part of the sky, ahead of the south at midnight, is called **Dhum-Ketu** <note>The "Smoke Comet"</note>. And the comet named **(Ka)** <note>Likely referring to a specific classification like Karaka or a similar root</note>, which is shaped like the yoke of a chariot, appears for seven days at the turning of an age <note>Yuga</note>. ||37|| And if the **(Ka)** named Dhum-Ketu is visible for many days, there is constant suffering caused by the "fury of weapons" <note>warfare</note> for ten years. ||38||

If the comet named **Shveta** <note>The "White Comet"</note> appears shaped like matted hair <note>Jata</note>, is rough, brownish-red in color, and returns after traversing three parts of the sky, then one-third of the population is destroyed. ||39|| The comet that appears with a somewhat smoky crest and touches the **Pleiades** <note>original: "Kruttika Nakshatra"</note> is called **Rashmi-Ketu** <note>The "Ray Comet"</note>; its effects are similar to the Shveta comet. ||40||

There is a type of comet named **Dhruva** <note>The "Constant" or "Fixed" Comet</note>; its shape, color, and size are not fixed, nor is its motion fixed. It is of three types: celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial. It is oily <note>glossy/bright</note> and gives unpredictable results. ||41|| This Dhruva-Ketu is often seen on the limbs of the armies of kings destined for destruction, on the trees of a country facing ruin, or in the homes of householders facing downfall. ||42||

The comet whose radiance is like a white water-lily <note>original: "Kumud"</note> and whose crest spreads toward the east is called **Kumud-Ketu**. It grants a "good harvest" <note>term: "Subhiksha" - a period of plenty and easy availability of food</note> for ten consecutive years. The comet that is shaped like a tiny star and is visible in the western direction for one watch <note>Pahar; approx. 3 hours</note> is named **Mani-Ketu** <note>The "Jewel Comet"</note>. Just as a stream of milk flows when pressure is applied to a breast, its crest is similarly straight and white in color. ||43|| 44|| Upon its rising, there is a good harvest for four and a half months, but its influence is mostly felt by small creatures. ||45||

The comet that has a high crest in another direction and is smooth/oily at the back is called **Jala-Ketu** <note>The "Water Comet"</note>. Upon the rising of Jala-Ketu, there is a good harvest for nine months and living beings find peace. ||46|| Its crest is turned to the right <note>clockwise</note> like a lion's tail, and a glossy, tiny star is seen in the eastern direction at night; that is **Bhava-Ketu**. ||47|| For as many moments <note>Muhurtas</note> as this Bhava-Ketu is visible, there will be an incomparable good harvest for that many months. If it appears rough, there will be life-threatening diseases. ||48||

The comet shaped like the previous one but white like a lotus stalk <note>Mrunal</note>, seen in the western direction for one night, is named **Padma-Ketu** <note>The "Lotus Comet"</note>. From this, there is a joyful good harvest for seven years. ||49|| The comet seen at midnight with a crest on the left, having the radiance of the dawn <note>Aruna; reddish-gold</note> and appearing glossy, is called **Avarta**. For as many moments as this comet is visible, there is a good harvest for that many months. ||50||

The comet that has a smoky or copper-colored crest, is terrifying, and occupies three parts of the sky, shaped like the tip of a trident <note>Shul</note> and appearing in the west during twilight, is called **Samvarta-Ketu**. ||51|| For as many moments as this comet is visible, kings will be tormented by the "falling of weapons" <note>war</note> for that many years, and at the time of its rising...

A person born under the constellation <term>Nakshatra; the 27 lunar mansions of Hindu astrology</term> which is currently being affected by a comet also suffers distress. ||52|| It is now described which king is slain when a particular constellation is smoked or touched by a comet. ||53|| If the constellation Ashwini is smoked or touched by a comet, the King of the Ashmaka country is destroyed. In Bharani, the Lord of the Kiratas; in Krittika, the King of Kalinga; in Rohini, the King of Shurasena; in Mrigashira, the King of Ushinara; in Ardra, the King of Matsya; in Punarvasu, the Lord of Ashmaka; in the Pushya constellation, the Sovereign of Magadha; in Ashlesha, the Lord of Asika; in the Magha constellation, the King of Anga; in Purva-Phalguni, the King of the Pandyas; in Uttara-Phalguni, the Ruler of Ujjain; in Hasta, the Lord of Danda; in Chitra, the King of Kurukshetra; in the Swati constellation, the Kings of Kashmir and Kamboja; in Vishakha, the Lords of Ikshvaku and Ratnaka; in the Anuradha constellation, the King of the Pundra country; and in the Jyeshtha constellation, the Universal Monarch <note>Chakravarti</note> dies. ||54||55||56||57||58|| If the Mula constellation is smoked or touched by a comet, the Kings of Andhra and Madra meet their death. In Purva-Ashadha, the Lord of Kashi; in the Uttara-Ashadha constellation, the King of Yodha, the King of Arjunayana, the Lord of the Shivi people, and the King of Vaidya are destroyed. And starting from Shravana, if the next six constellations are afflicted, the Kings of Kekaya, Punjab, Ceylon <note>Sinhala</note>, Bengal <note>Vanga</note>, Naimisharanya, and the Kirata country are destroyed in order. ||59||60|| If the crest of the comet is pierced by a meteor, it is auspicious. If it is accompanied by rain in every way, it is extremely fortunate; however, this same occurrence brings misfortune to the countries of Chola, Afghanistan <note>Avagana</note>, Sita, and China. ||61|| Those countries from which the crests of the comet are turned away or bowed, or those countries where it touches a constellation, all such countries are destroyed as if by divine power; just as the Great Eagle Garuda is pleased by consuming the hoods of snakes, other kings become happy by invading those weakened lands. ||62||
