# Varahi Samhita

One should understand *Kudadhamatsya* to mean a lizard. || 8 || *Kroda*, *Divya*, and *Dhanvan* are names for the boar; by saying *Uksha*, one should understand a cow. *Kurkara* refers to a dog, and the *Chataka* species is called *Shukarika*. || 9 || In this manner, having learned the names of omens established in various regions, one should carefully reflect and compare them with the scriptures to understand the sounds of omens. || 10 ||

The "blazing" <note>original: "dipta" - a technical term for an intense or alarming omen sound</note> sound of the *Vanjula* bird is "Tittid," but the "Kilikili" sound is its full, natural tone. The sounds of the hawk, parrot, vulture, and heron are considered "blazing" when they are contrary to their natural disposition. || 11 || A pigeon sitting on a vehicle, a seat, a bed, or on a house, or entering a house, is auspicious for men. Due to differences in species, the timing of the results is also explained. || 12 || The fruit of a white pigeon manifests in one year; that of a multi-colored or spotted pigeon in six months; and the fruit of a saffron-colored or smoke-colored pigeon occurs quickly. || 13 ||

The "Vichit" sound of the *Shyama* <note>The Indian Robin or a similar dark songbird</note> is full; the "Shuli-shul" sound is blessed; the "Chach" sound is "blazing"; and the "Chikchik" sound causes a meeting with one's beloved. || 14 || The "Guggu" sound of the *Harita* <note>Green Pigeon</note> is full, while its other sounds are "blazing." Every type of variegated song of the *Bharadwaja* bird <note>The Skylark</note> is said to be auspicious. || 15 || The "Kishikishi" sound of the *Karayika* is full, the "Kahkah" sound is auspicious, and the "Karkar" sound causes only well-being but does not fulfill the specific task. || 16 || Its "Kotukli" sound brings safety, and the "Katukli" sound causes rain. The "Kotikili" sound is fruitless, and the "Gukrut" sound is "blazing." || 17 ||

Seeing a *Divyaka* <note>likely a specific lizard or bird</note> on the left side is excellent, but if that *Divyaka* is raised one cubit high, the task should be known as successful. If a *Divyaka* is one cubit high on the left of a traveler, the earth up to the ocean comes under that traveler's control. || 18 || A snake coming from the front indicates an encounter with an enemy for the traveler, and also reveals imprisonment, slaughter, and destruction. Alternatively, if that snake comes from the left, the journey is neither prosperous nor successful. || 19 ||

The mark of a lotus on the heads of horses, elephants, and snakes is auspicious. A *Khanjana* bird <note>Wagtail</note> sitting in a pure, dark-green field full of crops grants a kingdom and is prosperous. If the Wagtail sits on ashes, bones, wood, chaff, hair, or straw, it becomes wicked and gives sorrow for one year. || 20 || The "Kilikilkili" peaceful sound of the partridge brings welfare. If a rabbit comes to the left side at night and makes a sound, it is called auspicious. || 21 || The "Kilikili" sound of a monkey is "blazing"; it does not indicate a good result for a traveler. However, the "Chugla" sound of a *Kulalakukkuta* <note>Wild fowl or pheasant</note>, which is similar to a monkey's "blazing" sound, reveals an auspicious result. || 22 ||

If a *Nilkantha* bird <note>Indian Roller</note> holding a worm, moth, or ant in its beak circumambulates a man or makes a *Swastika* <note>cross-like pattern</note> in the sky, that man desiring to travel will quickly gain much wealth. || 23 || If a *Nilkantha*, while fighting with a crow, goes to the right side and is defeated, then that defeat...

Time reveals the destruction of a traveling man; if the signs are contrary to this, the traveler achieves victory. ||24|| If the Blue Jay <note>original: "Neelkanth"</note> makes the 'Keka' sound on the left side like a full water-pot, it grants victory. However, its 'Kruk' sound, which is considered "blazing" <note>term: Deept (blazing) — a technical term in omenology for harsh, intense, or ill-omened sounds</note>, is not auspicious. Nevertheless, the mere sight of it is always beneficial for a traveler. ||25|| The Andeera bird is said to be "full" <note>auspicious</note> with the sound 'Ti' and "blazing" <note>inauspicious</note> when making the sound 'Tittittit'. If a Jackal <note>original: "Phenta/Shrygal"</note> is on the right side, it is auspicious; its vocalization does not produce any specific additional result. ||26||

The 'Kwa Kwa Kwa' sound of the Shreekant bird on the traveler's right is considered auspicious, while the 'Chikuchiki' sound gives middling results. All other sounds of this bird are said to be fruitless. ||27|| If the Bhandeek bird makes the 'Chirilu Chirilu' sound on the traveler's left, it is said to grant desired results. If it moves from the left side to the right side, the task is accomplished quickly. ||28|| If the Bhandeek makes the 'Chikuchiki' sound and moves from the left part to the right part, it brings well-being, but does not ensure the completion of the task. If the movement is opposite to this, it becomes a cause for slaughter, imprisonment, and fear. ||29||

The Myna bird that quickly makes the 'Kruk' or 'Tre-Tre' sound is named Abhaya. That Myna reveals that blood will soon flow from the traveler's body. ||30|| The 'Chirulu Iralu' sound of a Jackal from the left side is called auspicious, while its other sounds are called "blazing." ||31|| The sound of a donkey situated on the left side wishes the best for the traveler; the 'Om-kar' sound <note>a sound resembling the sacred syllable Om</note> is beneficial for the traveler. Apart from this, all other types of donkey sounds are called "blazing." ||32||

If the Kurang (Deer) makes the 'Aa' sound, and the Prishat (Spotted Deer) makes the 'O' sound, it is a "full" <note>auspicious</note> sound. Aside from these, other sounds are "blazing." All "full" sounds grant auspicious results, and "blazing" sounds grant sinful/unfortunate results. ||33|| Roosters <note>original: "Arunshikha/Kukkut"</note> make the 'Kuku-Kuku' sound when afraid; except for this sound at night, all other sounds are fear-inducing. If, at the end of the night, a healthy rooster makes its natural sound, there is growth in the nation, the city, and the earth. ||34||

The sound of a Lizard <note>original: "Chhipika"</note> is of many kinds. Among them, only the 'Kulukulu' sound is auspicious, while other sounds are not. All sounds of a cat are inauspicious for a traveler. The sneezing sound of a cow <note>original: "Gojatika"</note> indicates the death of the traveler. ||35|| The Owl, desiring its mate, makes the 'Hun-hunguluku' sound with joy. This is its "full" sound. The 'Gululu' and 'Kiskisi' sounds are always "blazing." When it makes the 'Valval' sound once, one should expect distress. The 'Tattata' sound is harmful. All other sounds are "blazing" and not auspicious. ||36|| A pair of Cranes <note>original: "Saras"</note> vocalizing together gives the desired result. The sound of a single crane is inauspicious; even if there is a delayed echo after one calls, it is not auspicious. ||37|| The Pingala (Spotted Owlet) reveals auspiciousness by making the 'Chirilu Iralu' sound; all its other sounds are "blazing"...

...is the definition. ||38|| The "isi" sound of the <term>Pingala</term> <note>The spotted owlet, often used in divination</note> stops one from departing. The "kushu-kushu" sound causes distress. Now, the method by which that <term>Pingalika</term> reveals the attainment of a desired goal is described. ||39|| After the day has passed, at the time of twilight, one should become purified and approach the tree where the <term>Pingala</term> resides. There, one should properly worship the gods, starting with Brahma, and the tree itself with new clothes and fragrant substances. ||40|| Then, at midnight, standing alone at the <term>Agni-kona</term> <note>The South-East corner</note> of that tree, one should give both divine and worldly oaths to the <term>Pingala</term>. Reciting this mantra, one should ask the <term>Pingala</term> about their desire. The mantra should be recited in a voice loud enough for the <term>Pingala</term> to hear. The mantra is as follows: ||41|| "O Auspicious One! Whatever has been spoken by me, tell me its true meaning. For, O Blessed One, you are said to be the knower of the meaning of all speech. I shall leave after asking you today, and returning in the morning, I shall ask again while stationed in the South-East. Whatever I have asked of you, explain it to me through your movements in such a way that I may understand it without confusion." ||42||43||44|| After speaking thus to the <term>Pingala</term> perched upon the tree, if she makes the sound "chirilu irilu," the work will be accomplished. If she utters the sounds "kuchakucha" or "dishikara," it indicates extreme anxiety. ||45|| If she gives no verbal response—that is, remains silent—the desired task will be successful. Then, one should determine the result using the previously mentioned <term>Dikka-chakra</term> <note>A directional diagram used for divination</note>. The results for a <term>Pingala</term> perched on high, middle, or low branches are said to be excellent, middling, and poor, respectively. ||46|| Within and outside the directional circle of the <term>Dikka-chakra</term>, the results for lizards are determined. For the shrew, the "chic-chid" sound is called "blazing" <note>intense/urgent</note> and the "tit-tid" sound is called "full" <note>complete/favorable</note>. ||47||

### Chapter Eighty-Nine

## Omens of the Dog-Circle (Shva-Chakra)

When a dog urinates upon a man, a horse, an elephant's forehead, a saddle, a milky tree, a heap of bricks, an umbrella, a bed, a seat, a mortar, a flag, a whisk, or a grassy or flowering spot and then moves ahead of a traveler, then success in one's task is assured. If it urinates on wet cow dung, there will be an arrival of sweet food; if on dry urine <note>or dry ground</note>, dry food; or perhaps the obtaining of jaggery or sweets. However, if it urinates on or strikes against poisonous trees, thorny bushes, wood, stones, dry trees, bones, or cremation grounds while in front of a traveler, it foretells misfortune. If it urinates on beds, potter's vessels, or other unused items or jewels, it brings a flaw or blemish to a maiden; if these items are currently being used, it indicates the corruption of the mistress of the house. The result for shoes is the same as for a cow: a mixing of castes. If a dog stands facing the direction of travel holding a shoe in its mouth, there will be success. If it holds a piece of meat, there is a gain of wealth. A wet bone is auspicious. If it holds a burning coal or a dry bone, death is indicated. If it holds a extinguished brand, a physical blow or injury occurs. If it holds a man's head, hand, or foot in its mouth, there is an acquisition of land. With clothes or rags, some say it brings calamity, while others say a cloth is auspicious. If it enters a house with a dry bone in its mouth...

# Chapter 89: With Hindi Commentary

If a dog approaches and stays near a person while holding a chain, a broken creeper, or a leather strap in its mouth, it signifies the death of a leader or some form of imprisonment. If it licks its own feet, shakes its ears, or jumps over the person, it indicates obstacles for a traveler. If it scratches its own body, it foretells a quarrel. A dog standing with its hind legs raised is always a sign of misfortune. ||1||

If a dog—either alone or in a pack—faces the sun at sunrise and howls in the middle of a village, it predicts the imminent arrival of a new ruler for that land. ||2||

If it faces the sun while standing in the southeast <note>original: "Agni-dik" or the direction of fire</note>, it warns of fear from thieves or fire in the near future. At midday, this behavior foretells death; in the afternoon, it signifies a violent quarrel involving bloodshed. ||3||

Howling while facing the sun at sunset brings immediate fear to farmers. During the first watch of the night <note>Pradosha</note>, if it faces the northwest <note>original: "Anila-dik" or the direction of wind</note>, it indicates danger arising from storms or thieves. ||4||

At midnight, facing north indicates distress for priests <note>Brahmins</note> and the theft of cattle. At the end of the night <note>dawn</note>, facing the northeast <note>original: "Shiva-dik"</note> foretells the corruption of maidens, fires, and miscarriages. ||5||

Dogs that howl loudly while perched on heaps of grass, or standing atop palaces and grand houses, predict heavy rainfall during the monsoon; at other times of the year, they signify death, fire, or dust storms. ||6||

During a drought in the rainy season, if dogs enter the water and, upon returning, repeatedly shake themselves or drink water frequently, they bring rain within twelve days. ||7||

If a dog rests its head inside a doorway while its body remains outside and howls while looking at the mistress of the house, it brings disease. If it stays inside the house but howls while looking outward, it suggests the woman of the house is unfaithful. ||8||

When a dog scratches the wall of a house, there is a fear of burglars <note>literally "tunnel-diggers"</note>. If it scratches the cowshed, it predicts the theft of cattle; however, if it scratches the ground where grain is stored, it foretells the gain of wealth. ||9||

A dog with a tear in one eye, a dejected look, or a poor appetite brings sorrow to that household. Conversely, a dog playing with cows indicates a time of plenty <note>Subhiksha</note>, safety, health, and joy. ||10||

If a dog sniffs a person's left knee, it indicates the arrival of wealth; if the right knee, it suggests a quarrel with women. Sniffing the left thigh indicates the enjoyment of sensory pleasures, while the right thigh suggests a conflict with treacherous friends. ||11||

If it sniffs the feet of someone about to depart, it predicts a successful journey; if it sniffs the feet of someone sitting still, it indicates they will soon undertake a journey. If it sniffs the shoes of someone staying in one place, the dog indicates they will travel quickly. ||12||

If it sniffs both arms, one should recognize the threat of enemies or thieves. If a dog hides food, meat, or bones in ashes, it foretells an immediate outbreak of fire. ||13||

If dogs bark inside a village and then howl in a cremation ground outside, it signifies the death of a prominent man. If a dog howls while facing someone who is about to depart, it forbids the journey. ||14||

A sound like "U" indicates success for a thief; an "A" sound on the left side indicates a distraction or delay. An "O" sound should be understood as a disturbance, and all such sounds heard from behind act as a prohibition of the current action. ||15||

Those dogs that howl "Shava" <note>meaning "corpse"</note> loudly and repeatedly as if being beaten with sticks, or those that run in circles, bring about desolation and the fear of death. ||16||

If a dog bares its teeth and licks the corners of its mouth, experts say it indicates a delicious meal is coming. If it licks its face but not the corners of its mouth, it creates obstacles to food, even if the meal has already begun. ||17||

If dogs gather in the middle of a village or city and bark repeatedly in unison, they announce distress for the ruler. A dog in the forest should be interpreted the same way as a wild deer. ||18||

Howling near a tree indicates rainfall; near a hitching post <note>Indrakila</note>, it means trouble for a minister. In the "house of wind" <note>open areas</note>, it means danger to crops; inside a house, it means trouble for the city; and at the city gate, it means trouble for the city itself. ||19||

Barking at beds brings fear to their owners; barking at vehicles brings fear later on. Now, regarding the left side... <note>The text cuts off as it begins a new section on directional omens.</note>

### By barking, they announce the fear of enemies in human settlements. ||20|| (Thus ends the fourth chapter on the Circle of Dogs in the General Omens)

### Thus ends the eighty-ninth chapter in the Brihat Samhita composed by the illustrious Varahamihira. ||89||

<note>Varahamihira was a 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath; the Brihat Samhita is his "Great Compilation" of worldly knowledge.</note>

When dogs urinate upon a human, a horse, an elephant, a water-pot, the shadow of a horse, milk-bearing trees, a pile of bricks, an umbrella, a bed, a seat, a mortar <note>ulūkhala: a stone or wooden vessel for grinding grain</note>, a flag, a fly-whisk <note>chāmara: a traditional symbol of royalty</note>, a grassy field, or a place full of flowers, and then move forward, the traveler’s task will be successfully accomplished. Alternatively, if at that same time they urinate upon wet cow-dung and then walk on, the traveler will receive a sweet meal. If a dog urinates on a dry object and then walks ahead of the traveler, the person will obtain jaggery and sweets.

If a dog urinates upon a poisonous tree <note>such as the Strychnine tree</note>, a thorny tree, wood, a stone, a withered tree, a bone, or in a cremation ground, and then returns to walk ahead of the traveler, it reveals misfortune for that person. If it urinates on a new and unbroken bed or a potter’s vessel, it signifies the defilement of a maiden. If these items (the bed, etc.) have already been used, then the fault lies with the housewife of the traveler. The omen for sandals is the same as that for the potter's vessel. If a dog urinates upon cattle and then walks before the traveler, it signifies the birth of mixed castes <note>term: Varna-sankara; a traditional sociological concern regarding the blurring of social boundaries</note>.

When a dog approaches a traveler from the front while firmly holding a shoe in its mouth, the traveler’s work will be successful. If it approaches with meat in its mouth, wealth will be obtained; if it carries a bone, it is auspicious. However, if it approaches carrying a burning piece of wood or a dry bone, it signifies the death of the traveler. If a dog comes carrying a human head, hand, foot, or a "quiet" (extinguished) piece of charcoal in its mouth, it signifies the gain of land. If it carries a piece of torn cloth, it reveals death—though some authorities say that a dog arriving with cloth is auspicious.

If a dog enters a house carrying a dry bone in its mouth, the master of the house will die. When a dog enters a home carrying a chain, a piece of wet vine, an elephant’s tethering rope, or any binding material, it signifies imprisonment or bondage. If, at the time of departure, a dog licks the traveler’s foot, flaps its ears, or jumps upon them, it indicates an obstacle to the journey. Scratching its body also opposes the journey. If a dog sleeps with its legs pointing upward, it is always a sign of misfortune. ||1||

If one or more dogs gather in the center of a village at sunrise and howl while facing the sun, that village will soon have a different landlord. ||2|| If dogs howl facing the sun in the southeast direction <note>Agni-kona</note>, there will soon be terror from fire and thieves. A dog howling toward the sun at midday reveals fear of fire and fear of death. If a dog howls toward the sun after midday, it signifies suffering involving the shedding of blood. ||3||

If a dog howls facing the sun at sunset, it indicates immediate danger to farmers. If it howls toward the sun in the northwest direction <note>Vayu-kona</note> during the twilight hour <note>Pradosha</note>, fear will arise from wind and thieves. ||4|| If a dog makes noise at midnight facing north, it signifies distress to the Brahmins and a plea for the recovery of stolen cows. If a dog howls toward the northeast <note>Ishan-kona</note> at the end of the night, it signifies the defilement of a maiden, fire, and miscarriage...

...reveals. ||5|| If a dog, during the rainy season, stands upon a thatched roof made of straw or atop a grand palace or house and howls in a high pitch, it indicates intense rainfall. ||6|| During the monsoon, if there is a drought and a dog bathes in water, and upon returning <note>The word "returning" here implies rolling over or turning on its side</note> it sheds water or stands shivering while drinking, it indicates that it will rain after 12 days. ||7|| If a dog keeps its head inside the doorway and its body outside and howls repeatedly while looking at the mistress of the house, it brings disease. If it stays inside the temple and howls while facing outward, it portends that the mistress may become barren. ||8||

When a dog digs at the wall of a house, it indicates fear for the one who built it <note>or the inhabitant</note>. If it digs in the place where cows are kept, it indicates the theft of cattle. If it digs in a place where grain is stored, it reveals a forthcoming gain of grain. ||9|| If a dog has one eye filled with tears or has diminished vision, and if that dog eats very little, it brings sorrow to the household. A dog playing with cows reveals a time of abundance <term>Subhiksha</term> <note>a period where food is easily available</note>, safety, health, and joy. ||10||

If a dog sniffs the left thigh, it indicates a gain of wealth; if it sniffs the right thigh, it indicates a dispute with women. Sniffing the left upper thigh <term>Uru</term> indicates sensory enjoyment, while sniffing the right upper thigh indicates a quarrel with beloved friends. ||11|| If a dog sniffs both feet of one about to depart on a journey, the journey will not take place. If it sniffs the feet of a man who is stationary, it reveals the attainment of a desired object. If it sniffs the shoes of one sitting upon a seat, it reveals an imminent journey. ||12||

Repeated sniffing of both arms reveals fear of enemies and thieves. Furthermore, if a dog hides meat, bones, or food items in ashes, it reveals the imminent wrath of fire <note>a house fire</note>. ||13|| If a dog howls first in the village and then howls in the outskirts or a cremation ground, it portends the destruction of a great man of that place. When a dog howls in front of a traveler, it halts the journey. ||14||

A sound resembling the vowel 'U' <note>original: "U-kara"</note> or an 'O' sound on the left side indicates the fulfillment of a goal. An 'Au' sound indicates delay, and all types of sounds made from behind indicate a prohibition <note>of the intended action</note>. ||15|| If all the dogs, as if beaten by a rod, howl repeatedly in a high pitch like the sound of a conch shell and run in circles, they reveal emptiness <note>desolation</note> and the fear of death. ||16||

If a dog shows its teeth and licks the corners of its lips, those who know the fruits of omens expect sweet food. If it licks the face in addition to the corners of the lips, then even if one begins to eat, the food becomes obstructed <note>by some calamity</note>. ||17|| If dogs gather in a village or city and howl repeatedly, they reveal distress for the lord of that city or village. Wild dogs, being similar to deer, are not to be considered in these omens. ||18||

A dog barking near a tree indicates rain. Barking near the <term>Indrakila</term> <note>the main pillar or threshold of a city gate</note> indicates suffering for the minister. Barking in the northwest corner <term>Vayukona</term> of the house indicates fear for the crops. Barking at the city gate indicates suffering for the citizens. ||19|| If a dog barks upon a bed, it indicates fear for its owners. Barking while situated on a vehicle indicates fear. If it barks while on the left side of men, it reveals fear of enemies. ||20||

### Now begins the Ninetieth Chapter
#### On Omens: The Cries of the Jackal

In terms of the results they portend, jackals are similar to dogs; the distinction is that jackals experience a period of rut <note>mating heat or intoxication</note> during the winter season. A cry of "Tata" following a "Huhu" sound is considered their "full" <note>auspicious or natural</note> note; all other sounds are designated as "blazing" <note>term: *Pradipta*—ominous or over-excited sounds associated with ill fortune</note>. ||1|| The "Kakka" sound of the female fox <note>original: *Lomashika*</note> is indeed her full and natural cry. Any other sounds she makes that depart from her nature are all declared by the sages to be "blazing." ||2|| A female jackal <note>original: *Shiva*</note> situated in the East or North is beneficial, and a "peaceful" <note>calm</note> jackal is honored everywhere. However, if she faces a "smoky" <note>inauspicious</note> direction and gives a "blazing" cry, she destroys the lords of the directions. ||3|| A "blazing" jackal is inauspicious in all directions, and particularly so if she makes a "Haha" sound. If she is on the left side of a city or an army, or faces the sun, she brings great distress. ||4|| A cry sounding like "Yahi" <note>Go!</note> foretells danger from fire; "Tata" is a messenger of death; "Dhig-dhig" <note>Fie! Shame!</note> speaks of wicked deeds; and a jackal with a "flaming mouth" <note>an omen where the animal appears to breathe fire</note> destroys the country. ||5|| Some authorities claim that the "flaming mouth" is not necessarily terrible, as her mouth may appear to glow naturally due to the nature of her saliva, similar to the glow of a firefly. ||6|| If she responds to another's cry from the South, she foretells death by hanging; if she responds from the West, she predicts death in water. ||7|| If the listener remains unperturbed upon hearing her, it is desirable and indicates the acquisition of wealth or the arrival of a loved one. If the listener is agitated, it signifies a rift among leaders or a loss of vehicles/mounts. ||8|| These results should be observed for up to seven cries; any cries beyond that are of no consequence. In the South, the results are reversed, except for the fifth and sixth cries. ||9|| That female jackal who causes the hair of men to stand on end, or causes horses to void dung and urine, or creates a cry of terror, is not a "Shiva" <note>auspicious one</note> but a bringer of ill-fortune. ||10|| If a jackal falls silent when a man, elephant, or horse makes a sound in response, she bestows welfare upon the army or the city. ||11|| A jackal crying "Bhe-bhe" is terrifying; "Bho-bho" indicates calamity; "Phi-phu" announces death or imprisonment; but "Huhu" is a jackal beneficial to one's own self in its tone. ||12|| A "peaceful" jackal crying "Au" after the letter "A," or crying "Tata" loudly, or "Tete" followed by "The-the"—these are cries born of her own contentment. ||13|| If a jackal first utters a loud, fierce sound and then howls in a manner that mimics someone else, she predicts safety, the acquisition of wealth, or a reunion with a loved one who has been traveling. ||14||

->(Thus ends the fifth chapter within the general section on Omens, titled "The Cries of the Jackal")<-

### Thus ends the ninetieth chapter in the Brihat Samhita composed by the venerable Varahamihira. ||90||

# Chapter Ninety-One
# Omens: The Behavior of Deer

Wild deer coming from the north, whether crying out, standing still, or moving, bring trouble if they arrive in an uneven or agitated manner. If they appear "blazing" <note>agitated or facing the sun</note> or wander around empty spaces, they indicate fears regarding the present, past, and future. ||1|| If these wild deer are barked at by domestic animals, it signifies fear and obstruction. If they are answered by other wild animals, or by both domestic and wild, it indicates the capture of prisoners. ||2|| If a wild animal stands at the gate of a city, a siege is predicted; if it enters, destruction follows. If it gives birth there, death occurs; if two stay there, it is a sign of ruin; and if it enters a house, imprisonment is foretold. ||3|| (Thus ends the sixth chapter on the behavior of deer in the general section on omens).

->Thus ends the ninety-first chapter in the Brihat Samhita of Shri Varahamihira. ||91||<-

<meta>This page continues the translation of the Brihat Samhita, a foundational Sanskrit encyclopedic text by Varahamihira, as interpreted by the 19th-century commentator Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra of Moradabad.</meta>

<page-num>(304)</page-num>
<header>The Barahi Samhita (The Compendium of Varahamihira)</header>

If wild deer enter the boundaries of a village and make noise, or remain there while wandering, or run about vigorously in all directions, they reveal danger in the past, future, and present. If they wander about making "blazing" <note>original: "dipta" - a technical term in augury referring to harsh, aggressive, or ill-omened sounds</note> noises, they cause that place to become desolate. ||1|| If the village animals make noise behind those deer, it is a cause for fear. If wild animals make noise behind village animals, the city or town will be surrounded by enemies. If both wild and domestic animals make noise behind one another, enemies will take the people of that city captive. ||2|| If a wild animal comes and stands at the door, enemies will besiege the city. If a wild animal enters fully inside a house, the city will be destroyed; if a wild animal gives birth in a house, death occurs; if it stays in the house, there is fear; and by its mere entry into the house, the master of the house faces imprisonment. ||3||

Thus ends the ninety-first chapter in the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western Provinces, on the Brihat Samhita composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira. ||91||

### Now begins the Ninety-Second Chapter

#### On Omens: The Movements of Cattle

<note>The following section translates the original Sanskrit verses into English.</note>

> If cows appear miserable, it bodes ill for the king; if they scratch the earth with their hooves, it foretells disease. If their large eyes are filled with tears, they bring death; and if they are terrified and low loudly, they indicate danger from thieves. ||1|| A cow lowing at night without cause signifies danger, but the lowing of a bull at night is auspicious. If cows are swarmed by flies or followed closely by puppies <note>original: "saramatma-jai" - offspring of Sarama (the divine bitch), i.e., dogs</note>, then rain will come quickly. ||2|| If cows come home lowing and huddle with other cows, it leads to the increase of the herd. If their limbs are wet or their hair stands on end with joy, such cows are considered blessed and bringers of wealth; the same applies to buffaloes. ||3|| (Thus ends the seventh chapter titled 'Movements of Cattle' in the General Omens section).

->Thus ends the ninety-second chapter in the Brihat Samhita created by the venerable Varahamihira. ||92||<-

<note>The following is the Hindi commentary on the verses above.</note>

If cows appear distressed, they are the cause of misfortune for the king. If cows scrape the ground with their feet, disease occurs. If their eyes are filled with tears, it signifies death, and if they are frightened and make a loud sound, they manifest fear of thieves. ||1|| A cow making noise at night without reason is a cause for fear, but the sound of a bull is auspicious. If flies or puppies surround the cows excessively, there will be immediate rain. ||2|| If cows come into the house while lowing <note>original: "rambha-shabd" - the 'moo' of a cow</note> and join with many other cows, it causes the growth of the cowshed. If the cows' limbs are drenched with water or if they experience horripilation <note>hair standing on end due to excitement</note>, those cows are said to be auspicious and joyful; buffaloes of this nature are also similarly fruitful. ||3||

Thus ends the ninety-second chapter in the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western Provinces, on the Brihat Samhita composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira. ||92||

## Now begins the Ninety-Third Chapter

### Omens: The Behavior of Horses

Excretion is not auspicious if it occurs while the horse is in a seated position or toward the rear; likewise, a flaming sensation <note>original: "jvalanam" - likely referring to a burning heat, supernatural glow, or metaphorical "fire" in the limbs</note> on the left side is inauspicious, though elsewhere it is favorable. A burning sensation over the entire body indicates a lack of growth for the horses, as do sparks of fire or the appearance of smoke for two years. ||1||

The inner quarters of the palace face destruction if the penis is inflamed; the treasury meets its end if the belly is burning. If the anus or tail is affected, there will be defeat; however, a glow in the mouth or the head brings victory. ||2||

A glow on the shoulders, the seat, or the mane leads to victory, while a burning in the feet is said to portend imprisonment. Smoke appearing in front of the forehead or chest leads to defeat, but a bright glow in those areas leads to victory. ||3||

At night, a glow in the nostrils, the snout, the head, the tear-ducts, or the eyes leads to victory. For horses that are the color of Butea flowers <note>pale red/orange</note>, copper, black, or variegated, a glow like a parrot’s green or white is always desirable. ||4||

Aversion to fodder and water, falling down, sweating without cause, trembling, blood falling from the mouth, or the appearance of smoke; sleeplessness or hostility at night; drowsiness, laziness, or brooding during the day; exhaustion and keeping the head cast downward—this behavior is considered undesirable for horses. ||5||

If a horse mounts other horses, or if a horse equipped with a saddle and gear—especially a royal mount or one ready for battle—meets with an accident, it is not auspicious. ||6||

A neighing sound like a crane <note>original: "krauñcha"</note> portends the death of a Brahmin; but if the horse neighs with a steady neck, looking upward, with a pleasant, loud, and resonant tone as if joyful, or while holding a mouthful of fodder, it is favorable. ||7||

If, while the horse neighs, there are nearby objects such as a full vessel, curd, a Brahmin, a deity, perfumes, flowers, fruits, or gold, or any other divine and pleasant thing, victory is near. ||8||

Horses that show delight in food, drink, or the bit, or those that whinny at the sight of their master, or those whose gaze is fixed toward the right side, grant the fruits of desired goals. ||9||

Those that strike the earth with their left hooves portend a journey for the master. If they neigh while looking at the glowing twilight, it leads to imprisonment or defeat. ||10||

If they neigh excessively, shed their hair, remain constantly asleep, or "speak" <note>make unusual vocalizations</note> during a march; if they shed their coat, have a piteous or hoarse voice, or are seen swallowing dust, it portends fear. ||11||

Those that lie on their right side like the ocean <note>calm and vast</note>, or stand with their right hoof raised, bring victory. A wise man should apply these results to other vehicles/mounts as well, as far as they are applicable. ||12||

When the king mounts, if the horse is well-behaved, neighs toward another horse following the procession, or touches its own right side with its mouth, that horse quickly increases the fortune of its master. ||13||

A horse that urinates or defecates repeatedly, does not move forward even when struck, is afraid of its duties, or has tearful eyes, does not portend well for the master. ||14||

Thus has been described the behavior of horses; hereafter, I shall speak of elephants—their behavior regarding the shaking, breaking, or withering of their tusks. ||15|| (Thus ends the eighth chapter in the General Omens section, titled "The Behavior of Horses.")

->Thus ends the ninety-third chapter in the Brihat Samhita of Shri Varahamihira. ||93||<-

If the excretion (dung) of horses produces a glow (smoke with light) and it occurs in the western part of the horse's seat or on the left side, it is inauspicious; in other places, it is auspicious. A glow in all limbs of the horse is not a cause for the horse's growth. For two years...

If sparks of fire or smoke emerge from the horse's body, it likewise causes destruction. ||11|| If the horse’s penis appears inflamed or glowing <note>The text uses 'pradipta' (glowing/inflamed), likely referring to an omen of unnatural heat or light</note>, it signifies the destruction of the inner harem; if the belly glows, the king's treasury will be destroyed; and if the anus or tail glows, it leads to defeat. If the horse’s mouth and head glow, it signifies victory for the king. ||12|| If there is a glow in the horse’s shoulders, the seat <note>the area where the rider sits</note>, or the lower shoulders, the king attains victory. A glow in the feet is a cause for the master’s imprisonment. Smoke appearing on the chest, forehead, eyes, or both arms brings defeat, while a glow in these areas brings victory. ||13|| At night, a glow in the horse’s nostrils, snout, forehead, tear ducts, or eyes is a cause for victory. Furthermore, the movements of horses colored like the Palasha flower <note>bright orange-red</note>, copper, black, camphor, parrot-green, or white are always victorious. ||14|| A horse’s strong aversion to grass and water, sweating or trembling without cause, blood coming from the mouth, the production of smoke, insomnia and hostility at night, or lethargy, sleepiness, and brooding during the day—along with keeping the head downcast even when comfortable—these behaviors are not auspicious. ||15|| It is not favorable if another horse mounts a saddled horse, or if a healthy horse intended for a carriage or fully decorated meets with a sudden mishap. ||16|| The neighing of a horse that keeps its neck steady like a crane and holds its head high is a cause for the slaughter of the enemy. If the horses' mouths are filled with foam and they let out a glossy, high-pitched sound as if joyful, that too causes the slaughter of the enemy. ||17|| A horse that neighs near a full vessel, curd, a Brahmin <term>Vipra: a member of the priestly class</term>, a deity, perfumes, flowers, fruits, or gold is a bringer of victory. ||18|| Horses that joyfully accept food, drink, and the bridle, or those that happily accept a small portion of what the master likes, and those whose gaze is directed toward the right side, grant desired results. ||19|| Horses that strike the earth with their left foot cause the master to go to a foreign land. If horses neigh at twilight while facing a "blazing" direction <note>the direction where the sun has set or an unlucky quarter</note>, it leads to the master’s imprisonment and is also a cause for defeat. ||20|| If a horse neighs excessively, bristles its hair, and sleeps, it indicates an upcoming journey. A horse that makes a piteous sound like a donkey and eats dust is a cause for fear. ||21|| A horse that sleeps on its right side like a *Samudra* <note>original: "समुद्र" - here referring to a specific auspicious vessel or posture</note> or stands with its right foot well-raised is a cause for the master’s victory. Wise men say these same results apply to other vehicles/mounts as well. ||22|| When the king has mounted, if the horse is disciplined, follows the direction of the journey, neighs upon hearing another horse, or touches its own right side with its mouth, that horse quickly gathers wealth for its master. ||23|| If a horse, even without being beaten, repeatedly urinates and defecates, walks crookedly, is frightened without reason, or has tears in its eyes, it does not portend well for the groom. ||24|| The subject of horses' movements has been told; now I shall speak of the results of elephants' tusks trembling, breaking, or becoming soiled. ||25||

# Now begins the Ninety-Fourth Chapter
## Omens: The Gestures of Elephants

To determine the proper place to cut an elephant's tusk, measure the circumference at the root. Leave a length equal to twice that circumference from the root and cut the remaining portion. For elephants living in marshy lands <note>original: "anūpa-caraṇām"</note>, leave a little more; for those living in the mountains, leave a little less. ||1||

If, upon cutting the tusk, marks resembling the *Shrivatsa* <note>a mystical mark or knot</note>, the *Vardhamana* <note>a ritual water vessel or earthen bowl</note>, an umbrella, a banner, or a fly-whisk are seen, it foretells health, victory, increase in wealth, and happiness. ||2||

If the marks resemble weapons, victory is assured. If the mark resembles a *Nandyavarta* <note>a complex labyrinthine symbol</note>, one recovers a lost kingdom. If it looks like a clod of earth, one gains a territory that was previously possessed. ||3||

If the mark resembles a woman, it portends one's own destruction. If a mallet <note>original: "mudgara"</note> appears, a son will be born. A pot <note>original: "kumbha"</note> signifies the discovery of treasure, while a staff <note>original: "daṇḍa"</note> indicates obstacles to a journey. ||4||

If the marks look like a lizard, a monkey, or a snake, the king will fall under the power of his enemies. If they resemble a vulture, an owl, a crow, or a hawk, it foretells a plague or great mortality among the people. ||5||

A mark resembling a noose or a headless trunk <note>original: "kabandha"</note> portends the death of the king. If the cut surface is bloody, there will be a popular uprising. If it is black, dusky, rough, or foul-smelling, it is inauspicious. ||6||

A cut that is white, smooth, fragrant, and glossy brings good fortune. The effects of a tusk breaking naturally are the same as those described for the falling of withered fruits. ||7||

The root, middle, and tip of the tusk are presided over by the Gods, the Demons, and Humans respectively. The results of marks in these areas manifest quickly, in a medium timeframe, or after a long time, according to their position. ||8||

The breaking of the right tusk portends the ruin of the king, his country, and his army. The breaking of the left tusk destroys the king's sons, his priest, the stars <note>astrological portents</note>, forest-dwellers, and the leaders of the army. ||9||

If both tusks break, one should predict the total destruction of the king's lineage. If the breaking occurs during a favorable Ascendant <note>term: "Lagna" - the rising sign of the zodiac</note>, lunar day, or lunar mansion, the evil is mitigated and good increases; otherwise, the evil is compounded. ||10||

If an elephant strikes its tusk against trees with milky sap, or those bearing fruit and flowers, or against a riverbank, and the left or middle part of the tusk is slightly chipped or broken, it signifies the destruction of enemies. Any other kind of breaking is unfavorable. ||11||

An elephant that stumbles in its gait without cause, whose ears tremble with fear, who looks dejected, breathes softly but deeply, rests its trunk on the ground, closes its eyes quickly, sleeps excessively, acts contrary to its nature, eats unwholesome things, or frequently voids blood or excrement, creates fear and indicates coming danger. ||12||

Conversely, an elephant that joyfully crushes anthills, stumps, shrubs, or trees, whose eyes are bright, who moves with a quick and steady gait in the direction of a planned journey, who raises its trunk high, and who trumpets or sprays water-mist at the time of putting on its girth-harness, brings victory—especially if it wraps its trunk around its right tusk. ||13||

If an elephant is dragged into the water by a crocodile, it portends the destruction of the king. But if the elephant seizes the crocodile and pulls it out of the water onto the land, it brings prosperity to the sovereign. ||14||

(Thus ends the ninth chapter in the section on all omens, titled "The Gestures of Elephants")

->Thus ends the 94th Chapter of the Brihat Samhita by Shri Varahamihira.<-

<margin>Hindi Commentary: The length to be left at the root of the tusk is twice the circumference. For marsh-dwelling elephants, leave more; for mountain-dwellers, leave less. Signs like the Shrivatsa bring health and victory. Weapon-shaped signs bring victory, while Nandyavarta signs bring back lost lands.</margin>

# Varahi Samhita

<page-num>308</page-num>
->Varahi Samhita<-

And if a mark shaped like a clod of earth appears, it signifies the recovery of previously held territory. ||3|| If a mark resembling a woman appears, it signifies one's own destruction. If a mark rises resembling a *bhringara* <gloss>a ceremonial water vessel or pitcher</gloss>, it signifies the birth of a son. A mark shaped like a pot indicates the acquisition of gems, and a mark shaped like a staff indicates obstacles in a journey. ||4|| If marks resembling a chameleon, a monkey, or a snake appear, it signifies famine, disease, and falling into the power of an enemy. If marks resembling a vulture, an owl, a crow, or a hawk appear, a plague or pestilence falls upon the people. ||5||

If, upon cutting the elephant's ivory, a mark of a noose or a headless torso <term>Kabandha: a headless trunk, often considered an ill omen in Vedic astrology</term> appears, it signifies the death of the king. If blood flows out, it signifies calamity for the people. If the ivory is black, livid <gloss>a mixture of yellow and black</gloss>, rough, or foul-smelling, it is inauspicious. ||6|| If the cut in the tusk is even, white, fragrant, or glossy, it is auspicious. If the elephant's tusk decays or becomes soiled, the result should be known as the same as that of a broken tusk. ||7||

Gods, demons, and humans reside respectively in the root, middle, and tip <gloss>the point</gloss> of the elephant's tusk. I shall describe in order their great, middling, and minor soft results, and whether the effects occur quickly, in a medium timeframe, or after a long time. ||8|| Now, the results of a broken tusk are described: If the right tusk breaks in the portion belonging to the gods, demons, or humans, it causes rebellion or turmoil for the king, the country, and the army. If the left tusk breaks, it causes the death of the son, the priest, and the elephant-driver <gloss>mahout</gloss>, along with forest-dwellers and those who clear the land. ||9||

If both tusks break, they reveal the total destruction of the king's lineage; however, if the *Lagna* <note>the rising sign or ascendant</note>, the lunar day, and the lunar mansion are favorable, they increase the auspicious results and diminish the inauspicious ones. ||10|| If the middle part of the left tusk is shattered or broken against an ivory object, a milky tree, fruit, flowers, atop a tree, or on a riverbank, it signifies the destruction of enemies. If it happens otherwise, the result is the opposite. ||11||

If an elephant's gait suddenly falters <gloss>stumbles</gloss>, if its ears stop flapping, if it becomes very dejected and drops its trunk to the ground, if it takes soft <gloss>slow</gloss> and long breaths, if its gaze becomes startled or bud-like and it falls asleep, if it begins to walk crookedly, eats harmful food, or passes only blood or excrement, then that elephant brings fear to its master. ||12||

If an elephant, by its own will, while crushing anthills, stumps <gloss>branchless trees</gloss>, shrubs, bushes <gloss>small trees</gloss>, and trees, looks joyful, moves its mouth up and down, walks quickly in a zigzag manner, and at the time of tightening the saddle during the day, repeatedly sprays water droplets, trumpets, or becomes rutted <note>Mada: a state of hormonal aggression and excitement in male elephants</note> at that very moment, or wraps its trunk around the right tusk, it brings victory. ||13|| If a crocodile seizes the elephant and pulls it into the water, it causes the death of the king; but if the elephant seizes the crocodile and brings it out of the water, it causes the expansion of the king's territory. ||14||

# Chapter Ninety-Five

## On Omens: The Character of Crows
<note>original: "Kaka-charitram"</note>

For those in the eastern regions, a crow appearing on the right is auspicious, while a <term>Karayika</term><note>a specific species of small crane or water-bird</note> is auspicious on the left. In other regions, the opposite may hold true based on local tradition. ||1||

In the month of <term>Vaishakha</term><note>April-May</note>, if a crow builds its nest in an undamaged tree, it grants plenty and prosperity. If built in forbidden, thorny, or withered trees, it foretells famine and fear in that land. ||2||

If the nest is on an eastern branch, the first rains will come in autumn; if on a western branch, the rains will be late. If on the southern or northern branches, the rains will be moderate; if at the very top of the tree, the rains will be excellent. ||3||

If in the southeast <note>original: "shikhi-dishi", the direction of Agni/Fire</note>, there will be scattered rain in circles; in the southwest, the autumn crops will reach completion. In the remaining directions (North and East), there will be plenty, but in the northwest, there will be an abundance of mice. ||4||

If a crow nests in autumn clouds <note>likely referring to high, wispy formations</note>, thickets, creepers, grain, palaces, houses, or low ground, that region will become desolate, suffering from thieves, excessive rain, and disease. ||5||

Having two, three, or four chicks brings plenty; five chicks indicates a change in the ruler. The scattering of eggs, or the production of only a single egg, does not lead to well-being. ||6||

Crows with the color of thieves <note>dark/sooty</note> indicate robbers; variegated colors indicate death; white crows indicate fear of fire. Crows with physical defects indicate fear of famine, while healthy crows indicate good fortune. ||7||

If crows gather in the middle of a village without cause and caw, there is fear of hunger. If they caw with angry, circular movements in groups, it indicates an impending attack or conflict between factions. ||8||

Fearless crows that strike people with their beaks, wings, or feet bring an increase in enemies. If they wander at night, it brings the destruction of the people. ||9||

Crows flying in circles to the left in the sky indicate fear from one's own people; circles to the right indicate fear from enemies. If they fly in great agitation, it foretells a violent windstorm. ||10||

Crows with upturned faces and moving wings are omens of fear on a journey; if they walk slowly, they steal grain. If they perch on parts of an army, it foretells war and plunder by enemy forces. ||11||

If a crow places ashes, bones, hair, or feathers on a bed, it foretells the death of the master. If it drops jewels, flowers, and such, it indicates the birth of a son or a woman's pregnancy. ||12||

If its mouth is full, it indicates gain of wealth; similarly with sand, grain, wet clay, or flowers. However, it is fearful if a crow carries away vessels from a human settlement. ||13||

If a crow pecks at a vehicle, weapon, shoes, or the shadow of an umbrella, it foretells death. If it "worships" <note>honors/touches gently</note> these items, it brings honor; if it leaves droppings on them, it brings the arrival of food. ||14||

If it brings an object, one will gain that item; if it carries it away, it may mean the loss of life. If it brings a yellow object, one gains gold; if cotton, clothes; if white, silver. ||15||

Crows perching on trees with milky sap, Arjuna trees, or Vanjula trees, or on the banks and sandbanks of rivers, indicate rain during the monsoon. If they bathe in dust or water out of season, it foretells a period of bad weather. ||16||

A crow making a harsh sound while entering the hollow of a tree brings great fear. If it looks at water while cawing, or caws back at the clouds, it brings rain. ||17||

An agitated crow with burnt-looking wings, pecking at a branch, creates a risk of fire; or if it brings red objects, burnt grass, or wood into the house. ||18||

If a crow looks toward the East or other directions while facing the sun and caws at a house, the householder will face fear from the king, bonds from thieves, or quarrels, as well as fear for their cattle. ||19||

If it looks toward the peaceful East and caws, it indicates the arrival of a king's official, the gain of gold, and the enjoyment of rice and molasses. ||20||

In the Southeast, it indicates gain of fire-related livelihoods, women, or excellent metals. In the South, it indicates a meal of beans and pulses, and association with musicians. ||21||

In the Southwest, it indicates the arrival of messengers, tools, curd, oil, and meat dishes. In the West, it indicates the gain of meat, wine, liquor, grain, and sea-gems. ||22||

In the Northwest, it indicates the gain of weapons, lotuses, creepers, and fruits. In the North, it indicates the eating of supreme food and the gain of horses and clothes.

<vocab>Shakuna (Omens), Kaka-charitram (Character of Crows), Subhiksha (Plenty/Prosperity), Durbhiksha (Famine), Aindri (East), Agneyi (Southeast), Nairriti (Southwest), Maruti (Northwest), Saumya (North)</vocab>

# The Varahi Samhita

### Chapter on the Omens of Crows (Continued)

... [23] If a crow is seen in the northeast direction, there will be an acquisition of ghee-filled vessels and oxen. Such is the result for the master of the house when the crow stays in the sixth house <note>This refers to the astrological division of the house or direction</note>. [24] If, while one is departing on a journey, a crow touches one's ear, it indicates safety but not the successful completion of the task. If it cries out while facing the traveler and then turns back, the traveler should cancel the journey. [25] If a cow lows on the left side or the right side of the traveler while a crow is cawing, it indicates the theft of wealth; if the opposite occurs, it indicates the attainment of wealth. [26] If a crow caws repeatedly on the left side of a traveler moving in a favorable direction, it leads to the success of wealth; for those in the eastern regions, the same applies to the right side. [27] A crow on the left moving in an unfavorable direction and cawing creates obstacles to the journey. If it stays in that same spot, it tells the fruit of whatever was desired for the journey. [28] Having cawed on the right, if it then caws on the left, one's desires will be fulfilled. If it caws in response and then flies quickly ahead, there will be a very great gain of wealth. [29] If it caws in response and then flies to the right behind the traveler, it indicates a wound or bloodshed <note>literally: "maker of blood"</note>. Standing on one leg, looking at the sun, and cawing in front of the traveler, it causes bloodshed. [30] If the crow <note>original: "balibhuk" - eater of offerings</note>, standing on one leg and looking at the sun, scratches its feathers with its beak, it foretells the death of a great person. [31] If it caws peacefully in a field filled with crops, there will be an acquisition of land with crops. If it caws with agitated movements at the boundary of the land, it causes distress to the traveler. [32] On trees that are very glossy, with fresh leaves, flowers, and fragrant, sweet fruits, or on trees that are milky and pleasant, the crow's caw brings wealth. [33] On ripened crops, grassy plots, houses, palaces, mansions, or green areas, or on heaps of grain and auspicious objects, the cawing crow grants wealth and gold. [34] If it stands on a cow's tail or an anthill, there will be a sight of a snake. If it caws while standing on a buffalo, a fever will soon follow; if on a bush, the result is small. [35] There is an obstacle to the work if it is on a heap of grass to the left, or if it stays on a bone. If the crow is scorched by fire from above or struck by lightning, death occurs. [36] On a thorny tree in the north, there is success in work but also a quarrel. On a thorny tree generally, there is a quarrel; if the tree is entwined with creepers, there is imprisonment. [37] If the top of the tree is broken, there is injury to limbs; if the crow stays on a withered tree, there is a quarrel. If it stays on cow dung, whether in front or behind, wealth is obtained. [38] If it caws while standing on the limb of a dead man, it creates fear of death. If it breaks a bone with its beak while cawing, it leads to the breaking of one's own bones. [39] If it caws with a rope, bone, wood, thorn, or hair in its mouth, there will be fear of snakes, disease, tusks <note>wild animals</note>, thieves, weapons, and fire, respectively. [40] If it has a white flower or impure meat in its mouth, the traveler's desired wealth is achieved. If it shakes its wings with its face turned upwards and croaks repeatedly, it indicates an obstacle. [41] If it caws while holding a chain, a leather strap, or a creeper, there is imprisonment. Standing on a stone, it brings fear and a struggle with an unprecedentedly large force. [42] If crows are seen transferring food to one another's mouths, there is great satisfaction. If a pair of crows caws simultaneously, it is known to indicate the gain of a woman. [43] If a crow stands on a full pot carried on a woman's head, there is the acquisition of a woman and wealth. If it strikes the pot, there is danger to a son; if it just touches the pot, there is the acquisition of limbs <note>likely meaning physical health or a new family member</note>. [44] At the time of pitching a camp, a crow cawing with moving wings indicates a change to another location; with still wings, it indicates only fear. [45] If crows enter the army with vultures and hawks carrying meat, and they are not hostile to each other, there is friendship; if they are hostile, there is war with enemies. [46] If the crow stands on a pig, there is imprisonment; if on a pig smeared with mud, there is the acquisition of wealth. On a donkey or camel, some say it brings safety, but others say death on a donkey. [47] If it stands on a horse, there is the gain of a vehicle; if it caws while following the traveler, there is a fall of blood. Others following the traveler...

...eyes of fire. ॥ 48 ॥ When the circle of directions is divided into thirty-two parts, whatever has been specified for each must be applied as the result of merit or fault for those wishing to travel. ॥ 49 ॥ The sound *'Ka'* made by a crow staying in its own nest is said to be fruitless. *'Kava'* is for self-satisfaction, while the sound *'Ka'* <note>original: "क इति"</note> indicates the arrival of a dear friend. ॥ 50 ॥ *'Kara'* indicates a quarrel; *'Kuru-Kuru'* indicates joy; *'Kata-Kata'* indicates a meal of curd and rice. The sounds *'Keke'* or *'Kuku'* are said by travelers to mean the gain of wealth. ॥ 51 ॥ *'Khare-Khare'* indicates the arrival of a traveler; *'Khakha-Khe'* indicates death for the traveler. The sound *'Akhal-Khal'* forbids departure but indicates immediate rain. ॥ 52 ॥ *'Kaka'* indicates an obstacle; *'Kakat-Ti'* indicates spoiled food. *'Kava-Kava'* is a sign of affection, while *'Kagaku'* indicates imprisonment. ॥ 53 ॥ *'Karaka'* sounds indicate rain; *'Gudavat'* <note>sweet like jaggery</note> indicates fear; *'Vada'* indicates the acquisition of clothes. *'Kalaya'* indicates the meeting of a Shudra <note>the laboring class</note> with Brahmins <note>the priestly class</note>. ॥ 54 ॥ *'Phad'* indicates the attainment of fruit or seeing a fruit-bearer; *'Tad'* indicates blows or assault. The sound *'Stri'* indicates the gain of a woman; *'Gad'* indicates cattle; *'Pud'* indicates flowers. ॥ 55 ॥ *'Taku-Takvi'* is for war; *'Guhu'* for fear of fire; *'Kata-Kata'* for a quarrel. *'Takuli'*, *'Chinti-Chi'*, *'Kekeke'*, and *'Puranje'* are for misfortune. ॥ 56 ॥ These same results mentioned for the crow's cries and movements apply to a pair of crows, to other wild birds, and to dogs or other animals with upper tusks/teeth. ॥ 57 ॥ The reversal of behavior between land and water creatures during the rainy season indicates heavy rain; at other times, it indicates danger. Honey found inside a house soon makes it empty <note>deserted</note>; a blue fly settling on the head also indicates death. ॥ 58 ॥ Ants dropping their eggs in water indicate a cessation of rain; when they carry them from low ground to a tree or high ground, they foretell rain. ॥ 59 ॥ The result of an omen occurring at the start of a task should be known that very day; these should be considered certain. At the time of beginning a sacrifice or entering a place, a sneeze is never considered auspicious. ॥ 60 ॥ For a king who honors omens, they foretell the ripening of fortune, the removal of obstacles, the protection of the foundation, the arrival of allies, the success of desires, and health. ॥ 61 ॥ Some say a bird's cry beyond a distance of two miles <note>term: Krosha; approx. 2 miles</note> is fruitless. If the first omen is inauspicious, the king should perform five or six breath-control exercises <note>Pranayama</note>; if the second is inauspicious, sixteen; if the third is inauspicious, he should return to his palace. ॥ 62 ॥

->(Thus ends the tenth chapter named 'The Cries of the Crow' within the General Omens)<-

## Thus ends the ninety-fifth chapter in the Brihat Samhita composed by Sri Varahamihira. ॥ 95 ॥

For the inhabitants of the eastern regions, a crow being on the right is auspicious, while a *Karayika* <note>a specific type of bird, likely a crane or woodpecker</note> being on the left is auspicious. A crow on the left and a *Karayika* on the right is auspicious. One should know the boundaries of the East and other directions from popular tradition. ॥ 1 ॥ If in the month of Vaishakha <note>April-May</note> a crow builds a nest on a tree free of disturbances, it brings abundance and welfare; however, if it builds a nest on a lowly or thorny tree, there is fear of famine. ॥ 2 ॥ In the autumn, if the crow's nest is on a branch facing East, rain occurs first in the West. If the nest is on top of the tree in the South or North, there will be heavy rain. ॥ 3 ॥ If it is in the South-East <note>Agni-kone</note>, there will be scattered rain; if in the South-West <note>Nairitya</note>, the autumn crops will be good. In the remaining two directions, there will be abundance, but if the nest is in the North-West <note>Vayu-kone</note>, there will be many rats. ॥ 4 ॥ Reeds, sacrificial grass...

However, if there are five, it indicates the takeover of the territory by another king. If the eggs are destroyed or if only one egg is produced, it is not auspicious. ||6|| If the color of the crow's chicks resembles fragrant substances <note>likely referring to a pale or yellowish hue</note>, there is a fear of thieves; a three-colored appearance signifies death; white signifies fire; and if they appear fearful or agitated, there is a fear of famine. ||7|| If crows gather without reason and make a loud noise, it portends famine; if they stand in a circular formation, it signifies anger/strife; and if they stand in distinct groups, it indicates an uprising or calamity. ||8|| If crows, becoming fearless, strike humans with their beaks, wings, or claws, it signifies an increase in enemies; and if they wander about at night, it leads to the destruction of the people. ||9|| If crows, while flying in the sky, circle to the right and then move from the west in a reverse-circle <note>counter-clockwise</note>, it brings fear to oneself; if they fly about in extreme agitation, it indicates a whirlwind or stormy weather. ||10|| Crows that lift their faces upward, flap their wings, steal food, and remain on the path are a cause for fear of famine and are generally ominous. A crow sitting on the parts of an army <note>soldiers or equipment</note> indicates impending war. If the wings of crows are as pitch black as a cuckoo's, it signifies theft. ||11|| If a crow drops ash, bones, hair <note>original: "lesh" interpreted here as remnants/waste</note>, or withered leaves onto a bed, it causes the death of the husband; however, if it drops jewels, flowers, and such, it heralds the birth of a son or daughter. ||12|| If a crow arrives with its beak full of sand, grain, wet mud, flowers, or fruit, it indicates a gain of wealth. But if a crow carries away a vessel from a human dwelling, it is a sign of fear. ||13|| If a crow pecks at a vehicle, weapon, shoe, umbrella, shadow, or a person's limb, death occurs. If one honors them, they receive honor; and if a crow drops excrement on someone, it signifies a gain of food. ||14|| Whatever object a crow picks up and brings from somewhere, a gain of that very object occurs; and whatever object it takes away, that object will be lost. From a yellow object, gold is gained, and from white cloth made of cotton, silver is gained or lost <note>depending on whether the crow brings or takes it</note>. ||15|| If groups of crows sit on an old tree, an Arjuna tree, a Vanjula tree, or on both banks and sandbanks of a river and make noise, rain will fall. If they bathe in water or dust out of season, it indicates a period of bad weather. ||16|| If a crow sits in the hollow of a tree and makes a harsh sound, it is a great omen of fear. If it looks at water and makes a sound, or sounds like a cloud <note>deep/rumbling</note>, it is a bringer of rain. ||17|| If a crow, flapping its wings and sitting on a tree, appears glowing and agitated, pecks its own limbs, brings a red object into the house, or places burnt grass or wood there, there is a fear of fire. ||18|| If a crow looks toward the eastern and other directions in the homes of householders and makes a sound while facing the sun, the master of the house faces fear from the government <note>original: "rajbhaya"</note>, fear of thieves, imprisonment, quarrels, and fear caused by animals. ||19|| If a crow makes a sound while looking toward the peaceful East, it signifies an encounter with a government official, the gain of gold, and the receiving of Shali rice, food, and jaggery to eat. ||20|| If a crow speaks while looking toward the peaceful Southeast <term>Agneya Kon|The corner associated with the fire god, Agni</term>, there will be a gain of livelihood through fire (such as goldsmiths or blacksmiths), a young woman, or excellent metals. If it is the opposite, wealth is obtained ||26|| If the crow, while making a sound on the left side of the traveler, moves repeatedly in a natural direction <note>Sanskrit: Anuloma; with the grain or clockwise</note>, wealth is obtained; for residents of the East, this same result occurs in the South ||27|| If the crow, situated on the left side while making a sound, moves in a contrary direction <note>Sanskrit: Pratiloma; against the grain</note>—that is, comes toward the traveler—it creates obstacles in the journey and says that the desired fruit of the journey will be achieved while sitting at home ||28|| If it first sounds on the right and then on the left, the desired result is obtained, and if it moves quickly ahead of the traveler while sounding, much wealth is gained ||29|| If, after making a counter-sound, it goes quickly from the back toward the South, or stands on one leg in the front part while looking at the sun and sounding, then blood will flow from the body of the traveler ||30|| If a crow, standing on one leg and looking at the sun, scratches its feathers with its mouth (beak), it reveals the killing of some prominent man ahead ||31|| If a crow makes a good sound in a peaceful direction of a field filled with grain, then land filled with grain is obtained; if it makes a particular sound at the edge of the village boundary while acting agitated, it causes distress to the traveler ||32|| A crow sitting on a tree bent with tender leaves, sprouts, flowers, and fruits, or on a fragrant or sweet tree, or on a milky, wound-less, well-situated, and beautiful tree, accomplishes the task while sounding ||33|| If a crow sounds while sitting on a dark field covered with ripe grain and new grass, a palace, an attic, a green-colored place, a high heap of grain, or an auspicious object, then wealth arrives ||34|| If a crow speaks while sitting on the tail of a cow or on an anthill, a snake will be seen. It is said that if a crow breaks a bone with its beak, it portends the breaking of a bone for the observer. || 39 || If it makes a sound while holding a rope, bone, wood, thorny objects, hollow/worthless items, or hair in its mouth, then in that order, the traveler faces fear from snakes, disease, fanged creatures, thieves, weapons, and fire. || 40 || If the crow speaks while holding a white flower or impure meat in its mouth, it fulfills the traveler's desired goal; however, if it repeatedly cries out while shaking its wings and looking upward, it acts as an obstacle. || 41 || If a crow makes a sound while grasping a chain, a leather strap <note>original: "varatra" - specifically a rope used for elephants</note>, or a vine, it indicates imprisonment. If the crow pecks the pot with its beak, it signifies calamity for her son, but if it drops excrement on the pot, food will be obtained. || 44 || If a crow flaps its wings and cries out at the time of setting up camp, it indicates another location—meaning the army should not stay here but at a different spot; however, if the crow cries with still wings, it merely reveals fear. || 45 || If groups of crows accompanied by vultures and kites enter an army camp without carrying meat, and they are peaceful, it signifies the joy of enemies <note>or success over enemies</note>; if they are aggressive, war follows. || 46 || A crow sitting on a pig signifies imprisonment; sitting on two pigs smeared with mud signifies the acquisition of wealth. Sitting on a donkey or camel is auspicious, though some say sitting on a donkey portends the death of the traveler. || 47 || If a crow cries while sitting on a horse, it signifies the acquisition of a vehicle/mount; if it cries while following behind, blood will be shed. All the results previously mentioned for crows apply equally to ravens. Furthermore, the omens for all wild or domestic tusked/fanged animals are the same as those described for dogs. || 57 || During the rainy season, if land-dwelling creatures enter the water and aquatic creatures come onto the land, it indicates heavy rain; however, at any other time, this signifies danger. In this manner, all omens should be considered. A sneeze is not considered auspicious at the start of any work or at the time of entering a new home. || 60 || Scholars of the science of omens, having interpreted signs in this way, should clearly explain to the King—who bestows honors—the arrival of good fortune, success without obstacles, the protection of the capital, the gaining of allies, the fulfillment of desires, and freedom from disease. || 61 || Some scholars, such as the sage Kashyapa and others, say that the sound of an omen becomes fruitless after one has traveled a distance of one *kosh* <note>A traditional Indian unit of distance, roughly 2 miles</note>. If the first omen is inauspicious, one should perform five or six *Pranayamas* <term>Pranayama: yogic breath control</term>. If the second is inauspicious, perform sixteen *Pranayamas* <gloss>1</gloss>. If the third omen is also inauspicious, one should not proceed with the journey and should return home. || 62 ||

->### The Supplementary Chapter on Omens<-

**One who knows the secrets of the elements should predict results after understanding the direction, region, physical movement, sound, day, lunar mansion, moment, planetary hour, the rising sign, and the strength or weakness of long-term, fixed, or mixed factors. || 1 ||** They describe two types of outcomes: those concerning things already present (Fixed) and those concerning things to come (Arrivals). Matters involving kings, messengers, spies, things from other lands, and the arrival of relatives are called "Arrivals." || 2 || Matters such as hangings, seizures, food, thieves, fire, rain, festivals, the birth or death of a son, quarrels, and fear are "Fixed." If the rising sign and the Moon are in a fixed sign, the result is fixed; if in a movable sign, the result is movable. || 3 || In fixed locations like stone houses, temples, or near land and water, fixed works are successful. In movable places, movable works and "Arrivals" are successful. || 4 || Those birds that cry out while facing the "blazing" <note>The direction currently occupied by the sun</note> direction in watery signs or regions, or at the end of a fortnight, bring rain. Even an aquatic bird, when "quiet" <note>Facing a direction not occupied by the sun</note>, brings rain. || 5 || A bird crying out while facing the sun in the southeast direction, or during an fiery moment or region, indicates fear of fire. In the direction of Yama <note>South</note>, or in harsh rising signs or "thorns" <note>astrological quadrants</note>, or on a leafless tree...

The ratio is usually four parts retention and two parts exhalation for every one part inhalation.</note>

...on creepers, it indicates the act of a thief. || 6 || A domestic bird, excited in its voice and movement, sounding fierce and harsh while perched on a thorny tree in a sign or Ascendant <term>Lagna: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> ruled by Mars, or situated in the Southwest, indicates a quarrel if seen nearby. || 7 || If the Ascendant or the Moon is in a division <term>Navāṃśa: a one-ninth subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> ruled by Venus, and the bird cries facing downwards in an intermediate direction, it indicates a capture if it is "excited" <note>original: "dipta" - a technical term for an omen that is over-stimulated or ill-omened due to direction or intensity</note>; the same applies to the intermediate direction specified. || 8 || In a masculine sign or Ascendant, on an odd-numbered lunar day, a bird situated in its proper direction and "excited" is called "human-named." In such a case, the capture of men should be predicted; if among friends, a division of spoils occurs. || 9 || Similarly, if the Ascendant is in the sign or division of the Sun, or if the Sun itself is in the Ascendant, an excited bird indicates the exile of a prominent man; that is the cause. || 10 || At the commencement of all works, one should calculate the Ascendant from the position of the Sun. Prosperity or adversity should be declared according to the sequence of the calculation. || 11 || If the Sun is in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, the person is blind in the right eye; if the Moon is there, in the left eye. If the Sun is in the Ascendant and aspected by malefic planets, the person is totally blind, or a hunchback, or if in its own sign, deaf or dull-witted. || 12 || If a malefic planet is in the sixth house and aspected by another malefic, there will be a wound on the limb corresponding to that sign. Whatever signs or forms I have described at the time of birth should be considered here as well. || 13 || If a movable sign or division is rising, the name has two syllables; if a fixed sign, four syllables; and in dual signs, the name consists of three or five syllables. || 14 || The groups of consonants starting with 'ka' <note>The Varga system of Sanskrit phonetics</note> are assigned respectively to Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn. The eight semi-vowels and sibilants belong to the Moon, and the vowels starting with 'a' belong to the Sun. || 15 || The names of Agni, Varuna, Kumara, Vishnu, Indra, Indrani, and Brahma should be considered in order from the Sun; one should deduce the name using two or three syllables by one's own intelligence. || 16 || Their ages are: infant (breastfeeding), childhood, student, youth, middle-aged, old, and very old—corresponding to the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn respectively. || 17 ||

### Thus ends the 96th Chapter of the Illustrious Varāhamihira's Bṛhat Saṃhitā.

The wise who know the science of sounds should reveal all results after knowing the relative strength of direction, movement, place, voice, day, constellation, moment <term>Muhūrta</term>, hour <term>Horā</term>, ritual action <term>Karaṇa</term>, rising division, and whether the signs are long-lasting, fixed, or dual-natured. || 1 || All omens reveal the results of future and fixed actions based on the present situation; in this, kings, messengers, spies, and those arising from different countries are all present. These are well-known through one's own people and arrivals. || 2 || Connection, capture, food, thieves, fire, rain, festivals, offspring, slaughter, distress, and fear—all these are fixed categories. If the Moon is with a fixed sign or rising, fixed works become firm; those called "movable" are determined in movable houses. || 3 || If an omen occurs in a steady place, a stone, a temple, a shrine, the earth, or near water, then fixed works should be undertaken; if in a moving place, then movable works. || 4 || Omens that are "excited" in watery Ascendants, constellations, moments, or directions, or near water at the end of a fortnight, are all indicators of rain. Even the peaceful sound of a water-dwelling creature causes rain. || 5 || If a bird, stimulated by the Sun, makes a sound in the Southeast direction, in a specific moment or fire-prone place, it causes fear of fire. If a bird sounds while sitting on a thorny tree or a leafless vine during the <term>Viṣṭi</term> period or the rising of Aquarius or Capricorn, theft occurs. || 6 || Domestic birds sitting on thorny trees, whose voice and movement...
