# Chapter 96: The Interpretation of Omens (Continued)

If a bird cries out while being inflamed <note>The term "inflamed" (dipta) refers to a bird facing the sun or crying from a harsh direction</note> and is situated in a sign of Mars (Aries or Scorpio) in the ascendant toward the southwest, it indicates a cause for a quarrel. || 7 ||

If the ascendant is Cancer, or if the bird is in the sub-division <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for precision</term> of Taurus or Libra, and the bird cries while facing downward in an intermediate direction, it signifies a meeting with a woman of the type previously described for that direction. || 8 ||

When the ascendant is a masculine sign and the lunar day is odd (such as the 1st or 3rd), and a male bird situated in that direction cries while "inflamed," it indicates a gathering of men. If the masculine signs are friendly, a meeting with a eunuch is indicated. || 9 ||

In this manner, if the sign of the Sun (Leo) is in the ascendant or the sub-division, or if the Sun itself is situated there, the omens reveal the arrival of an important or noble man. || 10 ||

In all commenced works, one should count the ascendant from the sign occupied by the Sun; by counting sequentially, one should designate them as "Prosperity" or "Adversity" to predict the outcome. || 11 ||

If the Sun is in the twelfth house from the ascendant at that time, the person met will be blind in the right eye. If the Moon is in the twelfth house, they will be blind in the left eye. If the Sun in the ascendant is aspected by a malefic planet, the person will be blind. If the Sun is in Leo and aspected by a malefic, the person will be a hunchback, deaf, or dull-witted. || 12 ||

If a malefic planet (such as Mars) is in the sixth house from the ascendant and is aspected by another malefic, or if a sign is occupied by a malefic aspected by another, a wound will appear on the corresponding part of the person's body according to the limb represented by that zodiac sign. All the results regarding birth that I have previously described should be considered in this context as well. || 13 ||

If the ascendant and its sub-division are "movable," the name of the person involved consists of two syllables; if "fixed," four syllables; and if "dual-natured," the person has two names. || 14 ||

The five groups of five letters <note>The Varga system of the Sanskrit alphabet</note> belong respectively to Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn. The eight letters starting with 'Ya' belong to the Moon, and the sixteen vowels starting with 'A' belong to the Sun. || 15 ||

Under the dominion of the Sun, Moon, and the seven planets are respectively the deities Fire, Water, Kartikeya, Vishnu, Indra, Shachi, and Brahma. To know the name of a desired object, one should match these deities' names. However, one must use their own intelligence to determine if the name has two or three syllables based on the previously mentioned letter arrangements and the specific deity. || 16 ||

According to the state of the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn, the person indicated by the omen will be, respectively: a milk-drinking infant, a child, a youth under a vow <note>original: "kaumara"</note>, a young man, a middle-aged man, an old man, or an extremely aged person. || 17 ||

### Chapter Ninety-Seven

### On the Ripening of Omens
<note>The term used is 'Pāka-vicāraḥ'. In Sanskrit, 'Pāka' literally means cooking or ripening, referring here to the time it takes for a prophetic sign or omen to manifest its actual effect in the world.</note>

The effects of an omen involving the Sun manifest after a fortnight (fifteen days); for the Moon, after a month. For Mars, the effect occurs when it becomes retrograde. For Mercury, the result appears as soon as it becomes visible in the sky, and for Jupiter, it takes a full year. ##1## For Venus, the period is six months; for Saturn, it is one year; and for Rahu <note>original: "suradviṣo", meaning the enemy of the gods</note>, it is half a year. In the case of a solar eclipse, the effect is immediate, as it is for the appearance of the celestial dark spots known as the 'Tvaṣṭra' and 'Kīlaka' comets. ##2##

The effects of a Comet <note>original: "Dhūmaketu"</note> manifest in three months, while the 'White Comet' <note>original: "Śveta"</note> takes seven nights. A period of seven days applies to halos around the sun or moon <note>original: "Pariveṣa"</note>, rainbows, evening clouds, and 'cloud-needles' <note>thin, vertical cloud formations</note>. ##3##

When the seasons reverse (cold appearing as heat or vice versa), when flowers and fruits grow out of season, when the horizons seem to burn, when the nature of stable and moving things is swapped, or when there are birth defects—these omens ripen in six months. ##4## When things that should not be done are performed, when earthquakes occur, when festivals are neglected, when sacrifices are performed incorrectly, when things that cannot dry up (like perennial rivers) go dry, or when the flow of rivers changes—these take half a year. ##5##

When statues, granaries, or idols speak, laugh, tremble, or sweat; or when there are quarrels, rainbows, or thunderclaps—the results manifest in three months. ##6## An abundance of insects, rats, flies, or snakes; the strange behavior of wild animals, birds, or the wind; or the floating of a stone in water—these ripen in exactly three months. ##7##

When a dog gives birth in a forest, when wild animals enter a village, or when beehives appear on gateways or Indra’s banners—the effect takes a year or slightly more. ##8## Gatherings of jackals or vultures bring results in ten days. The sound of celestial trumpets, a sudden outcry, the appearance of anthills, or the cracking of the earth—these manifest their fruit in a fortnight. ##9##

The spontaneous ignition of fire without fuel, or the raining of ghee (clarified butter), oil, or fat—these ripen immediately. Public rumors and gossip take a month and a half. ##10## Omens involving umbrellas, banners, stupas, sacrificial fires, or seeds manifest in seven fortnights (three and a half months). Some authorities say the fruit of an omen involving an umbrella or a gateway appears in one month. ##11##

When naturally hostile creatures (like cats and mongooses) show affection for one another, or when a mouse associates with them; or when strange sounds are heard in the sky—the result comes in one month. ##12## The appearance of a 'City of Gandharvas' <note>a mirage or Fata Morgana</note> takes a month. Changes in the taste of liquids, the transformation of gold, or when the horizons are clouded by dust and smoke—these also have a one-month ripening period. ##13##

The ripening periods for the lunar mansions <note>term: Nakṣatras; the 27 divisions of the sky</note> starting from Aśvinī are: nine, eight, ten, six, three, and three months respectively. For Āśleṣā, the result is immediate. ##14## Starting from Maghā <note>original: "Pitryān"</note>, the periods are: one month, six months, six months, three months, half a month, eight months, three months, six months, one month, and one month. For the four mansions starting from Pūrvāṣāḍhā, the period is four months each. For Abhijit, the result is immediate. ##15## For the mansions starting from Śravaṇā, the ripening periods are seven, eight, one and a half, three, three, and five months respectively. ##16##

If the predicted effect does not appear within the stated time, it will manifest with double the intensity in the next period—unless it has been pacified through the donation of gold, gems, or cows, and through the performance of 'Shanti' <note>propitiatory rites</note> by learned priests. ##17##

Thus ends the Ninety-Seventh Chapter, titled "The Ripening of Omens," in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā of Varāhamihira.

# Chapter 97: With Hindi Commentary

The results of the Sun ripen in one fortnight <note>original: "Paksha"</note>, the Moon in one month, Mars in days according to its retrograde motion, Mercury as long as it remains risen, and Jupiter's results ripen in one year. || 1 ||

The results of Venus ripen in six months, Saturn in one year, the enemy of the gods (Rahu/Lunar Eclipse) in half a year, and a Solar Eclipse in one year. The results of the planet named Tvashta and the dark spots <note>original: "Tamas Kilaka," likely referring to sunspots or specific dark atmospheric phenomena</note> occur quickly. || 2 ||

The results of a comet <note>original: "Dhumaketu"</note> occur in three months, a white comet in seven nights, and the results of halos <note>original: "Parivesha"</note>, rainbows, twilight phenomena, and cloud-needles <note>original: "Abhrasuchi," a specific cloud formation</note> occur in 7 days (one week). || 3 ||

Reversal of cold and heat (heat in winter and cold in summer), fruits and flowers blooming out of season, the burning of the quarters <note>original: "Digdaha," a reddish glow on the horizon</note>, the alteration of the stable and the moving (stationary objects moving, or moving objects becoming still), and abnormalities in birth—the results of these occur in six months. || 4 ||

The performance of unprecedented acts (doing what was never done before, or doing something against one's will or by force), earthquakes, lack of festivals, the occurrence of the undesirable, the drying up of perennial lakes, and the reverse flow of rivers—the results of these matters occur in six months. || 5 ||

The results regarding pillars, huts made of earth, etc., idols of worship—if they weep, tremble, or sweat—or quarrels, rainbows, and calamities ripen in three months. || 6 ||

An abundance of insects, rats, flies, and snakes; the cries of deer and birds; the blowing of wind or the floating of a stone in water—the results of all these ripen in three months. || 7 ||

Dogs giving birth in the forest, wild animals entering the village, the appearance of honeycombs, or any calamity occurring to a ceremonial arch <note>original: "Torana"</note> or Indra's banner—the results of all these occur in one year or slightly more than a year. || 8 ||

The results of jackals and vultures gathering occur in ten days. The results of a trumpet sounding without being blown ripen very quickly. The results of a curse, an anthill, or the cracking of the earth can be known within one fortnight. || 9 ||

Fire burning without fuel and the raining of ghee, oil, or fat reach their ripening quickly, and the results of public scandal <note>original: "Janapavada"</note> ripen in one and a half months. || 10 ||

The ripening of results for umbrellas, funeral pyres, pillars, fire, and sown seeds occurs in seven fortnights; some say the results for umbrellas and ceremonial arches manifest in one month. || 11 ||

Mutual affection between creatures who are natural enemies, the sound of beings in the sky, and the friendship of cats and mongooses with rats—the results of these matters occur in one month. || 12 ||

The appearance of a city of Gandharvas <note>a mirage or Fata Morgana</note>, abnormalities in tastes, or abnormalities in gold—the results of these occur in one month. If all directions are covered by banners, houses, dust, and smoke, their results occur in one month. || 13 ||

The results of calamities in the constellations <note>original: "Nakshatras"</note> from Ashwini to Pushya ripen after nine, one, eighteen, one, one, six, three, and three months respectively. If any portent occurs in the star Ashlesha, the result is immediate. || 14 ||

If any calamity occurs in the constellations from Magha to Mula, their results ripen in one, six, six, three, half, eight, three, six, one, and one month respectively. The results for Purvashadha and Uttarashadha occur in four months, and the results for the star Abhijit occur quickly. || 15 ||

The results for the constellations starting from Shravana ripen in seven, eight, three and a half <note>original: "Adhyarddha"</note>, three, three, and five months respectively. || 16 ||

If the results do not appear in the stated time, then—

### Now begins the Ninety-Eighth Chapter
### The Qualities of the Asterisms (Nakshatras)

The number of stars [in each constellation] starting from Ashvini are: 3, 2, 6, 5, 3, 1, 5, 3, 6, 5, 2, 5, 1, 1, 5, 4, 3, 11, 2, 8, 2, 5, 100, 2, 8, and 32. The duration [of influence] is according to the measure of these stars. || 1–2 || <note>The text uses symbolic words for numbers: e.g., 'Shashi' (Moon) for 1, 'Paksha' (Wings/Sides) for 2, 'Agni' (Fire) for 3.</note>

The good or bad results of a marriage should be predicted based on the number of stars in the Nakshatra. Similarly, the recovery from a fever or other diseases should be declared in a number of days equal to the number of stars. || 3 ||

The presiding deities of the Nakshatras are: 1. The Ashvins, 2. Yama, 3. Agni, 4. Brahma, 5. The Moon, 6. Shiva, 7. Aditi, 8. Jupiter, 9. The Serpents, 10. The Ancestors (Pitris), 11. Bhaga, 12. Aryaman, 13. The Sun, 14. Tvashtar, 15. Vayu, 16. Indra and Agni, 17. Mitra, 18. Indra, 19. Nirriti, 20. The Waters (Varuna), 21. The Universal Gods (Vishvedevas), 22. Brahma, 23. Vishnu, 24. Vasu, 25. Varuna, 26. Ajaikapada, 27. Ahirbudhnya, and 28. Pushan. || 4–5 ||

The three "Uttara" stars <note>Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, and Uttara Bhadrapada</note> and Rohini are considered **Fixed** (Dhruva). In these, one should perform coronations, peace rites, planting trees, founding cities, religious deeds, sowing seeds, and other permanent undertakings. || 6 ||

Mula, Ardra (Shiva), Jyeshtha (Indra), and Ashlesha (Serpents) are **Sharp/Dreadful** (Tikshna). In these, success is found in: striking, incantations (mantras), summoning spirits (vetalas), imprisonment, killing, and creating divisions or separations. || 7 ||

The "Purva" stars <note>Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, and Purva Bhadrapada</note>, Bharani, and Magha (Ancestors) are **Fierce** (Ugra). They should be used for destruction, deceit, imprisonment, poisoning, arson, and strikes with weapons to achieve success. || 8 ||

Hasta, Ashvini, and Pushya are **Light/Swift** (Laghu). They are declared to bring success in trade, sensual enjoyments, gaining knowledge, making ornaments, fine arts, craftsmanship, medicine, and travel. || 9 ||

The **Soft/Mild** (Mridu) group consists of Anuradha, Chitra, Revati (Pushan), and Mrigashira (Moon). These are beneficial for making friends, sexual union, clothing, ornaments, auspicious ceremonies, and singing. || 10 ||

Krittika (Fire) and Vishakha are **Mixed** (Mridu-Tikshna) and yield mixed results. Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Punarvasu (Aditi), and Swati (Vayu) are **Movable** (Chara) and are beneficial for activities involving motion. || 11 ||

The three stars starting from Hasta <note>Hasta, Chitra, Swati</note>, Mrigashira, the three starting from Shravana <note>Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha</note>, Revati, Ashvini, Jyeshtha, Pushya, and Punarvasu are beneficial for the act of **shaving** (tonsure), provided the Moon is rising or the moment is joined with an auspicious star. || 12 ||

Shaving is not beneficial for those who have just bathed, those eager to travel, those already adorned, those who have applied oil, those who have just eaten, or those in the midst of battle. It is also forbidden at twilight, at night, on the days of Mars, Saturn, or the Sun, on "Empty" (Rikta) lunar days, on the ninth lunar day, or during the Vishti (Karana) period. || 13 ||

By order of the King, with the consent of Brahmins, at the time of marriage, during periods of birth or death impurity (Sutaka), for the release of a prisoner, or during initiation for a sacrifice—in all these cases, shaving is considered auspicious regardless of the specific star. || 14 ||

Hasta, Mula, Shravana, Punarvasu, Mrigashira, and Pushya—in these "masculine" stars, one should perform...

The number of stars <term>Yogatara: junction stars</term> for the constellations starting from Ashwini are as follows:
Shikhi (3), Guna (3), Rasa (6), Indriya (5), Anala (3), Shashi (1), Vishaya (5), Guna (3), Ritu (6), Pancha (5), Vasu (8), Paksha (2), Vishaya (5), Eka (1), Chandra (1), Bhuta (14), Arnava (4), Agni (3), Rudra (11), Ashviva (1), Vasu (8), Dahana (3), Bhuta (14), Shata (100), Paksha (2), Vasu (8), and thirty-two. This is the result of the stars; that is, these are the junction stars of Ashwini and the other constellations. The fruits of the Ashwini and other constellations will be in accordance with the proportion of these stars. ||1|| ||2|| In marriage, the auspicious or inauspicious effects of a constellation manifest in as many years as there are stars in that constellation. Similarly, the destruction of fever or other diseases is said to occur in as many days as there are stars. ||3||

The twenty-eight deities of the constellations starting from Ashwini are, in order:
The Ashwini Kumaras, Yama, Agni, Brahma, the Moon, Rudra, Aditi, Brihaspati, the Serpents, the Ancestors <term>Pitris</term>, Yoni (Bhaga), Aryaman, the Sun, Tvashtr, Pavana, Indragni, Mitra, ||4|| Indra, Nirriti, the Waters, the Universal Gods <term>Vishvedevas</term>, Viranchi, Hari (Vishnu), the Vasus, Varuna, Ajapada, Ahirbudhnya, and Pushan. ||5||

Among these, Rohini and the three Uttaras (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada) are designated as **Fixed** <term>Dhruva</term>. In this group, it is appropriate to perform consecrations, peace-making rituals, planting trees, founding cities, religious acts, sowing seeds, and commencing any work intended to be permanent. ||6||

Mula, Ardra, Jyeshtha, and Ashlesha are ruled by **Sharp** <term>Tikshna</term> masters. In these, acts of assault, mantra-sadhana, dealing with spirits <term>Baital</term>, imprisonment, killing, and divisive actions are successful. ||7||

The three Purvas (Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Purva Bhadrapada), Bharani, and Magha—these five constellations belong to the **Fierce** <term>Ugra</term> group. These stars are suitable for success in acts of destruction, ruin, deceit, imprisonment, poisoning, burning, and strikes with weapons. ||8||

Hasta, Ashwini, and Pushya—these three constellations belong to the **Light** <term>Laghu</term> group. In these, success is achieved in trade, sensual enjoyment, acquiring knowledge, making ornaments, arts, crafts, medicine, and travel. ||9||

Anuradha, Chitra, Revati, and Mrigashira—these four constellations are of the **Soft** <term>Mridu</term> class. This group is beneficial for sexual union, clothing, ornaments, auspicious ceremonies, movement, and matters concerning friends. ||10||

Vishakha and Krittika constellations are of the **Soft-Sharp** <term>Mridu-Tikshna</term> group; their results are mixed. In the five constellations of Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Punarvasu, and Swati, **Mobile** <term>Chara</term> actions are beneficial. ||11||

...is beneficial. || 12 || One should not undergo <term>Kshaur Karma</term><note>The ritual shaving of hair or cutting of nails</note> if they have just bathed, are about to depart on a journey, are already adorned, have just applied oil to the body, have just eaten, during battle, while lacking a proper seat, during twilight or at night, or on Tuesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays. During the constellations of Hasta, Revati, Swati, Anuradha, Pushya, Chitra, and Mrigashira, and on Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, one should perform ceremonies of <term>Samskara</term><note>Rites of passage</note>, initiations, vows, and the tying of the sacred <term>Mekhala</term><note>Girdle worn by students</note>. || 16 ||

When malefic planets are in the third and eleventh houses from the <term>Lagna</term><note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note>, when the Moon sign and the Ascendant are in the domain of a benefic planet, and when no malefic planets occupy the Ascendant or the Moon sign—or when the Ascendant is in the signs of Jupiter (Sagittarius or Pisces)—the piercing of the ears (<term>Karnavedha</term>) should be performed under the constellations of Pushya, Mrigashira, Chitra, Shravana, or Revati. || 17 ||

When the twelfth house, the <term>Kendras</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, and the eighth house are pure (unoccupied by malefic planets), and malefic planets are in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses; when Jupiter and Venus are in the Ascendant or a Kendra; and when the birth sign of the person performing the act is rising—or when the Ascendant is a "civilized" sign (Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, Scorpio, Aquarius) or a "fixed" sign (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius)—the commencement of all works is auspicious, particularly the building or entering of a home. || 18 ||

->Thus ends the ninety-eighth chapter of the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western region, on the Brihat Samhita composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira. || 98 ||<-

### Chapter 99
### The Qualities of Lunar Days and Half-Days

> Brahma, Vidhatri, Hari, Yama, the Moon, Kartikeya, Indra, the Vasus, and the Serpents; Dharma, Ishvara, the Sun, Cupid, the Spirits of the Dead, and the All-Gods are the lords of the lunar days (<term>Tithis</term>). || 1 || The Ancestors (<term>Pitris</term>) are the lords of the New Moon day. The days are categorized into three types: Nanda (Joyous), Bhadra (Lucky), Vijaya (Victorious), Rikta (Empty), and Purna (Full). || 2 || Whatever work is prescribed for a specific constellation should also be performed on its corresponding lunar day. Such work, when done during the appropriate <term>Karana</term><note>A half-day lunar period</note> or <term>Muhurta</term><note>An auspicious moment of 48 minutes</note>, grants success according to the nature of the presiding deity. || 3 || For the Karanas known as Bava, Balava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara, Vanija, and Vishti, the presiding lords are Indra, Brahma, Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Shri, and Yama respectively. || 4 || From the second half of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, the "fixed" Karanas begin: Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga, and Kinstughna. Their respective lords are Kali, Vrishabha, the Serpent, and Vayu. || 5 || One should perform auspicious, mobile, stable, and nourishing acts, as well as religious deeds and those beneficial to Brahmins...

# Page 323
## Chapter 99: Qualities of Lunar Days and Half-Days (Tithi-Karana)

In the half-day known as *Balava*, one should perform religious acts and deeds beneficial to priests. In *Kaulava*, acts of friendship, making alliances, and choosing friends are favored. In *Taitila*, one should focus on matters of good fortune, seeking shelter, and establishing a home. **(6)** In *Gara*, activities related to agriculture, sowing seeds, and building houses or shelters are prescribed. In *Vanija*, trade-related unions and permanent works are suitable. The *Vishti* half-day <note>also known as Bhadra, often considered inauspicious</note> does not grant auspicious results, but it is effective for attacking enemies or administering poisons. **(7)** In *Shakuni*, one should perform nourishing acts, prepare medicines, and work with roots and mantras. In *Chatushpada*, tasks related to cattle, and state affairs dedicated to priests and ancestors should be done. In *Naga*, one should perform fixed or harsh deeds, acts of seizure, and works associated with misfortune. In *Kinstughna*, auspicious, desired, and nourishing acts, as well as ceremonies for success and well-being, are appropriate. **(8)**

-> Thus ends the ninety-ninth chapter of the *Brihat Samhita* by the illustrious Varahamihira, titled "The Qualities of Lunar Days and Half-Days." <-

***

Brahma, Vidhata, Hari, Yama, the Moon, the Six-faced One <note>Kartikeya</note>, Indra, the Vasus, the Serpent, Dharma, Isha, Savita, Manmatha, and Kali—these deities are the lords of the lunar days starting from the first day (*Pratipada*) in sequence. **(1)** The ancestors (*Pitris*) are the lords of the New Moon (*Amavasya*). One should perform actions corresponding to the nature of these presiding deities on their respective days. These days are categorized into five types: *Nanda* (Joyous), *Bhadra* (Lucky), *Vijaya* (Victorious), *Rikta* (Empty), and *Purna* (Full). **(2)** Whatever work is prescribed for a specific star constellation (*Nakshatra*) should ideally be performed on the lunar day ruled by that same deity. If the cause or the specific moment (*Muhurta*) also aligns with that deity, the work will be successful—for example, the *Rohini* constellation paired with the first lunar day <note>both ruled by Brahma/Prajapati</note>. **(3)**

The lords of the half-days known as *Bava, Balava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara, Vanija,* and *Vishti* are, in order: Indra, Brahma, Mitra, Aryaman, the Earth, Shri <note>Goddess of Fortune</note>, and Yama. **(4)** Starting from the second half of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, the four "fixed" half-days occur: *Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga,* and *Kinstughna*. These are stationary, and their lords are Kali, the Tree, the Serpent, and the Wind, respectively. **(5)** In the *Bava* half-day, one should perform auspicious, mobile, stable, and nourishing deeds. In *Balava*, religious ceremonies and works for the benefit of priests are recommended. In *Kaulava*, one should foster affection, friendship, and all types of formal selections. In *Taitila*, works concerning good fortune, seeking refuge, and house-consecration should be done. **(6)**

In *Gara*, agriculture, sowing seeds, and building houses or shelters are favored. In *Vanija*, commercial associations and permanent works should be undertaken. The *Vishti* half-day does not yield auspicious fruits, but it is successful for striking down enemies or using poisons. **(7)** In *Shakuni*, taking nourishing medicines, roots, and mantras is advised. In *Chatushpada*, cattle-related work and statecraft dedicated to priests and ancestors are duties. In *Naga*, fixed, harsh deeds, seizures, and acts resulting from misfortune should be performed. In *Kinstughna*, it is proper to perform auspicious, desired, and nourishing actions that bring about the success of celebratory rites. **(8)**

-> Thus ends the ninety-ninth chapter of the Hindi commentary on the *Brihat Samhita* written by the illustrious teacher Varahamihira, as composed by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, a resident of Moradabad in the North-Western province. <-

## Chapter 100
### The Lunar Mansion and Ascendant for Marriage

> Marriage should be performed when the Moon is in the <term>Nakshatras</term><note>Lunar mansions or star clusters</note> of Rohiṇī, the three Uttaras (Uttarāphālgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Uttarābhādrapadā), Revatī, Mṛgaśira, Mūla, Anurādhā, Maghā, Hasta, or Svātī, and when the <term>Lagna</term><note>The rising sign or Ascendant</note> is Virgo, Libra, or Gemini. Benefic planets should be in places other than the seventh, eighth, or twelfth from the rising sign; the Moon should be in the eleventh, second, or third house; and malefic planets should be in the third, eleventh, or sixth houses. However, Venus must not be in the sixth house, nor Mars in the eighth. ||1|| When the birth signs of the couple are not in the second, ninth, or eighth positions from each other <note>referring to unfavorable relationship matches like 2/12, 9/5, or 6/8 patterns</note>, when the Sun is favorable in transit, and the Moon is not joined with the Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Venus, nor placed between two malefic planets; avoiding the days of Vyatipāta and Vaidhṛti <note>inauspicious astronomical yogas</note>, the Viṣṭi <term>Karaṇa</term><note>a specific half-day period</note>, and the <term>Riktā</term> lunar dates <note>the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar month</note>; avoiding malefic weekdays and the months of Chaitra and Pausha; if the <term>Navāṃśa</term><note>the ninth-part sub-division of a sign</note> is a human sign (Gemini, Virgo, Libra), then the marriage is most excellent. ||2||

->Thus ends the one hundredth chapter of the Bṛhat Saṃhitā by Śrī Varāhamihira, titled "Determination of the Lunar Mansion and Ascendant for Marriage."<-

Marriage can take place in the constellations of Rohiṇī, Uttarāphālgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Uttarābhādrapadā, Revatī, Mṛgaśira, Mūla, Anurādhā, Maghā, Hasta, and Svātī, when the signs of Virgo, Libra, or Gemini are rising. Benefic planets should be seated in places other than the 7th, 8th, and 12th from this rising sign. The Moon should be in the 2nd, 3rd, or 11th house of the marriage chart. Malefic planets should be in the 3rd, 11th, 6th, or 8th houses, provided Venus is not in the 6th and Mars is not in the 8th. ||1|| If the birth signs of the bride and groom are not in the 2nd, 9th, or 8th positions from each other—meaning in the matching process, the 2/12, 9/5, or 6/8 patterns are absent—and the Sun and Venus are favorable in transit; if the Moon is not joined with the Sun, Saturn, Mars, or Venus, nor caught between two malefic planets; in yogas other than Vyatipāta and Vaidhṛti, in a Karaṇa other than Viṣṭi, on a date other than the Riktā dates, on the weekday of a benefic planet, during the Sun's northern course <note>Uttarāyaṇa</note>, excluding the months of Chaitra and Pausha, and if the sub-divisional rising sign is a human sign (Gemini, Virgo, Libra), then the marriage is considered best. ||2||

Thus ends the one hundredth chapter in the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western region, on the Bṛhat Saṃhitā composed by the Great Teacher Varāhamihira. ||100||

## Chapter 101
### Birth According to the Lunar Mansions

One born under [Aśleṣā] is deceitful, eats all kinds of food, is sinful and ungrateful—

### Now begins the One Hundred and Second Chapter
### The Division of the Zodiac Signs

> **Aries** is said to consist of the constellations **Ashwini**, **Bharani**, and one quarter of **Krittika**. **Taurus** consists of the remaining three quarters of Krittika, **Rohini**, and half of **Mrigashira**. || 1 ||
> The remaining half of **Mrigashira**, **Ardra**, and three quarters of **Punarvasu** constitute **Gemini**. The remaining quarter of Punarvasu, **Pushya**, and **Ashlesha** constitute **Cancer**. || 2 ||
> **Leo** consists of **Magha**, **Purva Phalguni**, and one quarter of **Uttara Phalguni**. The remaining three quarters of that, **Hasta**, and half of **Chitra** constitute the sign named **Virgo**. || 3 ||
> In **Libra** are the other half of **Chitra**, **Svati**, and three quarters of **Vishakha**. In **Scorpio** are the remaining quarter of Vishakha, along with **Anuradha** and **Jyeshtha**. || 4 ||
> **Mula**, **Purvashadha**, and the first quarter of **Uttarashadha** constitute **Sagittarius**. **Capricorn** consists of the remaining three quarters of that, **Shravana**, and the first half of **Dhanishtha**. || 5 ||
> **Aquarius** consists of the latter half of **Dhanishtha**, **Shatabhisha**, and three quarters of **Purva Bhadrapada**. The remaining part of that, along with **Uttara Bhadrapada** and **Revati**, constitute **Pisces**. || 6 ||
> Starting from **Ashwini**, **Magha**, and **Mula**, the signs **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius** begin respectively. In the odd-numbered signs, the quarters of the constellations proceed with an increase of one quarter each in succession. || 7 ||

->Thus ends the one hundred and second chapter, named "The Division of the Zodiac Signs," in the *Brihat Samhita* by the venerable Varahamihira. || 102 ||<-

### Now begins the One Hundred and Third Chapter

### On the Nuptial Chart
<note>Sanskrit: Vivaha-patala. This chapter discusses the astrological timing and planetary positions suitable for marriage.</note>

If the Sun is in the ascendant <note>the first house</note> at the time of marriage, it makes the woman a widow; Mars does the same. Rahu <note>the North Node</note> causes the loss of the husband, and Saturn makes her poor. Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter make her a virtuous wife, while the Moon causes a shortening of life. || 1 || The Sun, Saturn, Rahu, and Mars in the second house certainly cause incomparable misery and poverty. Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury make her a wealthy woman who does not suffer widowhood, while the Moon makes her a woman with many children. || 2 || The Sun, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury in the third house always make her the mother of many children and a sharer of wealth. Clearly, the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> makes her fortunate, but Rahu <note>the son of Simhika</note> definitely brings death. || 3 || If Saturn is in the fourth house, there is little milk <note>referring to breastfeeding or prosperity</note>; the Sun and the Moon cause misfortune. Rahu brings a co-wife <note>rivalry</note>, and Mars gives little wealth. Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury grant happiness. || 4 || The Sun and Mars in the fifth house cause the loss of children; Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus grant many children. Rahu brings death, Saturn causes diseases, and the Moon soon brings the birth of daughters. || 5 || Saturn, the Sun, Rahu, and Jupiter in the sixth house, along with Mars, make the woman fortunate and devoted to her in-laws. The Moon makes her a widow, Venus makes her poor, and the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> makes the bride fond of quarrels. || 6 || Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, Rahu, the Sun, the Moon, and Venus, if positioned in the seventh sign <note>the seventh house</note>, forcibly cause widowhood and imprisonment—

When Venus, the Sun, and Mars are situated in the ninth house <note>The house of fortune and dharma.</note>, and Jupiter is there, she is devoted to righteousness; Mercury makes her free from disease. Rahu and Saturn make her barren, while the Moon causes her to give birth to daughters and leads to wandering. ||9||
Rahu in the tenth house makes her a widow; the Sun and Saturn make her devoted to sinful acts. Mars brings death, the Moon makes her devoid of wealth and unchaste; the remaining planets make her wealthy and fortunate. ||10||
In the eleventh house <note>The house of gains.</note>, the Sun makes her have many children; the Moon makes her wealthy; Mars makes her endowed with sons; Saturn makes her very rich. Jupiter grants long life; Mercury makes her prosperous; Rahu ensures she does not become a widow; and Venus makes her endowed with wealth. ||11||
In the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and expenditure.</note>, Jupiter makes her wealthy; the Sun makes her poor; the Moon causes the depletion of wealth; and Rahu makes her unchaste. Venus makes her a virtuous wife; Mercury grants many sons and grandsons; while Saturn and Mars make her heart inclined toward drinking <note>Likely referring to intoxicants or strong wine</note>. ||12||
The dust that is raised by the hooves of cows at the end of the day <note>The 'Godhuli' or cow-dust hour, traditionally considered a highly auspicious time for weddings regardless of other astrological flaws.</note> is the destroyer of sins; for women being married, it bestows abundant wealth, children, health, and good fortune. At that specific time, there is no need to consider the lunar mansion (Nakshatra), the lunar day (Tithi), the half-day (Karana), the ascendant (Lagna), or the planetary yoga. The rising dust of cows is famous for bringing happiness to men and calming all evils. ||13||

**Thus ends the 103rd Chapter, titled "The Section on Marriage," in the Illustrious Brihat Samhita of Varahamihira. ||103||**

At the time of a woman's marriage, if the Sun or Mars is in the Ascendant (Lagna), that woman becomes a widow. If Rahu is in the Lagna, there is calamity for the children; if Saturn, the girl becomes poor. If Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus are there, she is possessed of a husband and wealth, and if the Moon is in the second house, it makes the woman have many children. ||2|| If the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, or Jupiter are in the third house, the woman always has many children and wealth. Saturn in the <insert>third</insert> house makes her fortunate, and the presence of Rahu causes the death of the girl. ||3|| If Saturn is in the fourth house, that woman produces only a moderate amount of milk in her breasts. If the Sun or Moon are there, she is unfortunate. If Rahu is there, the girl will have a co-wife; if Mars, she will have little wealth; and if Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus, she will be happy. ||4|| If the Sun or Mars are in the fifth house, her children do not survive. If Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus are there, she will have many sons. Rahu causes death, Saturn causes severe disease, and the Moon quickly makes the woman a mother of daughters. ||5|| If Saturn, Sun, Rahu, Jupiter, or Mars are in the sixth house, she is beautiful and devoted to her father-in-law. The Moon causes widowhood, and Venus causes poverty. If Mercury is in the sixth house, the woman is wealthy but quarrelsome. ||6|| If Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Rahu, Sun, Moon, or Venus are in the seventh house, the woman [suffers] according to the planets...

If Mercury and Jupiter are in the eighth house of the wedding chart <note>The eighth house is traditionally associated with longevity and the husband's lifespan in a woman's chart.</note>, there is constant separation from the husband. In the latter part of the day, when the cowherds drive the cows back home with their sticks, the dust that rises in the sky, trampled by the hooves of the cows struck by those sticks, is called *Godhuli* <note>Literally "cow-dust"; the twilight hour considered highly auspicious for weddings regardless of other astrological flaws.</note>. The beautiful women married during this *Godhuli* time become extremely wealthy, blessed with sons, healthy, and fortunate. During the *Godhuli* time, no consideration is given to the lunar mansion (*Nakshatra*), lunar day (*Tithi*), half-day (*Karana*), ascendant (*Lagna*), or planetary alignment (*Yoga*). Its fame is such that *Godhuli* <gloss>1</gloss> rises and destroys the heap of sins of men. || 13 ||

# The Varahi Samhita

-> Whether my steady verse is disliked or not, it is not so; a virtuous woman is not as dear to men as one who is as fickle as a swaying hip. <- <note>The author, Varahamihira, uses a poetic metaphor here to justify the use of varied and "fickle" (changing) meters in his technical verses, comparing the charm of rhythmic variety to the movements of a woman.</note> || 3 ||

The **Sun** is auspicious in the 6th, 3rd, and 10th houses; the **Moon** in the 3rd, 10th, 6th, 7th, and 1st; **Jupiter** when moving through the 7th, 9th, 2nd, and 5th; **Mars** and **Saturn** in the 6th and 3rd. **Mercury** is good in the 6th, 2nd, 4th, 10th, and 8th. All planets are beneficial in the 11th (the penultimate house). **Venus** is auspicious in all houses except the 7th, 6th, and 10th. Like a **tiger** <note>original: "Shardula," referring to the Shardulavikridita meter used here</note>, a planet in an unfavorable spot causes frequent terror. || 4 ||

When the **Sun** is in the **1st house** (Birth sign), it causes fatigue, loss of wealth, irritability, stomach diseases, and wearying journeys. In the **2nd house**, it brings loss of mental peace, lack of happiness, deception, and eye diseases. In the **3rd house**, it grants attainment of position, accumulation of wealth, joy, health, and the destruction of enemies. In the **4th house**, it brings diseases and creates constant obstacles to the enjoyment of "wearing flower garlands" <note>original: "Sragdhara," referring to the Sragdhara meter; metaphorically means sensual pleasures</note>. || 5 ||

In the **5th house**, the **Sun** causes many sufferings born of disease and the like. In the **6th house**, the Sun destroys diseases, eliminates enemies, and dispels sorrows. In the **7th house**, it causes travel, fear of stomach ailments, and humiliation. In the **8th house**, it brings sickness and fear; even a man with a **beautiful-faced** <note>original: "Suvadana," referring to the Suvadana meter</note> wife finds no pleasure in her. || 6 ||

In the **9th house**, the **Sun** brings danger, poverty, disease, and hinders mental efforts. In the **10th house**, one achieves fierce victory and the gradual completion of one's work. In the **11th house**, it brings victory, position, honor, wealth, and the destruction of disease. For those of **good conduct** <note>original: "Suvritta," referring to the Suvrittatilaka meter</note>, efforts in the **12th house** may bear fruit, but for others, it is not so. || 7 ||

The **Moon** in the **1st house** provides excellent food, bedding, and clothing. In the **2nd house**, it diminishes honor and wealth and brings obstacles. In the **3rd house**, one obtains clothes, women, wealth, and happiness. In the **4th house**, there is a lack of trust; it is like a **crested** <note>original: "Shikhari," referring to the Shikharini meter</note> mountain inhabited by a snake. || 8 ||

In the **5th house**, the **Moon** causes humiliation, disease, grief, and obstacles on the path. In the **6th house**, it produces wealth, happiness, and the destruction of enemies and diseases. In the **7th house**, it brings vehicles, honor, bedding, food, and financial gain. When the Moon is in the **8th house**, moving with a **slow gait** <note>original: "Mandakranta," referring to the Mandakranta meter</note> like a serpent, who does not feel fear? || 9 ||

In the **9th house**, it causes bondage, agitation, exhaustion, and stomach disease. In the **10th house**, it always grants authority and the fulfillment of work. In the **11th house**, it brings prosperity, meeting with friends, wealth, and joy. In the **12th house**, it causes expenses and faults similar to the **behavior of a bull** <note>original: "Vrishabhacharita," referring to the meter of the same name</note>. || 10 ||

When **Mars** is in the **1st house**, there is injury; in the **2nd**, trouble from the ruler, quarrels, and enmity. Even one who is like **Indra's thunderbolt** <note>original: "Upendravajra," referring to the Upendravajra meter</note> suffers greatly from bile, fire, disease, and thieves. || 11 ||

In the **3rd house**, **Mars** brings results through thieves and youths: brilliance, authority, wealth, woolen goods, and things known as "ores and minerals." || 12 ||

When the **Son of Earth** (Mars) is in the **4th house**, there is fever, stomach disease, and blood disorders. Through association with wicked men, it brings sudden misfortune. || 13 ||

In the **5th house**, Mars brings fear of enemies, disease, and anger, as well as grief caused by sons. His luster does not remain steady for long, like a **Jasmine garland** <note>original: "Malati," referring to the Malati meter</note> placed on the head of a monkey. || 14 ||

In the **6th house**, one is free from fear of enemies and quarrels, and gains gold, coral, and copper. When the Son of Earth enters the house of enemies (6th), why would one look at the **distorted face** <note>original: "Aparavaktra," referring to the Aparavaktra meter</note> of another? || 15 ||

In the **7th house**, it causes quarrels with the spouse, eye pain, and stomach disease. In the **8th**, one is afflicted by blood loss and wounds, with wealth and honor diminished. When Mars is in the **9th**, one's **gait is delayed** <note>original: "Vilambitagati," referring to the meter</note> by humiliation, loss of wealth, and exhaustion of the body's elements. || 16 ||

In the **10th house**, Mars brings mixed results; in the **11th**, various gains and victory. He enjoys the country like a **six-legged bee** <note>original: "Shatcharana"</note> hovering over a **flowering tree-top** <note>original: "Pushpitagra," referring to the Pushpitagra meter</note>. || 17 ||

In the **12th house**, Mars causes various expenses and a man is tormented by hundreds of misfortunes. Even one proud of his **Indra-like lineage** <note>original: "Indravamsha," referring to the Indravamsha meter</note> suffers from the anger of women, bile, breathing difficulties, and eye pain. || 18 ||

### The Transit of Mercury (Shashiputra)
When Mercury enters the **second house**, there is loss of wealth. In the **third house**, one gains friends. However, with a heart anxious from fear of the king and enemies, he wanders swiftly due to his own past misdeeds. (20)

When the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is in the **fourth house**, there is an increase in one's paternal family and an influx of wealth. In the **fifth house**, there is conflict with son and wife; he finds no pleasure even in a beautiful woman. (21)

In the **sixth house**, Mercury brings good fortune, victory, and progress. In the **seventh**, he causes loss of complexion and excessive quarreling. In the **eighth**, there is gain of children, victory, clothing, and wealth; his skill becomes a delight to the mind. (22)

In the **ninth house**, Mercury creates obstacles. In the **tenth**, he destroys enemies and bestows wealth. He provides a joyful bed and a house furnished with fine blankets <note>original: *kutha-starana*</note>. (23)

In the **eleventh house**, the Son of the Cold-Rayed One <note>Mercury</note> brings wealth, happiness, children, women, friends, and physical nourishment; the person speaks sweet words. In the **twelfth**, afflicted by defeat from enemies and diseases, he cannot endure the pleasures of union, even in the **Malini** <note>A double meaning: refers to a woman wearing garlands and the poetic meter *Malini* used in this verse</note> style. (24)

### The Transit of Jupiter (Jiva)
When Jupiter is in the **first house**, one loses wealth and intelligence, is displaced from one's position, and suffers many quarrels. Even if he obtains money, his enemies take it; he hovers like a bee around the lotus-face of a beloved <note>restless and unsettled</note>. (25)

In the **third house**, there is displacement from position and hindrance to work. In the **fourth**, many troubles arise from kinsmen. Jupiter here grants no peace to the afflicted mind, whether in the village or in the forest, even amidst the **Mattamayura** <note>The "Drunken Peacock" meter</note>. (26)

Entering the **fifth house**, the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> produces servants, auspicious children, elephants, horses, and bulls. He provides houses in golden cities, fine clothes, and heaps of jewels and virtues. (27)

When Jupiter goes to the **sixth house**, neither the face of a friend brightened by a *tilaka* <note>forehead mark</note>, nor a house echoing with the cries of peacocks and cuckoos, nor a place graced by leaping fawns can give joy to the mind. (28)

The Teacher of the Thirty <note>Jupiter</note>, upon reaching the **seventh house**, grants a bed, sexual pleasures, wealth, food, flowers, and vehicles. He bestows refined speech and great wisdom. (29)

In the **eighth**, he brings imprisonment, disease, intense grief, hardship on the road, and sickness equal to death. In the **ninth**, Jupiter grants skill, command, children, success in work and wealth, and the gain of **Shalini** <note>Virtuous women / the *Shalini* meter</note>. (30)

In the **tenth**, he destroys position, health, and wealth. In the **eleventh**, he bestows those very things. In the **twelfth**, the man suffers the sorrow of a reverse fortune on the road, even if he travels in a **Rathoddhata** <note>A chariot / the *Rathoddhata* meter</note>. (31)

### The Transit of Venus (Bhrigusuta)
When the Son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> enters the **first house**, he provides the tools of love: fragrant and delightful scents, flowers, and grand clothing. The man, possessing a bedroom and a seat, acts like a bee to the lotus-face of a passionate woman. (32)

In the **second house**, Venus brings children, wealth, grain, and the favor of kings and family. Adorned with flowers and gems, the man enjoys his desires, even if his hair has the luster of the **Vasantatilaka** <note>The "Grace of Spring" / the *Vasantatilaka* meter</note>. (33)

In the **third**, the Teacher of the Daityas <note>Venus</note> grants command, wealth, honor, and the destruction of enemies. In the **fourth**, he provides a circle of friends and power resembling the **Indravajra** <note>Indra's lightning bolt / the *Indravajra* meter</note>. (34)

Venus in the **fifth house** generates the satisfaction of elders and the acquisition of kinsmen. He brings gain of children and wealth, help from friends, and an undefeated spirit against enemy forces. (35)

In the **sixth**, Venus causes defeat, illness, and distress. In the **seventh**, he creates misfortune through women. Having gone to the **eighth**, he provides a house and household items, and brings a lady of fortune <note>Lakshmi-like wife</note> to the man. (36)

In the **ninth**, the Son of Bhrigu brings virtue, happiness from women, and luck, as well as heaps of wealth and clothes. In the **tenth**, even if one speaks **Pramitakshara** <note>Measured/few words / the *Pramitakshara* meter</note>, he receives insults, quarrels, and fear of fire. (37)

In the **eleventh**, the Son of Bhrigu gives friends, wealth, food, and scents. In the **twelfth**, there is an influx of wealth and clothing; however, the gain of clothing is not permanent. (38)

# The Varāhī Samhitā

Separated from his kinsmen, having caused the death of his own relatives, reaching a foreign land, and befriended by the wicked, he becomes destitute of wealth and children, wandering with a miserable face. **[Verse 39]**

When the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in the **second house** by transit, the body is deprived of beauty and happiness, and one is devoid of pride and strength. Whatever wealth is accumulated through the merits of others is like water fallen on a bamboo leaf—it is neither much nor does it last long. **[Verse 40]**

When the Son of the Sun is in the **third house**, one gains wealth, servants, attendants, camels, buffaloes, horses, elephants, and donkeys. He enjoys immediate prosperity and immense happiness, the cessation of diseases, and though he may be timid, he rules over his enemies with the grace of a hero. **[Verse 41]**

When the Son of the Sun enters the **fourth house**, one is separated from friends, wealth, and wife. His mind becomes wicked and crooked everywhere, imitating the movement of a serpent <note>original: *bhujanga-prayāta*, also a reference to a specific poetic meter</note>. **[Verse 42]**

In the **fifth house**, the Son of the Sun makes one destitute of children and wealth and involved in frequent quarrels. When he reaches the **sixth house**, enemies and diseases are destroyed, and one enjoys the pleasures of women <note>literally: "drinks from the face of a woman whose lips are like a treasure-chest of beauty"</note>. **[Verse 43]**

In the **seventh** and **eighth houses**, the Son of the Sun causes one to travel on weary paths, deprived of wife and sons, and acting miserably. Similarly, in the **ninth house**, there is enmity, heart disease, and imprisonment; even one's religious merit <term>Dharma: righteous duty and spiritual credit</term> is destroyed by divine calamities and the like. **[Verse 44]**

In the **tenth house**, Saturn brings the attainment of professional work, wealth, and fame, but also the loss of learning and reputation. In the **eleventh house**, there is harshness but also the gain of others' wealth. At the **end** <note>the twelfth house</note>, one encounters a series of waves of sorrow. **[Verse 45]**

Even a planet that bestows good results does so in accordance with the time and the worthiness of the recipient. A canopy of clouds does not pour a great quantity of water into a small measure <note>original: *kudava*, a small dry measure</note> during the spring. **[Verse 46]**

->**Remedies for the Planets**<-

The Sun and Mars should be worshipped with devotion using red flowers, scents, copper, golden bulls, and Bakula flowers. The Moon with a cow, white flowers, silver, and sweets. Venus with intoxicating/pleasurable things. Saturn with black objects. Mercury with gems, silver, and Tilaka flowers. Jupiter with yellow items. When pleased, there will be no suffering even if a planet falls from its exaltation or enters a difficult state <note>original: *bhujanga-vijrimbhita*, "the yawning of a snake," also a poetic meter</note>. **[Verse 47]**

One should pacify an evil planetary vision <term>Drishti: astrological aspect</term> that has arisen by worshipping gods and Brahmins, through peace-making rituals <term>Shanti</term>, chanting <term>Japa</term>, vows, charity, and self-control, as well as by associating with good people. **[Verse 48]**

The Sun and Mars give their effects in the first half of a sign; the Moon and Saturn are said to give theirs at the end of a sign. The good and bad characteristics are like the *Aryā*, *Gīti*, and *Upagīti* meters respectively. **[Verse 49]**

As a benefic planet is at the beginning, so it remains at the end. This is like the proper combination of groups <term>Ganas: metrical units</term> in the *Upagīti* meter. **[Verse 50]**

Even an *Aryā* verse is ruined if a heavy syllable <term>Guru</term> is placed in an odd position; similarly, a planet in an unfavorable house brings ruin. Just as a bad sixth group in a meter brings everything to "lightness" <note>a pun on *laghutā*, meaning both a short vowel and insignificance</note>. **[Verse 51]**

A planet, even if powerful in giving bad results, becomes auspicious when aspected by a benefic. Good and bad results reach an equilibrium, just as in the *Gīlaka* and *Narkuṭaka* meters. **[Verse 52]**

All that has been proclaimed is in vain if the planet is in its sign of depression, in an enemy's house, or aspected by an enemy. It is like the playful, side-long glances of a beautiful woman directed at a blind man. **[Verse 53]**

The Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> follows the results of the Sun, and the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> follows the nature of the planet he is with. This is like how the *Skandhaka*, *Aryā-gīti*, and *Vaitālīya* meters are contained within the *Māgadhī Gāthā*. **[Verse 54]**

Saturn, colored by the rays of the Sun, becomes excessively disturbed and increased in power. He acts like bile <term>Pitta: one of the three humors in Ayurveda</term> towards men who do what is beneficial, but not so towards those who are like the *Aryā* <note>noble or the meter</note>. **[Verse 55]**

A person becomes like the planet with which he is joined. Just as the expression of a face changes due to the movements of the mind. **[Verse 56]**

The fifth syllable in all quarters and the seventh in the second and fourth—just as these syllables become light <term>Laghu</term> in a verse, so does a man become insignificant when planets are ill-placed. **[Verse 57]**

One who is naturally "light" <note>lowly</note> and stands outside the "circle" <note>social circle or poetic meter</note> attains "heaviness" <note>dignity or a long vowel</note> in the world when the planets are well-placed. **[Verse 58]**

Whatever work is begun by the ignorant for their own advancement when the planets are ill-placed...

# Chapter 104: The Transit of Planets

That very action destroys them, just as a <term>Vetala</term><note>A ghost or spirit that animates corpses</note> destroys one who performs a ritual incorrectly. || 59 || A King who observes the favorable positions of the planets and initiates his actions at the right time—even if his personal effort is small—reaches the goal of his conduct, just as one masters the <term>Aupachhandasika</term><note>A specific Sanskrit poetic meter</note> meter. || 60 ||

When the Sun is in an <term>Upachaya</term><note>The 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses, associated with growth and improvement</note> house, or when the Sun is in the <term>Lagna</term><note>The ascending sign on the eastern horizon</note>, one should carry out tasks related to: gold, pearls, horses, wood, bones, leather, woolen blankets, mountains, trees, bark, sky, snakes, thieves, soldiers, forests, service to cruel kings, royal consecration, medicines, silk cloth, trade, cowherds, wilderness, physicians, stones, and famous heroes. Success is also found in battles, praising others, sacrifices, and fire rituals.

On the day of the Moon (Monday), or when the Moon is in the Lagna or a <term>Kendra</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered pillars of the horoscope</note>, success comes to: ornaments, conch shells, pearls, lotuses, silver, water, sacrifices, sugarcane, food, women, milk, oily trees, shrubs, marshy grains, liquid substances, Brahmins, horses, cooling treatments, horned animals, agriculture, army commanders, crying out for help, royal favor, nocturnal wanderers, those living in pits, single items, elephants, flowers, and clothing.

On the day of the Son of Earth (Mars/Tuesday), all works related to minerals and mines are successful, as are: gold, fire, coral, weapons, cruelty, theft, assault, forests, forts, military authority, red flowers, trees with red sap, bitter and pungent substances, deceit, those who earn wealth through fire, princes, physicians, Buddhist monks, those who work at night, silk, and acts of villainy or pride.

On the day or Lagna of the Son of the Moon (Mercury/Wednesday), success follows: emeralds, land, perfumes, clothes, ordinary theater, scientific scriptures, poetry, all arts, cleverness, mantras, alchemy, eloquence, trade, vows, yoga, messengers, longevity rituals, illusions, baths, and works that are short, long, or medium in duration, following one's desire like the <term>Vrishtaprayata</term><note>A poetic meter</note> meter. || 61 ||

On the day of the Preceptor of the Gods (Jupiter/Thursday): gold, silver, horses, elephants, bulls, physicians, and medicines. Also successful are: works for Brahmins, ancestors, and gods; umbrellas, fly-whisks, ornaments, and kings. One should engage in building temples, religious shelters, auspicious scriptures, speech that gives strength and truth, vows, fire oblations, and wealth-gathering, all of which are as pleasing as the <term>Varnaka</term> or <term>Dandaka</term><note>Types of poetic meters</note> meters. || 62 ||

On the day of the Son of Bhrigu (Venus/Friday): colorful clothes, aphrodisiacs, merchants, amorous women, playfulness, laughter, youth, enjoyment, and beautiful lands. Also: crystals, silver, churning tools, vehicles, alkaline substances, ramparts, cows, traders, farmers, medicines, and lotuses.

On the day of the Son of the Sun (Saturn/Saturday), one should deal with: buffaloes, goats, camels, iron, slaves, the elderly, low-caste work, birds, and hunters. Otherwise, do not attempt tasks involving loss of discipline, broken vessels, or elephants, for even the ocean would not yield a drop of water if the timing is wrong. || 63 ||

Even after understanding the vast science of meters, the essence of action is this. Varahamihira has spoken this summary of verses which are pleasing to the ear. || 64 ||

# Thus ends the 104th Chapter of the Shri Varahamihira Brihat Samhita, titled "The Transit of the Planets."

Just as ancient gems with holes already bored, if worn without a thread—that is, if they are bound with beautiful metals—are capable of being adorned with ever-new qualities; so too, these ancient scriptures, though their "holes" (meanings) are already revealed, when bound together without the original "thread" (the old structure), are capable of being greatly beautified by new qualities. For this reason, the results of the transits of the planets are extensively used...

->### Varahi Samhita<-

Because of this, I shall reveal the entire results of the planetary transits using various types of <term>metres (poetic rhythms)</term>. Therefore, may the noble scholars forgive the primary boldness of my "talkativeness" <note>original: "mukhachapalatva" - literally 'fickleness of the mouth' or loquacity</note>. (In this book, I will present many types of metres, though their formal rules will generally not be included here). || 1 || 2 || Those who have heard the words of the Sage Mandavya will not find my words pleasing; however, it is not proper to say even this, for just as a man is captivated by a "fickle-hipped" <note>original: "jaghanachapala" - also the name of a specific poetic metre</note> woman of restless gait, he is not so easily captivated by a virtuous, steady wife. || 3 || (One should calculate the transit from the <term>birth sign</term>, which is the zodiac sign where the Moon was positioned at the time of birth).

The Sun is auspicious when in the 6th, 3rd, or 10th house from the birth sign. The Moon is auspicious in the 3rd, 10th, 6th, 1st, or 7th. Jupiter is auspicious in the 7th, 9th, 2nd, or 5th. Saturn and Mars are auspicious in the 3rd or 6th. Mercury is auspicious in the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, or 10th. Any planet in the 11th house is a giver of good fortune. However, Venus in the 7th, 6th, or 10th house is as terrifying as a "tiger" <note>original: "shardula" - referring to the Shardulavikridita metre, meaning 'tiger's sport'</note>. || 4 ||

During a transit, if the Sun is in the birth sign, it causes distress, loss of wealth, stomach ailments, and weary travels. In the 2nd house, the Sun causes loss of money, unhappiness, deception, and eye diseases. In the 3rd house, the Sun brings acquisition of position, accumulation of wealth, joy, auspiciousness, and the destruction of enemies. In the 4th house, the Sun causes disease and interferes with the "wearing of garlands" <note>original: "sragdhara" - also a metre name</note> and the enjoyment of earthly pleasures. || 5 ||

In the 5th house, the Sun causes suffering from various diseases and enemies. In the 6th house, it destroys disease, grief, and enemies. In the 7th house, it causes weary travels, stomach ailments, and humiliation. In the 8th house, it causes illness and coughs, and one's wife no longer remains "fair-faced" <note>original: "suvadana" - also a metre name</note>, meaning she turns her face away in anger. || 6 ||

In the 9th house, the Sun brings calamity, humiliation, disease, and obstacles in the pursuit of wealth. In the 10th house, the Sun brings great victory and the fulfillment of desires. In the 11th house, it leads to "virtuous conduct" <note>original: "suvritta" - also a metre name</note> and good behavior. In the 12th house, the Sun leads to wicked conduct. || 7 ||

If the Moon is in the birth sign, it provides food, excellent beds, and clothing. In the 2nd house, the Moon causes loss of honor and wealth, and creates obstacles. In the 3rd house, it brings clothing, women, wealth, and happiness. In the 4th house, there is a lack of trust, much like the distrust one feels toward a snake on a "mountain peak" <note>original: "shikharini" - also a metre name</note>. || 8 ||

In the 5th house, the Moon produces humiliation, illness, grief, and obstacles on the road. In the 6th house, it gives wealth and happiness, and diminishes enemies and diseases. In the 7th house, it brings vehicles, honor, sleep, food, and financial gain. In the 8th house, everyone feels fear, as if from a snake that has been "slowly stepped upon" <note>original: "mandakranta" - also a metre name</note>.

If the Moon is in the ninth house, it causes imprisonment, anxiety, fatigue, and stomach ailments. If it is in the tenth, it grants authority and the successful completion of tasks. If Mars is in the twelfth house, a man incurs many types of expenses and is tormented by hundreds of calamities. If Mercury is in the second house, there is disrespect but also the gain of wealth. If Mercury is in the third house, friends are gained; however, fearing the king and enemies, and due to his own bad character, he moves with a <term>‘Drutapada’</term> <gloss>quickened pace</gloss> || 20 ||

If Mercury is in the sixth house, it brings good fortune, victory, and progress. If Mercury is in the seventh, there is extreme distress...

# The Varahi Samhita

<page-num>338</page-num>
->**The Varahi Samhita**<-

...extreme profit, and the gain of foreign women and wealth are achieved. If Saturn is in the twelfth house, one receives the "garland of waves" from the ocean of sorrow. <note>Verse 45</note> Just as a mass of clouds cannot pour much rain into a *kudava* <note>A small wooden measure holding about a quarter-seer of grain</note> during the spring season, so too this planet (Saturn), even when being auspicious, ordains results only in proportion to the time and the worthiness of the recipient. <note>Verse 46</note>

If one wishes to perform a worship for the pacification of the Sun and Mars, one should worship with devotion using red flowers, incense, copper, gold, and *Bakula* <note>Spanish cherry</note> flowers. One should worship the Moon with the gift of a cow, white flowers, silver, and sweet substances; and worship Venus with white flowers and intoxicating <note>or nourishing</note> substances. Worship Saturn with [dark] objects, Mercury with gems, silver, and *Tilaka* flowers, and Jupiter with yellow substances, all with devotion. When the planets are pleased by worship, then even if a man falls from a height or enters into a "serpent’s yawn" <note>original: *bhujanga-vijrimbhita* — meaning the wide-open jaws of a snake</note>, he suffers no pain. <note>Verse 47</note>

Just as when an inauspicious gaze has "arisen" <note>original: *udgata*</note>, it is pacified by worshipping the gods and Brahmins, so too all faults arising from planetary transits can be destroyed through peace-offerings, chanting (*japa*), charity, self-restraint, virtue, the speech of good people, and the company of the righteous. <note>Verse 48</note>

Within the *Arya* meter, there are two variations called *Giti* and *Upagiti*. Just as the first and second halves of the *Arya* characteristic are equal, so do the Sun, Mars, Moon, and Saturn give their transit results during the first half of a sign (upon entry) and the second half of a sign (at the time of exit). <note>Verse 49</note> Just as the counting of the poetic feet in the *Upagiti* variation of the *Arya* meter is balanced in both the first and second halves—meaning it gives equal weight to both places—so does the planet Mercury give equal results in both the first and second halves of a zodiac sign. <note>Verse 50</note>

In the *Arya* meter, if a "middle-heavy" foot <note>a metrical unit where the middle syllable is long</note> falls in an odd position, it destroys the meter; however, if that same foot falls in the sixth position, it achieves "total lightness" <note>four short syllables</note>. Similarly, when Jupiter enters an odd sign, he spreads destruction even among "noble" (*Arya*) groups. But, like a presiding deity of a metrical foot, if the sixth house from the birth sign is aspected or occupied by Jupiter, he brings "total lightness" (loss of dignity) to men in all matters. <note>Verse 51</note>

Just as a *Nakuntaka*¹ song is always uniform, so too the planets that were inauspicious or auspicious at the time of birth—even if they are aspected by powerful beneficial or malefic planets in sequence—will give equal (balanced) results regardless of being good or bad. <note>Verse 52</note> Just as a beautiful woman’s "playful" <note>original: *vilasa*</note> side-glance is fruitless to a blind man, so too is the glance of an enemy planet upon a planet that is in its sign of debilitation, an enemy's territory, or in combustion...

<margin>¹ A song in Sanskrit or Prakrit where the sentences remain uniform is called *Nakuntaka*.</margin>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of planetary influences and astrological timing, specifically linking the behavior of planets to the rules of Sanskrit and Prakrit prosody (poetic meters).</meta>

<page-num>339</page-num>
->Commentary in Hindi, Chapter 104<-

If the [planetary] aspect is present, then all results become futile. ||53|| Just as in the science of prosody <note>the study of poetic meters</note> the *Skandhaka* meter <insert>1</insert> follows the *Aryagiti* meter, or as the *Magadhi* follows the *Vaitaliya* meter, or as the *Gatha* meter follows the *Arya* meter, in the same way, Saturn, the son of the Sun, follows the Sun, and Mercury, the son of the Moon, gives results according to the Moon. ||54|| Because of the color of the Sun's rays, Saturn becomes disordered and acts like bile <note>pitta</note> toward men, increasing significantly; however, it does not give such [bad] results to the "Pathya" <note>wholesome or righteous</note> noble people (holy men). ||55|| Just as the expression of the "Vaktra" (face) changes according to the state of the mind, so do the planets produce results in their transit <term>Gochar: the current movement of planets across the zodiac</term> according to how they meet with the Moon. ||56|| Just as the fifth syllable of all quarters of a "Shloka" <note>a specific poetic verse form</note> and the seventh syllable of the second and fourth quarters are "Laghu" (light/short), so does a man attain "Laghuta" (lightness or insignificance) if the group of planets is situated in inauspicious houses. ||57|| Those who are naturally considered "Laghu" (light/lowly) attain "Guruta" (heaviness or greatness) at the end of a verse (at the end of a foot), similarly, if the planets are well-placed, a man attains greatness everywhere. ||58|| If all planets are inauspicious, the actions that ignorant people begin for their own advancement destroy them, just like an improperly performed "Vaitaliya" <note>a play on words: the meter Vaitaliya and 'Vetala' or demonic spirits</note> act related to a ghost. ||59|| Seeing the planets situated in auspicious places, the King who begins an "Akarman" (invasion/advancement) at that time, even if he possesses little valor, obtains the wealth of others through "Aupacchandasika" (persuasive or rhythmic) dealings. ||60||

When the Sun is in the "Upachaya" <term>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses of a horoscope, signifying growth</term> or in the Ascendant, on the day of the Sun (Sunday), the following are successful: gold, copper, horses, wood, bone, leather, woolen goods (pashmina), mountains, trees, bark, nails, snakes, thieves, forests, cruel deeds, royal service, consecration, medicine, linen cloth, meritorious goods (trade items), cattle rearing, difficult paths, medical work, stone heaps, deeds befitting noble families, deeds of famous heroes, praiseworthy positions in war, fame, and all fire-related works.

If the Moon rises on a Monday or is situated in a "Kendra" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the pillars of a chart</term>, then for a man, the following are successful: ornaments, conch shells, pearls, lotus, silver, water, fame, sugarcane, food, women, milky and clean trees, shrubs (like walnut trees), grains from marshy lands, liquid substances, deeds befitting Brahmins, activities involving horses, cooling treatments, agricultural work done by horned animals (plowing), the work of a general, cries for help, royal duties, good fortune, nocturnal activities, substances that produce phlegm, elephant-flowers, and the commencement of making clothes.

On Tuesday, all types of work involving metals and mines are successfully accomplished, as well as gold, fire, coral, weapons, cruelty, theft, riots, forest-related work, activities related to Goddess Durga, military authority, all red-flowered trees, red-colored pungent substances, sharp spices (like black pepper), snakes, and...

# Varāhī Saṃhitā (The Compendium of Varāhamihira)

(Page 340)

Activities involving wealth gained through execution <note>original: "फांसीसे कमाया हुआ धन" - likely referring to fines or assets seized from criminals</note>, the work of young physicians, Buddhist monks <note>original: "शाक्य" (Shakya)</note>, and ascetics, nocturnal occupations, all tasks involving silk garments, and acts of cunning or deceit are successful [under certain planetary conditions]. During the ascendant of Mercury or on a Wednesday, the following are successful: dealings in emeralds, land, and fragrant clothing; general theater, science, scriptures, poetry, all artistic skills, mantra rituals, metallurgy, disputes, expertise, meritorious deeds, the vow of the "Great Downpour" <note>a specific ritual for rain</note>, yoga, messengers, longevity rituals, tax-related work, illusion, falsehoods, bathing, short and long poetic meters, and all imitative arts. || 61 ||

On Thursdays, the following are successful: gold, silver, horses, elephants, bulls, physicians and medicines, all tasks related to Brahmins, ancestors, gods, and city-dwellers; religious prohibitions, the fly-whisk <note>a symbol of royalty</note>, ornaments, and royal duties; temples, religious shelters, auspicious scriptures, acts of personal strength, divine rituals, truthful speech, vows, fire sacrifices <term>Homa: a ritual where offerings are made into a consecrated fire</term>, and financial interests. These succeed like a "Varṇadaṇḍaka" <note>a poetic meter, here used as a metaphor for something as beautiful and orderly as a decorated staff</note>. || 62 ||

On Fridays, the following are successful: the cutting of cloth, the preparation of aphrodisiac medicines, the pleasures of courtesans and lovers, beautiful lands for enjoying youthful humor, objects of desire made of crystal and silver, vehicles, sugarcane, autumn-harvested grains, cattle, merchants, farmers, and tasks related to medicine or water. On Saturdays, the following are successful: buffaloes, goats, camels, black iron, menial tasks involving slaves and the elderly, birds, thieves, the use of snares, acts lacking humility, broken vessels, tasks requiring elephants, and all obstructive activities. Otherwise, these efforts become like "Samudraga" <note>literally "going to the ocean"</note>—as insignificant as a drop of water lost in the sea—and do not succeed. || 63 ||

The expansion of poetic meters is extremely "Vipula" (vast). With excellent knowledge of this expansion, the study of meters becomes easy. For this reason, Varāhamihira has compiled this collection of verses which is pleasing to the ear. || 64 ||

Thus ends the one hundred and fourth chapter of the *Bṛhat Saṃhitā* composed by the Great Teacher Varāhamihira, with the Hindi commentary by Pandit Baldev Prasad Mishra, resident of Moradabad in the North-Western region. || 104 ||

### Chapter One Hundred and Five

->The Vow of the Constellation Man<-
<note>original: "Nakshatra Purusha Vratam" - a ritual where parts of the human body are mapped onto the lunar mansions (Nakshatras)</note>

The feet are represented by the *Mūla* constellation, the shanks by *Rohiṇī* and *Aśvinī*. The thighs are the two *Āṣāḍhās*, and the private parts are the two *Phālgunīs*. || 1 || The hips are *Kṛttikā*, and the two *Bhādrapadās* are the sides. *Revatī* is located in the abdomen, and *Anurādhā* is known as the chest. || 2 || The back is *Dhaniṣṭhā*, the arms are remembered as *Viśākhā*, and the hands are *Hasta*. The fingers are *Punarvasu*, and the nails are named *Āśleṣā*. || 3 || The neck is *Jyeṣṭhā*...

# Chapter 105: The Vow of the Constellation-Man

The ears are Shravana; the mouth is Pushya; the teeth are Swati; the laughter is Shatabhisha; the nose is Magha; and the eyes are Mrigashira. || 4 ||

The forehead is Chitra; the head is Bharani; and the hair is Ardra. This <term>Nakshatra-Purusha</term><note>The "Constellation-Man," a visualization of the divine form of Vishnu composed entirely of the lunar mansions or Nakshatras.</note> should be fashioned by those desiring physical beauty. || 5 ||

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Chaitra <note>March-April</note>, when the Moon is in conjunction with the Mula constellation, one should observe a fast after worshipping Lord Vishnu and the constellations. || 6 ||

Upon completion of the vow, one should give a gift of clarified butter <note>ghee</note>, grain flour, and gold to a Brahmin who is an expert in the science of time <note>an astrologer</note>, along with gems and clothes according to one's financial capacity. || 7 ||

A man desiring beauty should worship the Brahmins with foods rich in milk and clarified butter, along with jaggery, and likewise offer them clothes and silver. Starting from the feet <note>Mula constellation</note>, one should fast as each constellation arrives, calling upon the names of the constellations and performing the worship of Lord Keshava <note>Vishnu</note> and the stars according to the prescribed rites. || 8 ||

<note>Verses 9-12 describe the physical rewards of this ritual for men and women.</note>

Such a person becomes one with long arms, a broad and muscular chest, a face like the moon, and white, beautiful teeth. They walk like a majestic elephant, have eyes as wide as lotus petals, and possess a form as attractive as the God of Love, stealing the hearts of women. || 9 ||

A woman born of this merit has a face like the autumn moon, eyes like lotus petals, beautiful teeth, and fine ears. Her hair resembles the dark belly of a bee. || 10 ||

Her voice is like that of a male cuckoo, her lips are copper-red, and her hands and feet are like lotus leaves. Her waist bends under the weight of her breasts, and her navel has a right-handed curl. || 11 ||

Her thighs are like the trunk of a banana tree, she has beautiful hips, and she is fortunate and graceful. Whether a woman or a man, they possess well-joined fingers and toes. || 12 ||

As long as the garland of stars wanders in the sky, adorning it with light, so long does the performer of this vow dwell in the world of Brahma as a celestial being. At the start of a new cosmic age <note>Kalpa</note>, they become a wise universal emperor <note>Chakravarti</note>, and even when reborn in the world of mortals, they become a king or a wealthy Brahmin. || 13 ||

<note>Verses 14-15 list the twelve names of Vishnu associated with the months/constellations.</note>

Mrigashirsha and the others are associated with Keshava, Narayana, Madhava, Govinda, Vishnu, Madhusudana, Trivikrama, Vamana, Shridhara, Hrishikesha, Padmanabha, and Damodara—these are the names of the months in order. || 14-15 ||

The man who fasts on the twelfth day of each month and recites these names in order while worshipping Keshava reaches that supreme state where there is no fear of rebirth. || 16 ||

->Thus ends the One Hundred and Fifth Chapter of the Brihat Samhita<-
->by Varahamihira, titled "The Vow of the Constellation-Man"<-

<margin>The Hindi commentary below summarizes the anatomical mapping: Mula (feet), Rohini/Ashwini (shanks), Purvashadha/Uttarashadha (thighs), Phalgunis (secret parts), Krittika (waist), Bhadrapadas (sides), Revati (belly), Anuradha (chest), Dhanishta (back), Vishakha (arms), Hasta (hands), Punarvasu (fingers), Ashlesha (nails), Jyeshtha (neck), Shravana (ears), Pushya (mouth), Swati (teeth), Shatabhisha (smile), Magha (nose), Mrigashira (eyes), Chitra (forehead), Bharani (head), and Ardra (hair).</margin>
